topics.blurb: Sign in, find your way around the screen, and see what waits for you.
topics.summary: What the ETL Console is for, how to sign in safely the first time, and how every screen is laid out: the menu, the top bar, Home, your profile and notifications, and why your menu may differ from a colleague's.

start.title: Turn on two-factor sign-in

faq.q: I forgot my password. What do I do?
faq.md: Ask your workspace administrator to reset it; you choose your own at your next sign-in. See [When you cannot sign in](#gs-sign-in--when-you-cannot-sign-in).

faq.q: I lost my phone with the authenticator app.
faq.md: Sign in with one of your recovery codes, or ask an administrator to reset your two-factor sign-in. See [When you lose your phone](#gs-two-factor--when-you-lose-your-phone).

faq.q: Why does my colleague see menu entries I don't?
faq.md: Your role and your page access profile decide your menu. See [Who sees what](#gs-who-sees-what).

faq.q: Why was I signed out?
faq.md: Your workspace signs out sessions that are not used for a while, with a warning a minute before. See [Sign in](#gs-sign-in--when-you-cannot-sign-in).

faq.q: Which time zone are the times in?
faq.md: Your own device's, on the 24-hour clock. Billing days follow your workspace's billing time zone. See [Times and dates](#gs-tour--times-and-dates).

faq.q: Can I use a dark screen?
faq.md: Yes: choose the sun or moon in the top bar and pick **Dark**, **Midnight** or another theme. It follows you to any device. See [Themes](#gs-tour--themes).

faq.q: Can I choose which notifications I get?
faq.md: Not one by one: what reaches you follows the work in your name and your teams'. See [Notifications](#gs-profile--notifications).

topics.title: The tour: a patient's journey
topics.blurb: The whole product through one fictional patient at Summit Valley Health System.
topics.summary:
The whole ETL Console through one patient's stay: Elena Marsh, admitted to the fictional Summit Valley Health System
with diabetes, an infected foot wound and heart failure. Each part says what happened, which screen shows it, and which
topic explains it. Every person, patient and result is fictional and every data set synthetic; every model answer is a
DRAFT a person checked.

start.title: A referral arrives by email
start.text: Mailed in, read into fields, approved by a person.

start.title: The journey starts
start.text: One approval workflow carries the whole stay.

start.title: Diagnostics
start.text: Labs, a wound photo and an X-ray, each checked by a person.

start.title: The care plan
start.text: Who decides depends on the risk and on who is in.

start.title: Discharge
start.text: The signed PDF, its QR check and the follow-up.

faq.q: Is any of this real patient data?
faq.md:
No. Summit Valley, Elena Marsh and every clinician are fictional, and every file, reading and result is synthetic, made
for the demonstration; the X-ray is a public research image assigned to the fictional patient. See
[A referral arrives by email](#tour-referral).

faq.q: Does the AI decide anything?
faq.md:
No. A model drafts the wound description, the X-ray triage, the care plan and the discharge summary, each labelled
DRAFT, and a named person approves each one. Measurements are made in code, not by the model. See
[Diagnostics](#tour-diagnostics).

faq.q: What happens when the doctor who should approve is away?
faq.md:
A colleague standing in for her decides, and the request's history records that he approved for her. See
[The care plan](#tour-care-plan).

faq.q: Why was a senior doctor asked only for this patient?
faq.md:
The workflow has a condition on the care plan's risk: when it is High, the senior physicians are asked as well. See
[The care plan](#tour-care-plan).

faq.q: How do I know the discharge PDF is the one that was approved?
faq.md:
Choose **Verify signature** on the report's page, or follow the QR code on the PDF: it says whether the file is intact
and one of the workspace's approved reports. See [Discharge](#tour-discharge).

faq.q: Can I build the same journey for my organisation?
faq.md:
The tour uses only what every workspace has: documents, forms, pipelines, an approval workflow, Report Studio and a
dashboard. Start with [the journey starts](#tour-journey-starts) to see how the parts link.

topics.part: Part II · Set up your workspace
topics.blurb: Your workspace, its people, page and tab access, teams, delegates and out of office.
topics.summary: How a workspace administrator sets up the workspace for its people: who may sign in and with which role, which pages and tabs each member opens, who may grant access for a while, how teams share the work, and how approvals keep moving when someone is away.

start.title: Make an access profile

faq.q: What is the difference between a workspace administrator and a member?
faq.md: An administrator opens every page and changes people, connections, pipelines and settings; a member opens the pages on their profile. See [The two roles](#adm-people--the-two-roles).

faq.q: Someone forgot their password. How do I reset it?
faq.md: Choose **Reset password** in their row on **Administration › Users**; they choose their own at their next sign-in. See [Reset someone's password](#adm-reset-remove--reset-someones-password).

faq.q: Should I deactivate or delete someone who left?
faq.md: Deactivate: it keeps their work and history and can be undone. See [Remove someone's access](#adm-reset-remove--remove-someones-access).

faq.q: Why does a new member see every page?
faq.md: The workspace has no access profiles yet, or no default. See [How it works](#adm-access-profiles--how-it-works).

faq.q: Can a team lead give their team access without being an administrator?
faq.md: Yes, as a delegate, within limits and for a set time. See [Delegates](#adm-delegates).

faq.q: Do teams decide which pages people see?
faq.md: No. Teams decide where work goes; page access decides what people open. See [Teams](#adm-teams).

faq.q: How do I give a colleague my approvals while I am away?
faq.md: With an out of office, or pass one task on with **Pass on**. See [Out of office](#adm-out-of-office).

topics.title: Connections and API collections
topics.part: Part II · Set up your workspace
topics.blurb: Storage, read-only databases, API collections, data contracts and connectors.
topics.summary:
Connections are where a workspace's data comes from and goes to: the buckets pipelines read and write, the databases
they may only read, the outside APIs they call, and the contracts the data must meet. Set them up once; pipelines,
sources, forms and the AI Assistant refer to them by name, and their secrets never come back to the browser.

start.title: Connect your storage
start.text: Add a bucket or an FTP server, test it, and pick the one the file drop uses.

start.title: Add a read-only database connection
start.text: Let pipelines query a PostgreSQL database that the console only reads.

start.title: Make an API collection
start.text: Group the APIs you call, with their sign-in and environments.

start.title: Page through results
start.text: Fetch every page of a long answer, and stop in time.

start.title: Test a request
start.text: Make one real call and read the answer before a pipeline relies on it.

start.title: Data contracts
start.text: Say what a record must hold, so a bad one is caught where it enters.

faq.q: Why can't I see the Storage tab?
faq.md:
Storage connections are a workspace administrator's: the tab shows only to them. Ask an administrator to add or change
one. See [Connect your storage](#con-storage).

faq.q: Can the console change data in our database?
faq.md:
No. A database connection is opened read-only, a query must start with SELECT, WITH, VALUES or TABLE, and results are
written to your storage, never back. See [Add a read-only database connection](#con-databases).

faq.q: Where do I put an API key or a password?
faq.md:
In an environment of the collection, as a variable marked **Secret**; the request or the default auth then says
`{{name}}`. A credential typed in plain text is refused. See [How an API signs in](#con-api-auth).

faq.q: My test says Blocked. What does that mean?
faq.md:
The address the call would reach is private, loopback, link-local or a cloud metadata address, so nothing was sent.
See [What the console may call](#con-addresses).

faq.q: Will changing an API break the pipelines that use it?
faq.md:
Every save is a new version. A source is pinned to the version it names, and **Used by** shows what follows the latest.
Test the change first. See [Versions and pinning](#con-api-versions).

faq.q: Can I bring in what we already have in Postman?
faq.md:
Yes: **Import** takes a Postman v2.1 collection with its environments, or a Bruno folder, as a new collection. See
[Import a Postman or Bruno collection](#con-api-import).

faq.q: A connector says "On request". How do I get it?
faq.md:
Its sign-in has to be registered for your platform first. Ask your account team. See
[Sources and connectors](#con-sources).

topics.title: Building pipelines
topics.blurb: What a pipeline is, three ways to start one, the builder, trying it out, versions and settings.
topics.summary:
A pipeline is one unit of work your workspace does again and again: steps in order that read your data, check and
shape it, ask a model where it helps, wait for a person where one must decide, and send the results where they are
needed. This chapter shows how to start one, put its steps together in the builder, try it on sample rows, save it as
versions and set what applies to all its steps.

start.title: Learn what a pipeline is
start.text: Steps in order, a run, and what a run leaves behind.

start.title: Start a pipeline
start.text: Describe it to the AI Assistant, add steps yourself, or copy one.

start.title: Put the steps together
start.text: Add, move and fill in steps; see them as a flow.

start.title: Try it on sample rows
start.text: Test with sample, Validate, then run it once.

start.title: Set what applies to every step
start.text: Review, sensitivity, tags, retention and defaults.

start.title: Save it and read its history
start.text: Each save is a version; a run keeps the one it started with.

faq.q: Why can't I edit a pipeline?
faq.md:
Building and changing pipelines is a workspace administrator's work, and in a workspace our team manages the pipelines
are read-only to you. Anyone whose page access includes Pipelines can still see them. See [What a pipeline is](#pl-overview).

faq.q: Does saving a change affect a run that is going?
faq.md:
No. A run uses the version of the steps that was current when it started; your save is the next version, used by the
next run. See [Save, versions and history](#pl-versions).

faq.q: How do I put today's date in a file name?
faq.md:
Write `{{date}}` in the step's file name or key, such as `ops/beds/census-{{date}}.csv`. See
[Placeholders and run parameters](#pl-placeholders).

faq.q: What is the difference between Duplicate and Copy an existing pipeline?
faq.md:
**Copy an existing pipeline** (under **New pipeline**) makes a pipeline with its own copy of the steps. **Duplicate** in
the list keeps using the original's steps, so a change to one changes both. See [Three ways to start](#pl-start--copy-an-existing-pipeline).

faq.q: Can I try a pipeline without real data?
faq.md:
Yes: **Test with sample** puts rows you write first, **Validate** checks the whole definition, and **Save & run now**
shows each step's result. See [Try a pipeline](#pl-try).

faq.q: How do I make results wait for a person?
faq.md:
Tick **Our team** under **Results need review by** on the **Settings** tab, or add an **Approval** step where the run
should pause. See [Pipeline settings](#pl-settings--review-whether-a-person-approves-the-results).

faq.q: Can a pipeline use another pipeline's answer?
faq.md:
Yes, with a **Run pipeline** step, once or once per row, up to three calls deep. See
[Call another pipeline](#pl-run-pipeline).

topics.title: Step reference
topics.blurb: Every step a pipeline can use, grouped by what it does, with its settings, defaults and limits.
topics.summary:
Every step a pipeline can use, by what it does: read rows in, shape them, combine them, check and enrich them, work on
recordings, documents and images, wait for a person, and send the results out. Each step's settings are described by the
names on its panel, with their defaults, an example from Summit Valley Health System and the step's limits. The last
article puts every step on one table.

start.title: Read rows in
start.text: Files, folders, APIs, databases, approved documents and past runs.

start.title: Shape the rows
start.text: Choose columns, filter, work out values, clean and sort.

start.title: Combine and call
start.text: Join, stack and group; check against a contract; call an API.

start.title: Use AI and media
start.text: Prompts, transcripts, conversions, OCR and image measurements.

start.title: Send the results out
start.text: Files, buckets, reports, notices and webhooks.

start.title: See every step at once
start.text: The settings, defaults and limits of all steps on one table.

faq.q: Why is a step marked (disabled) in Add step?
faq.md:
It is switched off in this workspace (in **Settings › Task Registry**), or it is an administrator's step and you are
not one. The hint beside it says which. See [Every step at a glance](#step-glance).

faq.q: Which steps can only an administrator add?
faq.md:
**Call API**, **Read runs**, **Run pipeline**, **Send webhook** and **Upload to bucket**. See
[Every step at a glance](#step-glance).

faq.q: Why can't I add Write Database?
faq.md:
Writing to a database is not part of this release: database connections are read-only, and pipelines never write into
your systems. See [Write Database is switched off](#step-outputs--write-database-is-switched-off).

faq.q: How do I read only the files that are new since the last run?
faq.md:
Set **Read S3**'s **Which objects** to `last_run`. A failed run moves nothing on, so its files come again. See
[Read S3](#step-read--read-s3).

faq.q: How do I call an API once for every row?
faq.md:
Use **Call API** with **Send** set to `each` (or `batch` for many rows a call), up to 8 calls at once. See
[Call API](#step-check--call-api).

faq.q: Is an AI step's answer final?
faq.md:
No. A model's answer is a DRAFT for a person to check; follow an important AI step with an **Approval** step or the
pipeline's review. See [AI prompt](#step-ai--ai-prompt).

faq.q: What happens when a step reaches a limit?
faq.md:
It fails and says which limit, before or while it works; it never cuts rows silently. See
[Data a step can hold](#step-glance--data-a-step-can-hold).

topics.title: Triggers and schedules
topics.blurb: Run now, on a timetable, or when a file, form, document, event or API call arrives; and backfills of past periods.
topics.summary:
A pipeline runs through a schedule. A schedule runs it on a timetable or only when started, and can also start it when a
file arrives in the inbox or a document is approved. Forms, events from your systems, the API and approval workflows
start runs too, and a backfill runs a schedule once for each day of a past range.

start.title: Run it now
start.text: Run now, or Run with… to give one run its own dates and choices.

start.title: Put it on a timetable
start.text: Hourly, daily, weekly, monthly or a cron line.

start.title: Start it when a file arrives
start.text: The inbox, File drop, and only new files since the last run.

start.title: Start it when a document is approved
start.text: Each approved document of a type starts a run.

start.title: Start it from your own systems
start.text: Event routes and the API.

start.title: Fill in past periods
start.text: A run for each day of a range, the cost estimate first.

faq.q: What time zone does a schedule use?
faq.md:
Server time, Chicago, as the editor and its **Next runs** say. A cron line is in Chicago time too. See
[Run a pipeline on a timetable](#trg-schedules).

faq.q: Why is Run now greyed out?
faq.md:
The schedule is inactive ("Activate this schedule to run it"), or it already has a run queued or running. See
[Run now and Run with…](#trg-run-now).

faq.q: What happens to runs while a schedule is switched off?
faq.md:
They do not happen: slots that pass while it is inactive are recorded as **Missed** and are not replayed when you turn
it back on. To fill the gap, run a [backfill](#trg-backfills). See [Pause, skip or stop a schedule](#trg-schedules--pause-skip-or-stop-a-schedule).

faq.q: Can one pipeline run every hour and also when a file arrives?
faq.md:
Yes: give the schedule a timetable and **A file arrives**, and set **Read S3** to read the run's own files first and
only objects since the last run. See [One pipeline for a timetable and the inbox](#trg-file--one-pipeline-for-a-timetable-and-the-inbox).

faq.q: Does Run with… change the schedule?
faq.md: No. The values are for that run only; the next scheduled run takes the defaults. See [Run with…](#trg-run-now--give-one-run-its-own-values-run-with).

faq.q: What does a backfill cost?
faq.md:
Its runs are billed like any run. Before you start, the preview estimates the total from what the pipeline's runs were
billed in the last 30 days. See [Backfills](#trg-backfills).

faq.q: What if the same API request is sent twice?
faq.md:
With the same `Idempotency-Key` within 24 hours, the platform returns the first run instead of starting another. See
[Start a pipeline from your own systems](#trg-api).

topics.title: AI in the console
topics.blurb: Model connections, prompts, AI steps, transcription, the AI Assistant and Ask your data.
topics.summary:
AI in the console helps people do their work faster, and never decides for them. Model connections say where models run
(local models by default for sensitive data), prompts say what a step asks, and AI steps classify, extract, summarise and
describe images inside pipelines. The AI Assistant designs pipelines in a conversation, and Ask your data answers questions
with its sources. Every model answer is a DRAFT for a person to check.

start.title: Connect a model
start.text: Add a model connection, test it, set its caps and the workspace default.

start.title: Write a prompt
start.text: Instructions, variables and a JSON answer; try it before anything uses it.

start.title: Use it in a pipeline
start.text: Add an AI prompt step, row by row or a few at a time.

start.title: Describe a pipeline to the assistant
start.text: It draws the flow; you check it, fill it and create it.

start.title: Decide which models see which data
start.text: The data policy's three levels and their model rules.

faq.q: Is a model's answer ever used without a person?
faq.md:
Only if your pipeline does so. Every answer is a DRAFT: mark it so in the prompt, and hold the results for a review or an
Approval step when a person must decide. See [AI in pipelines](#ai-steps).

faq.q: Does patient data leave our machines?
faq.md:
Not by default. The **Sensitive** level starts as *Local only*: only model connections your organisation runs itself may
see it until an administrator changes the data policy. See [Which models may see which data](#ai-data-levels).

faq.q: Why did my AI step fail before it asked anything?
faq.md:
Usually a cap: the input had more rows than **At most rows**, or the connection's **Daily token budget** was reached.
See [AI in pipelines](#ai-steps--when-the-model-is-busy).

faq.q: What does the AI Assistant do without asking?
faq.md:
It reads, as you, what you may open. Anything that runs, saves or deletes comes back as a card to confirm, and a pipeline
is saved only when you choose **Create pipeline**. See [Design a pipeline with the AI Assistant](#ai-assistant).

faq.q: Where do I see what AI costs?
faq.md:
In **Cost & usage**: model tokens in and out, minutes of audio and pages read, by prompt and by pipeline. See
[What AI costs](#ai-costs).

faq.q: Can AI help design a report?
faq.md: Yes: Report Studio has its own AI designer, see [Report Studio's AI designer](#rs-ai-designer).

topics.title: Documents
topics.blurb: Send documents in, read their fields, review what was unsure and use the approved data.
topics.summary:
Documents turns the paper that reaches you (referrals, lab reports, insurance cards, invoices) into checked data.
Upload them or mail them in; each one is read, matched to its document type and split into fields, and a person
checks what the reading was unsure of. Approved values land in the type's dataset and can start a pipeline.

start.title: Document types
start.text: Add the ready-made types you receive, or make your own.

start.title: Upload documents and mail them in
start.text: Upload files or give senders your workspace's own address.

start.title: Review a document
start.text: Check the page beside its fields, correct, approve or reject.

start.title: Approved data
start.text: One row per approved document, to download or read in a pipeline.

start.title: When a document is approved
start.text: Start a pipeline each time a document of a type is approved.

faq.q: What is the difference between Upload and the file drop?
faq.md:
Upload (and Email-in) make documents: each file is read and split into fields for review. The file drop only stores
files for pipelines and starts the schedules waiting for them. See [The file drop](#doc-file-drop).

faq.q: Why is a value flagged "check" when it looks right?
faq.md:
It was read less surely than the type's **Auto-approve at** line (80 % when there is none), or a rule found a problem.
Confirm it against the page and approve. See [How documents are read](#doc-reading).

faq.q: Our Email-in address has leaked. What now?
faq.md:
An administrator chooses **New address** on **Intake › Email-in**: the old address is shut out at once. Give the new
one to your senders. See [Upload documents and mail them in](#doc-intake--give-it-a-new-address-or-turn-it-off).

faq.q: I uploaded the same file twice. Do I now have two documents?
faq.md:
No. A file the workspace already has, by any channel, is kept once and listed as **Duplicate**. See
[How documents are read](#doc-reading--one-document-per-file).

faq.q: Why can't I approve these documents in bulk?
faq.md:
The workspace's review policy may not allow it, a document may be claimed by someone else, or its rules fail. See
[Review many documents at once](#doc-bulk-review).

faq.q: Can I catch an invoice that does not add up, or one sent twice?
faq.md:
Yes: give the type rules such as **A table column adds up to a field** and **Not a duplicate of another document**. See
[Checks on a document](#doc-checks).

faq.q: Where do the approved values go?
faq.md: To the type's dataset on **Documents › Approved data**, with your corrections. See [Approved data](#doc-approved-data).

topics.blurb: Build forms, share them, start work from a submission and keep the answers.

start.title: Build a form
start.text: Add fields, required answers, placeholders and help text, then publish.

start.title: Show or require a field when
start.text: Ask a question only when an earlier answer calls for it.

start.title: What a submission starts
start.text: Start a pipeline, an approval workflow, or both.

start.title: Share a form
start.text: Members fill it in inside the workspace; links only when you decide.

start.title: Submissions
start.text: See who sent what, the run and approval it started, and its answers.

faq.q: Who can fill in our forms?
faq.md:
Signed-in members of the workspace whose page access includes **Forms**, and only **Active** forms. Links for anyone
else are off until an administrator turns them on. See [Share a form](#form-share).

faq.q: Why can't I find the New form button?
faq.md: Building forms is a workspace administrator's. Others see the Active forms to fill in. See [Build a form](#form-build).

faq.q: Can a question appear only when it applies?
faq.md:
Yes: on the **Logic** tab, **Show only when** or **Also required when** an earlier answer says so. See
[Show or require a field when](#form-logic).

faq.q: My submission says "Run not started". Why?
faq.md: The form's pipeline could not start; **Details** on its row says why. See [Submissions](#form-submissions).

faq.q: Where do attached files and signatures go?
faq.md:
They are kept with the submission and listed with its answers. A file can also be sent to Document Intelligence to be
read. See [Submissions](#form-submissions--read-a-submission).

faq.q: Analytics is missing some of a form's submissions. What can I do?
faq.md:
An administrator can choose **Rebuild dataset files** in the form's row menu; no answer changes. See
[The form's dataset and Rebuild dataset files](#form-dataset).

topics.title: Runs and the Items view
topics.blurb: Follow runs, open each item, see the outputs and retry what failed.
topics.summary:
Every time a pipeline runs, the console keeps a record: its steps, its items, what it made and what went wrong.
Runs lists them by schedule, by date, by how they measure up and by how they failed; a run's page and its Items view show
each one in full, and a failed run is retried from the step that failed, or only for the items that failed.

start.title: Find a run
start.text: Runs › Latest, narrowed by when, status, pipeline and what started it.

start.title: Read a run's page
start.text: Steps, Map, AI answers, Items, Outputs and Log.

start.title: Open one item
start.text: An item's steps, data and files; act on many at once.

start.title: Fix what failed
start.text: Failed runs grouped by error; retry from the failed step or only the failed items.

start.title: Compare two runs
start.text: Find an item across a schedule's runs and compare two of them.

faq.q: Why is a run Completed but marked waiting for review?
faq.md:
Its pipeline holds its results until a person approves them. Decide it in **Review**. See
[Run statuses](#run-statuses).

faq.q: Can I retry only the items that failed?
faq.md:
Yes. On the run's **Items** tab, **Retry failed items** runs only the failed ones again, each from the step it failed at.
See [When something fails](#run-failures--retry-only-the-failed-items).

faq.q: Does a retry run everything again?
faq.md:
No. **Retry from the failed step** reuses the steps before it. Only **Run again from the start** runs every step again, and
is billed again. See [When something fails](#run-failures--retry-a-run).

faq.q: Why was my Run now refused?
faq.md:
A schedule runs one run at a time: while its last run is in flight, another is refused. See
[Runs at once and big data](#run-at-once).

faq.q: How long are a run's files kept?
faq.md:
Files kept with the run expire after 24 hours unless the pipeline or the data policy sets another time; files written to
your own buckets stay there. See [A run's page](#run-page--view-a-file-or-take-it-away).

faq.q: Why can't I see a colleague's runs?
faq.md:
A member sees the runs of their own schedules and the runs they are asked to review; administrators see all. See
[Follow runs](#run-runs--who-sees-which-runs).

topics.title: Approvals, review and teams
topics.blurb: Everything waiting for a person, approval steps, workflows and who decides.
topics.summary:
Approvals are where people decide: a run's results, a step in the middle of a run, a document's values, or a request
that walks an approval workflow. Review gathers everything waiting for you in one list with one count; approval workflows
lay out who approves, what is checked and what runs; teams and managers say who decides.

start.title: See what waits for you
start.text: Review's All waiting, Approvals, Runs and Documents.

start.title: Decide a run's results
start.text: Approve, or reject with a reason; one by one or in bulk.

start.title: Design an approval workflow
start.text: Approvals, tasks, conditions, pipelines; publish a version.

start.title: Say who decides
start.text: People, roles, teams and managers.

start.title: Start and follow a request
start.text: New request, and its history in My requests.

faq.q: Why can't I approve my own request?
faq.md:
No one approves their own request: someone else decides it, as the workflow names. See
[Who decides](#apr-who-decides).

faq.q: Why was an item skipped when I approved several at once?
faq.md:
Each item is decided by the rules of a single decision; the panel says why each one was skipped, such as *The pipeline
requires individual review*. See [Decide many at once](#apr-bulk--why-an-item-is-skipped).

faq.q: What happens when I reject an Approval step?
faq.md:
The run fails in a moment, and its message carries your reason. See
[Approval steps inside a run](#apr-approval-steps--decide-it).

faq.q: What does the number beside Review mean?
faq.md:
Everything waiting for your decision: approvals, run results and documents, counted from the list **All waiting** shows.
See [Review](#apr-review-home--the-badge).

faq.q: If I publish a new version, what happens to requests already running?
faq.md:
They keep the version they started on; new requests use the new one. See
[Design an approval workflow](#apr-workflows--publish-versions-and-test-runs).

faq.q: Who may change a team's members?
faq.md: Its lead, or a workspace administrator; an administrator names the leads. See [Who decides](#apr-who-decides--teams).

topics.title: Report Studio
topics.blurb: Design report templates once, fill them from your data, approve and sign every version.
topics.summary:
Report Studio turns your data into finished, branded PDF and HTML reports: a discharge summary, a monthly safety report,
a statement for every guarantor. Design a template once, fill it from a pipeline's run, a file or a sample, and keep
every version. A person approves a version, and the approval signs its PDF in their name, so anyone can check later
who approved it and that it has not changed.

start.title: Brand your reports
start.text: Upload your logo and letterhead, and make a brand profile.

start.title: Make a template
start.text: Start from a starter or your own on Reports › Templates.

start.title: Lay it out
start.text: Add tables, charts and fields in the designer, with test data.

start.title: Generate a report
start.text: Pick a published template and the data, check the preview, generate.

start.title: Approve and sign it
start.text: Someone else approves; the PDF is signed and can be verified.

faq.q: Why can't I approve a report I generated?
faq.md:
Whoever generated a version never approves it, so every signed report has two people behind it. Ask a colleague with
**Approve and sign reports**. See [Approve, sign and verify](#rs-approve).

faq.q: Can I change a published template?
faq.md:
No: a published version never changes, so every report keeps the exact version it was made from. Choose **New draft
from vN**, change the draft and publish it as the next version. See [Templates and the library](#rs-templates).

faq.q: How do I make one report for each row, such as a statement per guarantor?
faq.md:
In the pipeline's **Generate report** step, turn on **One report per row** and name each report from the row's columns.
See [Reports from a pipeline](#rs-pipeline).

faq.q: My report failed: "is not in this data". What now?
faq.md:
The template reads a field the data does not have. Choose **Fix field mapping** and match it, or add the field to the
pipeline's output. See [Report Studio troubleshooting](#rs-troubleshooting).

faq.q: How do I check that a PDF someone sent me is genuine?
faq.md:
Open the report and choose **Verify signature**, then **Check a file someone sent**. See
[Verify a signed PDF](#rs-approve--verify-a-signed-pdf).

faq.q: How many pages can a report have?
faq.md:
300 by default; a workspace administrator may set fewer, and the platform can allow up to 2,000. See
[Retention and page limits](#rs-limits).

faq.q: Can I take a report back after it was approved?
faq.md:
You cannot delete an approved report, but you can **Void** the version with a reason: every copy served from then on says
VOID. See [Versions, COPY, void, archive and delete](#rs-versions).

faq.q: Does the AI design reports for me?
faq.md:
In a draft, the AI assistant drafts a template from your words, suggests mappings and charts and explains the checks.
Nothing changes until you accept. See [The AI designer](#rs-ai-designer).

topics.title: Dashboards and analysis
topics.blurb: Boards, Ask your data, Analytics Studio, the Data Catalog, files and tools.
topics.summary:
What your pipelines produce lands in files, and this part of the console is where people read them: boards of widgets
that run again each time they are opened, questions in plain words with chart answers, Analytics Studio to explore a
file, the Data Catalog to see what data you have and who may see it, and the file browser and tools.

start.title: See where its data comes from
start.text: The pipeline that keeps the board's files, and its last run.

start.title: Explore a file in Analytics Studio
start.text: Preview, profile, group and query a file, and save it for a board.

start.title: Build and edit a dashboard
start.text: Add widgets from saved work, pick each chart, set sections and a filter bar.

start.title: Put an answer on a board
start.text: Ask your data in plain words and pin the chart answer.

start.title: Check what is sensitive
start.text: The Data Catalog, masked columns and asking for access.

faq.q: Why does my board show yesterday's figures?
faq.md:
A board reads the files its pipeline wrote, as they are now. If the pipeline has not run since yesterday, neither has
the board's data. Follow **Made by** on the board to the pipeline's last run. See
[Where a board's data comes from](#dash-data-sources).

faq.q: Why can't I change a board?
faq.md:
Opening, running and filtering boards needs **Dashboards** in your page access; changing them needs **Edit dashboards**
(or **Analytics Studio**). Ask your workspace administrator. See [Who may do what](#dash-boards--who-may-do-what).

faq.q: Can I share a board with someone?
faq.md:
Yes, with anyone signed in to your workspace who may open Dashboards: copy the board's address, filters included. It
never opens without signing in. See [Share a board](#dash-boards--share-a-board).

faq.q: Why are some values masked for me?
faq.md:
Those columns are marked sensitive in the Data Catalog and you have no access to them. Ask for access for a time from
the asset's panel. See [Ask for access to masked values](#dash-catalog--ask-for-access-to-masked-values).

faq.q: A widget says "Not by" a filter. Is that an error?
faq.md:
No. That widget's data has no column the filter can land on, so it shows everything. Its editor can list the column's
other names in the filter. See [Add a filter bar](#dash-build--add-a-filter-bar).

faq.q: How do I get an Ask your data answer onto a board?
faq.md:
Choose **Pin to dashboard** under its chart, and pick a board or name a new one. It reruns its query each time the
board opens. See [Put an Ask your data answer on a board](#dash-ask-pin).

faq.q: Can I download what I see?
faq.md:
Yes: **Export CSV** on a table widget, **Download CSV** under an Ask your data answer, and **Download** under a result
in Analytics Studio (CSV, TSV or JSON). See [Take the result away](#dash-studio--take-the-result-away).

topics.title: Developers and the API
topics.blurb: API clients, the sandbox, runs and events from your systems, webhooks and the portal.
topics.summary:
Your organisation's own systems use the API to start runs, send events, files and form answers, read what runs made
and decide reviews, and webhooks tell them when something happens. A workspace administrator gives each system an API
client with only the scopes it needs; the Developer portal holds the guides and samples for the developers.

start.title: See what the API is for
start.text: What your systems can do, and what an administrator sets up.

start.title: Try it in the sandbox
start.text: Test keys against sample pipelines, never billed.

start.title: Make an API client
start.text: Scopes, limits, IP allowlist, embed sites; copy the secret once.

start.title: Hear back with webhooks
start.text: Subscribe a URL, check the signature, read the delivery log.

start.title: Hand the portal to your developers
start.text: Guides, reference and samples in curl, Python and Node.js.

faq.q: I lost an API client's secret. Can I see it again?
faq.md:
No: a secret is shown once. Make a new one with **New secret** in the client's menu; the old one stops working at
once, so give the new one to the system straight away. See [Change, rotate or revoke](#dev-clients--change-rotate-or-revoke).

faq.q: Is testing in the sandbox billed?
faq.md:
No. Nothing a test key does is billed, and its usage never appears on your invoice. See
[The sandbox and test keys](#dev-sandbox).

faq.q: A system sent the same request twice. Did it start two runs?
faq.md:
Not if it sent the same **Idempotency-Key**: the second answer is the first run. See
[Send it twice, get one run](#dev-runs--send-it-twice-get-one-run).

faq.q: Our receiver was down. Did we miss the webhooks?
faq.md:
No: each delivery is tried again for a day, and **Deliveries** shows each one with **Send again**. A webhook with no
success for 3 days is paused until you resume it. See [Retries and pausing](#dev-webhooks--retries-and-pausing).

faq.q: What are the API's limits?
faq.md:
By default 600 calls a minute for each client and 1,200 for the whole workspace, with bursts, and a monthly quota if
your account has one. See [Limits](#dev-clients--limits).

faq.q: How do I let a portal show a run?
faq.md:
List the portal's site under **Sites that may embed its run views** on its client; the portal then asks for
15-minute view links. See [Embed a run view](#dev-embed).

faq.q: Who may read the Developer portal?
faq.md:
Administrators, and members whose page access names **Developer portal**. See
[Give a developer access](#dev-portal--give-a-developer-access).

topics.title: Billing
topics.blurb: How usage is counted, Cost & usage, estimates, invoices and what is not billed.
topics.summary:
Everything a workspace uses is metered as it happens and priced from its rate card. Cost & usage shows the month as the
invoice will read it, down to each pipeline, run and model call; each closed month becomes an invoice with its PDF,
payments, credit notes and receipts, all kept under Billing documents.

start.title: Learn how usage is counted
start.text: Every meter in plain words, and your billing time zone.

start.title: Read Cost & usage
start.text: The month so far, by day, service, line, pipeline, run and model call.

start.title: Estimate a backfill
start.text: The runs it will make and what they should cost, before you start.

start.title: Pay an invoice
start.text: Drafts, issued invoices, credit notes, card or bank slip, receipts.

start.title: Find a billing document
start.text: Every bill, slip, receipt and statement, and checking a receipt.

faq.q: Why does the month on Cost & usage change after the month has ended?
faq.md:
Usage is rolled up every few minutes, so the last runs of a month catch up shortly after it ends. Once the month is
over in your billing time zone its invoice is issued and frozen. See [Invoices, credit notes and paying](#bill-invoices).

faq.q: Which time zone are my days counted in?
faq.md:
Your workspace's billing time zone, shown as **Days in** on Cost & usage and beside the invoice's period (America/Chicago
unless your account team set another). See [Your billing time zone](#bill-usage--your-billing-time-zone).

faq.q: What does one pipeline cost me?
faq.md:
Open **Cost by pipeline** on Cost & usage: each pipeline's runs, cost, cost per run and what it was spent on, and each
run below. See [Cost by pipeline and by run](#bill-cost--cost-by-pipeline-and-by-run).

faq.q: Is testing in the sandbox billed?
faq.md: No, never. See [What is not billed](#bill-not-billed).

faq.q: If I retry a failed run, do I pay twice?
faq.md:
Not for the steps that already worked: **Retry from the failed step** reuses their outputs. **Run again from the
start** runs, and bills, every step again. See [Not billed twice](#bill-not-billed--not-billed-twice).

faq.q: How do I pay?
faq.md:
With **Pay now** by card, when card payment is on for your account, or by bank transfer with **Upload payment slip**.
A receipt is issued once the payment is confirmed. See [Pay an invoice](#bill-invoices--pay-an-invoice).

faq.q: A line on my bill looks wrong. What can I do?
faq.md:
Choose the line on Cost & usage to see what is behind it, then ask your account team: credit notes and corrections are
theirs. See [Line by line](#bill-cost--line-by-line).

topics.title: Security and privacy
topics.blurb: Sign-in security, keeping data apart, the managed service, data policies, retention and audit.
topics.summary: How the console protects your workspace and its data: the sign-in rules, how workspaces are kept apart and when our team may see yours, which models may see which data, masked columns, how long data is kept, and where every action is recorded.

start.text: One rule per data level.

start.text: Days per kind of data, previewed first.

start.text: Sign-ins, access changes and approvals.

faq.q: How do I hide patient identifiers from researchers?
faq.md: Mark the columns sensitive in the Data Catalog; they are masked for anyone without access. See [Masked columns](#sec-data-policies--masked-columns).

faq.q: Can your staff see our data?
faq.md: Only inside a recorded managed session, and everything they change or open is listed for your administrators. See [What our team can see, and when](#sec-data-yours--what-our-team-can-see-and-when).

faq.q: Can the console write to our database?
faq.md: No. Database connections are read-only. See [What the console never does](#sec-data-yours--what-the-console-never-does).

faq.q: Does sensitive data go to a hosted AI model?
faq.md: Not by default: Sensitive data starts as **Local only**. See [Choose which models may see sensitive data](#sec-data-policies--choose-which-models-may-see-sensitive-data).

faq.q: How do I require two-factor sign-in only for clinicians?
faq.md: Turn it on on their access profile. See [Two-factor sign-in for everyone, or for some](#sec-sign-in--two-factor-sign-in-for-everyone-or-for-some).

faq.q: Is anything deleted automatically?
faq.md: Not until you set retention: it starts off, and keeps everything. See [Retention](#sec-retention).

faq.q: What changes if our workspace is managed by your team?
faq.md: The build screens become read-only for your people; you still run, review and manage access. See [The managed service](#sec-managed).

faq.q: Does the console make us compliant?
faq.md: No product does that by itself; it gives you the controls. See [Working with health data](#sec-health-data).

topics.title: Settings, alerts and help
topics.blurb: Alerts, model connections, the registries, configuration values, appearance and help.
topics.summary:
The workspace's settings: alert rules that tell the right people when runs fail, schedules miss or reviews wait; the
models, tools and tasks the workspace may use; the values pipelines read at run time; the console's look; and where to
find help.

start.title: Get told when something fails
start.text: Alert rules, who hears of them, and alerts that open and resolve.

start.title: Decide what may be used
start.text: Model connections, the Tool Registry and the Task Registry.

start.text: Configuration values, home pages, task groups, topics.

start.title: Pick a theme
start.text: Your own theme, and the workspace's default.

start.title: Find help
start.text: The help centre, the Developer portal, and whom to ask.

faq.q: How do I get told when a run fails?
faq.md:
Make a rule under **Settings › Alerts** that watches **Runs failed**, or choose **Add the recommended rules**, and pick
who hears of it and how. See [Make a rule](#set-alerts--make-a-rule).

faq.q: An alert went away by itself. Is that right?
faq.md:
Yes: an alert resolves by itself when the trouble clears, for example when a later run of the pipeline completes. It
says *cleared by itself*. See [Read the alerts](#set-alerts--read-the-alerts).

faq.q: Can I stop an alert from waking people at night?
faq.md:
Yes: give the rule **Quiet hours**. Mail waits until they end; the bell and webhooks are not held. Or **Mute** the rule
for a while. See [Make a rule](#set-alerts--make-a-rule).

faq.q: Where do I put a password a pipeline needs?
faq.md:
In **Configuration values**, as a secret; the pipeline names it as `${secret:KEY}`. It is never shown again. See
[Configuration values](#set-reference--configuration-values).

faq.q: Why is a tool or a task marked Blocked?
faq.md:
Our team blocked it for the workspace; the row says who and why, and it cannot be switched on from the workspace. Ask
your account team. See [Model connections, Tool Registry and Task Registry](#set-registries).

faq.q: How do I change the console to dark?
faq.md:
Pick **Dark** (or another theme) from the theme button in the top bar, or under **Theme** on your profile. See
[Pick your own theme](#set-appearance--pick-your-own-theme).

topics.title: Troubleshooting and FAQ
topics.blurb: What a message means and how to fix it, and the questions people ask most.
topics.summary:
When something does not work, the console says what and where: a failed step with its message, a skipped item with
its reason, a report that was not made with what to do. This topic is organised by those messages, each with its cause
and its fix, and ends with the questions people ask most.

start.text: Read the failure, then retry from the failed step.

start.title: Files and media
start.text: Photos, conversions and recordings that cannot be read.

start.text: Calls refused up front, by the other system, or by a contract.

start.title: Documents, contracts and reports
start.text: Contracts, duplicates, page limits and missing pictures.

start.title: Approvals
start.text: Rejected, expired, overdue, or skipped in bulk.

start.title: Frequently asked questions
start.text: About thirty short answers.

faq.q: Where do I see why a run failed?
faq.md:
On the run's page: the failed step is marked red with its message, and **Runs › Failed** groups the same error across
runs. See [When a run or a step fails](#ts-runs--read-a-failure).

faq.q: Will a retry run every step again?
faq.md:
No. **Retry from step N** reuses what the earlier steps kept; **Run again from the start** runs them all. See
[Retry](#ts-runs--retry).

faq.q: "No object at …": what is missing?
faq.md:
The file the step reads is not in the bucket, or not under that name. See
[A missing file](#ts-runs--a-missing-file-no-object-at).

faq.q: Why did Call API fail before calling anything?
faq.md:
The input needed more calls than the step's **At most calls** allows, so nothing was sent or billed. See
[Connections and APIs](#ts-connections).

faq.q: Why was my report not made?
faq.md:
It was over the workspace's page limit, or a field it needs was missing. See
[Documents, contracts and reports](#ts-documents--a-report-over-the-page-limit).

faq.q: Why can't I see the Billing menu?
faq.md: Billing is for workspace administrators. See [Frequently asked questions](#ts-faq--access-and-the-menu).

topics.blurb: The words the console uses, the menu, schedule frequencies, roles and run statuses.
topics.summary:
The words the ETL Console uses, in plain words from A to Z, and the facts people look up: the menu, the ways a schedule
repeats, what each role may do, and what a run's status means.

start.text: About a hundred terms, each with where to read more.

faq.q: What is the difference between a pipeline, a schedule and a run?
faq.md:
A pipeline is what is done, a schedule is when it is done, and a run is one time it was done. See the
[Glossary](#gl-glossary).

faq.q: What do Skip and Missed mean?
faq.md:
**Skip**: passed over on purpose, or because the last run was still going. **Missed**: its time passed while nothing
was running to take it. See [Run statuses](#gl-reference--run-statuses).

faq.q: Why does the run's page say "Queued" when the list says "Queue"?
faq.md:
They are the same status: lists show the short word, the run's page the full one. See
[Run statuses](#gl-reference--run-statuses).

faq.q: In which time zone does a cron expression run?
faq.md: In server time, Chicago. See [Schedule frequencies](#gl-reference--schedule-frequencies).

faq.q: What can a workspace member do that a viewer cannot?
faq.md: Both are workspace members; what each may open is their page access profile. See [Roles](#gl-reference--roles).

topics.title: Recipes: build it yourself
topics.blurb: Step-by-step guides that build each worked example from an empty workspace, with sample files to download.
topics.summary:
Each recipe builds one working example in your own workspace, from nothing: what you will build, what you need first,
every step with the exact screen names and the values to type, how to check it worked, and the mistakes people make.
The sample files are synthetic and download from each recipe. Follow the patient journey in order, or pick any recipe on
its own.

faq.q: Do I need the Summit Valley workspace to follow these?
faq.md:
No. Every recipe starts from an empty workspace and gives you the sample files. Summit Valley Health System is the
fictional example the screenshots come from.

faq.q: Are the sample files real patient data?
faq.md:
No. Every file is synthetic and made up for this guide, and the people in them are fictional. Use synthetic or
de-identified data while you learn.

faq.q: A recipe says "Not yet verified end to end". What does that mean?
faq.md:
The steps were written from the product and checked piece by piece, but the whole recipe has not been run from start
to finish yet. Follow it, and if a step differs from your screen, the screen wins.

faq.q: Which recipe should I start with?
faq.md:
If you are new, [Find duplicate patient records](#rcp-mpi-duplicates) is the shortest complete pipeline. For reports,
start with [A branded one-page report](#rcp-branded-report).

faq.q: The counts in "Check it worked" don't match mine.
faq.md:
Check you used the sample file unchanged and the same settings; a filter or a date left at its default changes the
counts. The [Troubleshooting](#ts-runs) topic explains the messages.

topics.title: Manual test guide
topics.blurb: Numbered checks with steps, expected results and a pass/fail box, feature area by feature area.
topics.summary:
A checklist for testing the ETL Console by hand, one article per feature area, in the order of this book. Each check has
a number that never changes, exact steps with the screen names, the result you should see, and a box to tick. Roles and
isolation are tested in every area: what a reviewer, a viewer and a front-desk person may open, and that a second
workspace can see and open nothing of yours.

start.text: An administrator, a second administrator, a reviewer, a viewer, a front desk, a researcher and someone in a second workspace.

start.text: Profiles, one person's tabs, delegates and teams.

start.text: Three wards in, two out, every number known.

start.text: Run reviews, Approval steps, workflows and bulk decisions.

start.text: A researcher sees sensitive columns masked until access is granted.

faq.q: Which accounts do I need?
faq.md:
Seven test accounts, each with a letter used in the steps: A, A2, R, V, F, RS and X. See
[The test accounts](#qa-guide--the-test-accounts).

faq.q: What do I do when a check fails?
faq.md:
Keep the screen, take a screenshot, note the run's number and the exact message, then write what you expected and what
you saw. See [When a check fails](#qa-guide--when-a-check-fails).

faq.q: What does "(not yet verified)" mean?
faq.md:
The behaviour is built or planned but has not been seen working end to end. Test it like any other check: your result
is how it becomes verified. See [How a check reads](#qa-guide--how-a-check-reads).

faq.q: May I use real patient data to make a test realistic?
faq.md: No. Every file, answer and number must be made up. See [Synthetic data only](#qa-guide--synthetic-data-only).

faq.q: How do I test that the AI never writes to a database or invents a file?
faq.md:
Ask the AI Assistant to do exactly that: it must refuse the write and name the missing file. See
[the AI Assistant checks](#qa-ai--the-ai-assistant).

faq.q: How do I test that another workspace cannot see our data?
faq.md:
Copy the addresses of a run, a form, a document and a dashboard, and open them signed in to the second workspace. See
[Workspaces are kept apart](#qa-security--workspaces-are-kept-apart).

faq.q: Can a check's number change?
faq.md: No. Once printed, a number stays; new checks are added at the end of their area.

articles.title: Your workspace
articles.summary: What a workspace holds, its name and time zones, its default theme, and the difference between self-managed and managed by our team.
articles.who: Workspace administrators; the name and billing time zone are set by the platform's team
articles.md:
A **workspace** is your organisation's own space in the console. It holds everything else: its people and their access, connections, pipelines, schedules, runs, files, reports, dashboards, settings and bills. Nothing crosses from one workspace to another, and a person belongs to exactly one.

Your workspace's administrators run it from **Administration & billing › Administration**, whose tabs are **Users**, **Teams**, **Page access**, **Sign-in security**, **Data policies** and **Appearance** (and **Activity** when our team works in it).

## Its name
The workspace's name shows on **Your profile** (under **Workspace**), on **Administration › Users** and in the bar our staff see while they work in it. It is set when the workspace is created; to change it, ask the platform's team.

## Its time zones
- **Times on screen** are shown in each person's own device time zone, on the 24-hour clock.
- **Billing days and months** are counted in the workspace's **billing time zone** (America/Chicago unless the platform's team set another). **Billing › Cost & usage** shows it as **Days in …**. A change takes effect from the next month that has not started, never the month under way, and issued invoices never change.
- **Retention** runs its daily pass after 02:00 Chicago time.

## Its default theme
People who have not chosen a theme of their own open the console in the workspace's default theme. Set it under [Appearance](#adm-appearance).

## Self-managed or managed by our team
A workspace is built either by its own administrators or by our team for you.

| | Self-managed | Managed by our team |
|---|---|---|
| Who builds pipelines, schedules, connections and forms | Your administrators | Our team |
| What your administrators can still do | Everything | Manage people and access, run pipelines (**Run now**), review and approve, read results and bills |
| Build screens | Editable | Read-only, with the note **Managed by our team** |
| Our team's work | Only in a recorded managed session | In a recorded managed session |
| **Administration › Activity** | Appears once our team has acted in the workspace | Always there |

![The note on a build screen in a managed workspace](adm-managed-banner "Managed by our team: the build screens are read-only; ask your account team for a change")

The platform's team switches a workspace between the two. Whichever it is, everything our staff change or open in your workspace is recorded: see [The managed service](#sec-managed).

> **Tip:** Give the workspace at least two administrators, so nobody is locked out when one is away.

## Example
Summit Valley Health System is a self-managed workspace with two administrators: the Summit Valley admin builds the pipelines and Jordan Reyes, the operations director, approves report assets and covers when the first is away. Its billing time zone is America/Chicago and its default theme is Light.

articles.title: Add a person and choose their role
articles.summary: Add someone to the workspace, pick Workspace member or Workspace administrator, give them a profile, and edit them later on their own page.
articles.who: Workspace administrators
articles.popular: Add a person
articles.md:
Everyone who signs in to your workspace is on **Administration › Users**. Each person has a **role**, which says how much they may do, and (for members) a **page access profile**, which says which pages they open. Roles are enforced on the server: they decide what a person can reach, not just what they see.

![Administration › Users](adm-users "Users: the people by standing at the top, then the table with role, access, last sign-in and state")

## The two roles
| Role | Opens | May change |
|---|---|---|
| **Workspace member** | The pages on their page access profile (or the workspace default) | Only what those pages allow: running, reviewing, reading |
| **Workspace administrator** | Every page of the workspace; page access does not apply | People, connections, pipelines, policies and settings |

Give someone the administrator role only when they look after the workspace itself.

## Add a person
1. Open **Administration › Users** and choose **New user**.
2. Under **Who and how they sign in**, type the **Full name** and the **Email**; the email is their sign-in.
3. Leave **Password** empty to have the console email them a one-time password. If you type one, it is not emailed: you pass it on yourself.
4. Under **Role and access**, pick the **Role**. For a member, pick their **Page access** profile, or leave **Workspace default**.
5. Under **About them**, add their **Position** (job title), their **Manager** and their **Phone** if you like. The manager is whom their workflow approvals go to when a step says "their manager", and whom their overdue tasks escalate to.
6. Choose **Create**.

![The New user dialog](adm-new-user "New user: who they are, their role and page access, and about them")

The person appears as **Invited** until they first sign in. At that sign-in they choose their own password, and set up two-factor sign-in if your workspace or their profile requires it.

## Find people
The tiles at the top count the people by standing (**Active**, **Deactivated**, **Invited**, **Locked**, **2FA on**, **2FA off**, **Single sign-on**, **Administrators**, **Members**, **Signed in · 30 days**, **Never signed in**); choose one to filter the list. Filter further by role (**All roles**), profile (**All access**) and state (**All states**), or search by name or email. **Table** and **Cards** show the same people.

## Edit a person
Choose **Edit** in a person's row menu (the three dots) to open their own page. It has six parts:
1. **Profile**: picture, name, email, position, manager and phone.
2. **Role and access**: the role, the **Page access profile**, their **Teams** (add or take them out), and **What they can see**, their menu as it will be after you save.
3. **Sign-in security**: whether two-factor is on, their last sign-in, their password and any lock, with **Reset password**, **Unlock** and **Reset two-factor login**, and the sessions they have open.
4. **Activity**: their recent sign-ins and the account's history.
5. **Notifications**: where the console's notices reach them, and who reports to them.
6. **Danger zone**: deactivate or delete the account.

Choose **Save changes** for the profile, role and access; the other parts act at once.

![A person's role and access](adm-user-access "Role and access: the role, the profile, the teams, and what they can see")

> **Note:** Nobody changes their own role, and the workspace is fixed once the account exists.

## Example
The Summit Valley admin adds Rosa Alvarez: **Full name** Rosa Alvarez, her work email, **Role** Workspace member, **Page access** Nurse, **Position** Charge nurse, Ward 4B. She is then added to the Ward 4B nursing team on her page. At her first sign-in she chooses her own password; had her profile required two-factor sign-in, she would set up her app then too.

articles.title: Reset a password or remove someone's access
articles.summary: Reset a password, unlock an account, reset two-factor sign-in, sign someone out, deactivate or delete an account.
articles.who: Workspace administrators
articles.popular: Reset someone's password
articles.md:
When someone forgets their password, loses their phone or leaves, an administrator puts it right from **Administration › Users**: from the person's row menu (the three dots) or from their own page.

![A person's Sign-in security](adm-user-security "Sign-in security on a person's page: two-factor, last sign-in, password and lock, with Reset password and Reset two-factor login")

## Reset someone's password
1. Open **Administration › Users** and, in the person's row menu, choose **Reset password**.
2. Type a **New password** that meets the workspace's rules (the rules tick as you type).
3. Choose **Reset password**.
4. The notice at the top right offers **Copy password** for two minutes. Pass the password to the person by a channel you trust.

They sign in with it and are asked to choose their own straight away. The password is stored hashed and nobody can read it back.

## Unlock an account
After too many failed sign-ins in a row an account is locked for a while, and administrators are told. The person's row shows **Locked**. Choose **Unlock** in the row menu to let them try again now.

## Reset two-factor sign-in
For someone who lost their phone and their recovery codes:
1. Make sure it is really them asking.
2. In their row menu choose **Reset two-factor login**, then confirm.

Their authenticator app and recovery codes stop working and they are signed out everywhere. If two-factor sign-in is required of them, they set it up again at their next sign-in.

## Sign someone out
On the person's page, **Sessions open now** lists where they are signed in; **Sign out everywhere** ends them all.

## Remove someone's access
Choose between two:

| | Deactivate | Delete |
|---|---|---|
| What it does | Signs them out everywhere and stops them signing in | Removes the account for good: they can never sign in again |
| Their work, schedules and history | Kept | What they made and the account's history stay; their profile picture and their page exceptions go |
| Can it be undone? | Yes: **Activate** | No |

1. In the person's row menu choose **Deactivate** (or, on their page under **Danger zone**, **Deactivate**).
2. Confirm. The row now reads **Inactive**.

To delete, choose **Delete** in the row menu (or **Delete user** under **Danger zone**) and confirm.

> **Warning:** Deactivate first when you are not sure. A deactivated account can be switched back on; a deleted one cannot.

> **Note:** You cannot deactivate or delete your own account.

![The Danger zone](adm-user-danger "Danger zone: deactivate or delete the account")

## Example
Kevin Lee in finance leaves Summit Valley at the end of the month. The admin deactivates his account on his last day, so his expense claims and their history stay; his manager Claire Martin's approvals are unaffected.

articles.title: Page access profiles
articles.summary: Bundles of pages for members: whole pages or some of their tabs, the default profile, a custom profile, and requiring two-factor sign-in on a profile.
articles.who: Workspace administrators
articles.popular: Make an access profile
articles.md:
A **page access profile** is a named bundle of pages for workspace members: Clinician, Nurse, Billing analyst, Viewer. Each member holds one; anyone without a profile of their own gets the workspace's **default** profile. Administrators always open everything, so profiles do not apply to them.

![Administration › Page access](adm-access-profiles "Page access: the profiles, who can open what, and Check a person")

## How it works
- A workspace with **no profiles** lets every member open every page. The first profile you make becomes the default, and everyone without one moves onto it.
- A profile opens **whole pages**, and for a page with tabs, **every tab or only some**.
- **Home**, **Your profile** and **Notifications** are always open; **Administration** stays administrator-only.
- On top of a profile, a page or tab can be opened or withheld **for one person**: see [Give a person only some tabs](#adm-some-tabs).
- A profile can **require two-factor sign-in** of the people on it.

The top of the page counts the **Profiles**, the **People assigned**, the **Default** and the **Pages** that can be granted. **Who can open what** explains how roles and profiles combine.

## Make an access profile
1. Open **Administration › Page access** and choose **New profile**.
2. Type the **Profile name** (for example Clinician) and a one-line **Description** of who it is for.
3. Tick **Default for this workspace** if members without a profile should get this one.
4. Tick **Require two-factor sign-in** if its people must use an authenticator app.
5. Under **Pages this profile opens**, tick the pages. They are grouped as the menu groups them, and each page lists the places on the menu it opens. Use the search box, **Chosen** and **Not chosen**, a group's checkbox, or a hub's **All** and **None** to go faster.
6. For a page with tabs, untick the tabs this profile should not open. A tab marked **hides the tab** has no data of its own: unticking it only hides it.
7. Where a page offers **Edit** beside it (such as dashboards), tick it to let the profile save, pin and delete there as well as read.
8. Check **What this person will see** on the right: the menu a member on this profile will have.
9. Choose **Create profile**.

![Editing the Clinician profile](adm-profile-editor "A profile: name, default, two-factor, the pages it opens, and what its people will see")

## Change or remove a profile
In a profile's menu (the three dots on its card):
- **Edit pages** opens it to change; choose **Save changes**.
- **Make default** makes it the workspace's default.
- **Delete** removes it. A profile someone holds cannot be deleted: move its people to another profile first.

Changes reach people at their next sign-in or when their session refreshes.

## Assign people to profiles
- When you add or edit a person on **Administration › Users**, pick their **Page access profile**.
- Or switch to **People × pages** on **Page access**: each member's row shows their profile and every page. The profile row shows the baseline; tick a box to open or withhold that page for that person alone.

**Check a person** shows what one member opens and which pages were opened or withheld for them alone.

## Require two-factor sign-in on a profile
Tick **Require two-factor sign-in** on the profile. Its people set up an authenticator app at their next sign-in and cannot switch it off. The profile card then shows **Two-factor required**, with how many on it have not set it up yet; the editor names them. To require it of everyone instead, use [Sign-in security](#sec-sign-in).

## Example: Summit Valley's profiles
| Profile | Opens (in menu words) | Two-factor |
|---|---|---|
| Clinician | Forms › Submissions, Runs › Analytics, Review, Dashboards (with Edit), Reports › Overview and Library, approving and signing reports | Required |
| Nurse | Forms, Runs, Review, Dashboards, Reports, Documents › Intake and Analysis › Files | |
| Researcher | Analysis: Ask your data, Analytics Studio, Data Catalog; Dashboards | |
| Viewer (default) | Runs › Analytics, Dashboards | |

The Researcher sees sensitive columns masked: see [Data policies](#sec-data-policies).

> **Note:** The profile cards and the person-by-person list name a few pages by their own names rather than the menu's: **Queue** is Runs › Latest, By date and Failed; **Run analytics** is Runs › Analytics; **Saved Analyses** is Dashboards; **Review queue** is Review › Documents; **Task inbox** is Review › Approvals, Runs and My requests; **Browse files** is Analysis › Files.

## Limits
| What | Limit |
|---|---|
| Profile name | 100 characters |
| Description | 500 characters |
| Profiles per member | 1 (plus pages opened or withheld for them alone) |
| Who may make profiles | Workspace administrators only; a delegate may move people between existing profiles if allowed |

articles.title: Give a person only some tabs
articles.summary: Open or withhold a page or a tab for one person, for a number of days or until removed, with a reason kept in the change log.
articles.who: Workspace administrators; an access delegate for the people their delegation reaches
articles.popular: Give a person only some tabs
articles.md:
Sometimes one person needs a little more or a little less than their profile gives: a nurse covering month-end needs **Runs › Failed** for a week; a clinician should see **Review › Approvals** but not **Review › Runs**. Rather than make a new profile, open or withhold that page or tab for them alone.

![Grant pages and tabs for one person](adm-grant-tabs "Grant pages and tabs: each page Open, Some tabs or Closed for this person, with its tabs underneath")

## Open or withhold for one person
1. Open **Administration › Page access** and scroll to **Grant pages and tabs**. Make sure **A person** is chosen.
2. Pick the **Person**.
3. Under **For**, choose how long: **Until removed**, **7 days**, **30 days** or **90 days**.
4. Type a **Reason**. It is kept in the change log.
5. In the list, each page reads **Open**, **Some tabs** or **Closed** for them:
   - **Open** or **Open every tab** opens the whole page.
   - **Withhold** closes it.
   - Tick or untick a tab under a page to open or close only that tab.

Each change applies at once and is recorded under **Changes**. The person's menu follows at their next sign-in or when their session refreshes.

## How tabs combine
- A page with **no tab chosen** opens every tab.
- A tab marked **hides the tab** has no data of its own: closing it hides it from the menu, and its data is the page's. Other tabs, when closed, also have their data refused by the server.
- What you open for one person adds to their profile; what you withhold takes away from it. Their profile is not changed.

## Put someone back on their profile
On **People × pages**, reset the person's exceptions to bring them back to their profile alone. The change log records it as **Back to their profile**.

## Example
Dr. Anika Patel's Clinician profile opens Review. For one week of ward cover the Summit Valley admin also opens **Runs › By date** for her: **Person** Dr. Anika Patel, **For** 7 days, **Reason** "Ward 4B cover, 3–9 Nov", then ticks **Runs by date** under **Queue**. After seven days the tab closes again on its own.

> **Note:** The list names some pages by their own names: **Queue** is Runs › Latest, By date and Failed, **Task inbox** is Review › Approvals, Runs and My requests. See the note in [Page access profiles](#adm-access-profiles).

articles.title: Delegates
articles.summary: Let a trusted member grant pages and tabs to the people they manage, for 90 days or another period, within limits; every grant is in Changes.
articles.who: Workspace administrators set up a delegation; the delegate then grants on Page access
articles.md:
A **delegate** is a workspace member who may grant access to other members without being an administrator: a director who opens their team's pages, or HR who gives new starters the HR or Viewer pages. The delegation lasts a set time and has firm limits, and everything a delegate does is recorded.

![Delegates on Page access](adm-delegates "Delegates: who may grant, to whom, for how long, and why")

## Make someone a delegate
1. Open **Administration › Page access**, scroll to **Grant pages and tabs** and choose **Delegates**.
2. Under **Member who may grant**, pick the member.
3. Under **To whom**, choose **Every member** or **Only people I choose**, and tick the people.
4. Under **For**, choose **90 days** (the default), **30 days**, **180 days** or **A year**.
5. Tick **May move people between existing profiles** if they may also change which profile someone holds.
6. Type **Why**. The access review reads it.
7. Choose **Delegate**.

The delegation appears in the list with its **Until** date and state **Active**. **End** stops it at once; when its time runs out it reads **Expired**.

## The limits
A delegate:
- grants only pages and tabs they hold themselves;
- never grants to an administrator or to themselves;
- never creates, changes or deletes profiles (at most moves people between existing ones, if allowed);
- reaches only the people the delegation names.

## What the delegate sees
A delegate sees **Administration › Page access** in their menu, showing only **Grant access for the people you manage**, a line saying who delegated it and until when, and **A person** and **Changes**. They grant as an administrator does: see [Give a person only some tabs](#adm-some-tabs).

## Every change is recorded
**Changes** lists every access change in the workspace, newest first: **When**, **Who** made it, **What** (for example **Opened a tab**, **Withheld a page**, **Moved to a profile**, **Back to their profile**, **Delegated access**, **Ended a delegation**, **Changed a profile's two-factor rule**), the **Person**, the **Page or tab**, **Until** and **Why**. A delegate's own **Changes** shows the changes they made.

![The change log](adm-changes "Changes: every access change, who made it and why")

## Example
At Summit Valley, Owen Wright in HR is a delegate for 90 days, for every member, and may move people between existing profiles. His reason: "HR grants HR and Viewer pages to the HR and Facilities teams". When a new facilities coordinator starts, Owen moves her onto the Viewer profile himself; the change shows under **Changes** with his name and reason.

articles.title: Teams
articles.summary: Groups of people that approvals, reviews, alerts and report approvals can go to; leads and members; what teams are for and what they are not.
articles.who: Workspace administrators make teams and name leads; a team's lead adds and removes its members
articles.popular: Make a team and name its lead
articles.md:
A **team** is a group of people who work together: Physicians, Ward 4B nursing, Pharmacy, Finance controls. Work can be sent to a team instead of to one person, so whoever in the team is free picks it up. A person can be in many teams.

Teams are used for:
- **approval workflows**: a step can be assigned to a team;
- **run reviews** and **workflow tasks** waiting for the team;
- **alerts**: an alert rule can notify a team;
- **Report Studio**: the reviewers who approve reports and the publishers of templates can be a team.

Teams open no pages. What a person may open is their page access.

![Administration › Teams](adm-teams "Teams: each team's lead, members and where it is used")

## Make a team and name its lead
1. Open **Administration › Teams** and choose **New team**.
2. Type its **Name** (for example Wound care nurses) and, if you like, a **Description**. Choose **Make team**.
3. In the team's panel, under **Add a person**, choose someone, pick **Member** or **Lead**, and choose **Add**. Repeat for each person.
4. To make an existing member the lead, change **Member** to **Lead** beside their name.

![A team's panel](adm-team-panel "The team's panel: about, members with Member or Lead, and where it is used")

## Leads and members
- A **lead** adds and removes the team's members. They reach the team from **Review › Approvals** (**My teams**, then **See who is in your teams**).
- Only an administrator names a team's leads, renames it or archives it.
- A team with **No lead** is changed by administrators only.

## Find and read teams
The tiles count **Teams**, **People in teams**, **Leads** and teams **Without a lead**. Search by team, description or person, or filter by lead, member and state. **Used by** shows how many workflows, approvals, alerts and Report Studio settings send work to the team; **Where it is used** in the panel names them, each a link.

You can also add a person to a team from their own page on **Administration › Users** (**Teams**, then **Add to a team…**).

## Archive a team
In the team's panel choose **Archive team**. Nothing new goes to an archived team, and its history keeps its name. Show archived teams with the state filter.

> **Tip:** Before archiving, check **Where it is used**: a workflow step or alert that names the team will have nobody to send to.

## Example
Summit Valley's Physicians team has Dr. Anika Patel (lead), Dr. Minh Nguyen and Dr. Chidi Okafor. **Where it is used** shows the Patient journey's care-plan and discharge approvals and the Report Studio reviewers, so either doctor can approve a discharge summary when Dr. Patel is with a patient.

articles.title: Out of office
articles.summary: Let a colleague act on your approvals while you are away; how their decisions show "for" you, and the rules.
articles.who: Anyone with approvals; an administrator can set it for someone else
articles.md:
When you are away, an **out of office** lets a colleague (your stand-in) act on the approval and workflow tasks assigned to you, for a set period. Every decision they make records both of you.

## How decisions show
A decision made by a stand-in appears in the request's history with both names, for example:

```A request's history
Care plan: approved by Dr. Minh Nguyen (for Dr. Anika Patel)
```

So the record always says who decided and on whose behalf.

## The rules
- An out of office runs from a start to an end in the future, **at most 90 days**. For longer, reassign the work instead.
- The stand-in must be an active person of the same workspace, and not yourself.
- You set your own; only an administrator sets one for someone else.
- One at a time: if one already covers those dates, cancel it first.
- It does not chain: your stand-in's own stand-in cannot act for you.
- Cancelling stops it at once. It is never deleted, so the history can always say who stood in for whom. Only the person away, or an administrator, can cancel it.

> **Note:** There is no page in the console for setting an out of office yet. For a single task, use **Pass on** in **Review › Approvals** instead: choose the task, **Pass on**, pick the person under **Pass it to**, add a note if you like, and choose **Pass on**.

## Other ways to keep work moving
- Send approvals to a [team](#adm-teams) rather than one person, so anyone in it can decide.
- Give each person a **Manager** on their page: overdue tasks escalate to them.

## Example
Dr. Anika Patel is at a conference for three days. Her out of office names Dr. Minh Nguyen. The care plan for a ward patient reaches Dr. Patel's list; Dr. Nguyen approves it, and its history reads "approved by Dr. Minh Nguyen (for Dr. Anika Patel)".

articles.title: Appearance
articles.summary: The workspace's default theme, which people see until they choose their own.
articles.who: Workspace administrators
articles.md:
**Appearance** sets the theme your workspace's people open the console in until they choose their own. Anyone can still pick another theme in the top bar or on **Your profile**; their own choice always wins.

![Administration › Appearance](adm-appearance "Default theme: the themes, the one saved now, and Save default")

## Set the default theme
1. Open **Administration › Appearance**.
2. Under **Default theme**, pick **System (no default)**, **Light**, **Dark**, **Ocean**, **Midnight** or **High contrast**. The line under the title says what is saved now.
3. Choose **Save default**. **Undo** goes back to the saved one before you save.
