| **When the image is missing** | `placeholder` |
| **At most pictures** | `12` |

6. The canvas now shows the six photos. **Validate**, then **Publish v1**.

![The Image grid's settings](rcp-b-grid-design "Summit Valley's Patient health chart, its Image grid selected: picture field image_key, caption field finding, pictures from the bucket, 40 mm high")

### Generate

1. **Create report** on the template's page, **Report name** `Wound photo review · 19 to 23 October 2026`.
2. Data: **Test sample** `Six visits`. **Preview and check**: the checks pass, and the preview shows the photos.
3. **Generate v1** and **Open the report**.

## Check it worked

- The Library has **Wound photo review · 19 to 23 October 2026**, **v1**, **Ready**.
- The PDF has the table with **6** rows (areas 9.24, 6.5, 4.1, 4.87, 3.6 and 12.57 cm²), then **Wound photos**: **2**
  rows of **3** photos, each 40 mm high, captioned like *SV-000117 · visit 1 · 2026-10-19 · 9.24 cm²*.
- Every photo shows its ruler and the SYNTHETIC banner; none shows the placeholder.
- SV-000117's three photos get smaller visit by visit, as the table's areas do.

## Common mistakes

| What you see | Why, and what to do |
|---|---|
| Grey placeholders instead of photos | A key does not match a file. Compare `photo_key` with the file's path under **Details**, letter for letter (case counts). |
| Every photo is missing, though the keys are right | **Pictures from** names another bucket, or you may not open this bucket in **Files**: the photos are read as you. |
| Photos missing only when a pipeline makes the report | The pipeline's rows give a different field name; set **Picture field** to the column the rows have. |
| The folder printed twice in the key | **Folder before the key** is filled in and `photo_key` also starts with the folder. Use one of them. |
| A row of photos moved to the next page | By design: a row of pictures never splits. Lower **Picture height** to fit more on a page. |
| A web address in `photo_key` does nothing | Pictures come from your storage (or a run's files), never from a web address. |

> **Privacy:** Real wound photos are health data. Keep them in a storage connection only the care team can open, and
> check who can see the reports in the report's **Access** tab.

> **Note:** Not yet verified end to end: this exact template was not generated in Summit Valley. Its Image grid
> settings are those of Summit Valley's *Patient health chart*, whose report (4 pages) was made and signed.

articles.title: A nightly schedule that reads only new files, and also starts when a file arrives
articles.summary: One pipeline and one schedule for an admissions feed: every night it reads only the files written since its last run, and a file dropped in the inbox starts a run for that file at once.
articles.who: A workspace administrator (a pipeline's Upload to bucket step is an administrator's); anyone whose page access includes Schedules & triggers sets the schedule
articles.popular: Read only the new files each night
articles.md:
Feeds arrive as many small files: admissions, discharges and transfers every hour, lab results, device readings. You
want each file read once, not every file every night. A **Read S3** step set to read only the objects written since the
schedule's last completed run does that; tick **A file arrives** on the same schedule and a file put in the inbox is
handled at once, between the nightly runs.

## What you'll build

- A pipeline, **ADT feed, nightly**: **Read S3** (new files only) → **Remove duplicates** → **Sort** →
  **Upload to bucket**.
- A schedule, **ADT feed (nightly and inbox)**: **On a timetable**, **Daily** at `02:00`, and **Also starts when** **A
  file arrives** named like `adt-*.csv`.
- Three runs that prove it: the first night reads both files waiting (240 rows, 230 events), the next run reads nothing
  new, and a dropped file starts a run of its own (120 rows).

Summit Valley's *ADT feed: hourly admissions, discharges and transfers* is the same pipeline, read hourly.

## What you need first

- A storage connection (its alias goes in **Bucket**; the examples use `summit-valley-s3`) and the workspace inbox
  (**File drop**, see [The file drop](#doc-file-drop)).
- The sample files, synthetic ADT events (`event_id`, `mrn`, `event_type`, `ward`, `event_time`), 120 rows each:
  - [adt-2026-10-01-a.csv](/help/samples/nightly-new-files/adt-2026-10-01-a.csv)
  - [adt-2026-10-01-b.csv](/help/samples/nightly-new-files/adt-2026-10-01-b.csv): its first 10 events repeat the last
    10 of file a, as feeds often do.
  - [adt-2026-10-02-a.csv](/help/samples/nightly-new-files/adt-2026-10-02-a.csv): the next day, for the File drop.
- Upload the two `2026-10-01` files to the folder `ops/adt/` of your bucket (**See results › Analysis › Files**, **New
  folder**, **Upload**). Keep the third for later.

## Build it

### The pipeline

1. **Build › Pipelines** → **New pipeline** → under **Add steps yourself**, **Name** `ADT feed, nightly`, **Create and
   add steps**.
2. **Add step from the Task Registry…** → **Read S3**:

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| **Key** / **Name** | `new` / `ADT files since the last run` |
| **Bucket** | your alias, such as `summit-valley-s3` |
| **Prefix** | `ops/adt/adt-` |
| **Read as** | `csv` |
| **At most objects** | `50` |
| **The run's own files first** | **Yes** (ticked) |
| **Which objects** | `last_run` |
| **CSV has a header row** | on (the default) |

3. Add **Remove duplicates**: **Key** `unique`, **Key columns** `event_id`, **Keep** `first`.
4. Add **Sort**: **Key** `ordered`, **Sort by** `event_time`, `asc`.
5. Add **Upload to bucket**: **Key** `keep`, **Bucket** your alias, **Object key** `ops/adt/clean/{{date}}-{{run}}.csv`,
   **Format** `csv`.
6. **Save**.

![The Read S3 step reading only new files](rcp-b-read-s3 "Summit Valley's ADT feed: Read S3 under ops/adt/adt-, read as csv, at most 50 objects, which objects last_run")

> **Tip:** With **The run's own files first** ticked, a run started by a file reads only that file; any other run reads
> the prefix. That is what lets one pipeline serve both ways in.

### The schedule

1. Open **Build › Pipelines › Schedules & triggers** and choose **New schedule** (or **Schedule** on the pipeline's page).
2. **Schedule name** `ADT feed (nightly and inbox)`, **Pipeline** `ADT feed, nightly`.
3. **When it runs**: **On a timetable**. Under **How often**: **Daily**, every `1` day at `02` : `00`.
4. **Also starts when**: tick **A file arrives**. **Which files** `adt-*.csv`. **Files per run** `1`.
5. **Email me when**: tick **A run fails**.
6. Read **What you will get** on the right: *Every 1 day at 02:00. Also when a file arrives in the inbox matching
   adt-\*.csv*, and the next five runs at 02:00 (server time, Chicago).
7. Leave **Active: runs as soon as it is saved** ticked, and **Create schedule**.

![A daily schedule that also starts when a file arrives](rcp-b-nightly-schedule "New schedule: on a timetable, daily at 02:00, and also when a file named adt-*.csv arrives; the next runs on the right")

## Check it worked

Do not wait for the night: start the first two runs by hand.

1. On the schedules list, the schedule's **⋮** → **Run now**. The run reads both files: **Read S3** `0 → 240`,
   **Remove duplicates** `240 → 230` (the 10 repeated events dropped), **Sort** `230 → 230`, and one file
   `ops/adt/clean/<today>-<run>.csv` with 230 rows.
2. **Run now** again. This run reads only what was written since the first completed: nothing. It completes with
   **Read S3** `0 → 0`, and the later steps run on 0 rows.
3. Open **Documents › Intake › File drop** and drop `adt-2026-10-02-a.csv`. It shows **Uploaded**, and a run of the
   schedule starts by itself, reading only that file: `0 → 120`, `120 → 120`.
4. The next night at 02:00 the timetable run reads anything new under `ops/adt/` and nothing else: the dropped file was
   stored under the inbox's own folder (`intake/<date>/…`), and its run already handled it.

> **Note:** Not yet verified end to end: Summit Valley's inbox-triggered schedules are switched off while the showcase
> is built, so the File drop run (step 3) was not seen there.

At Summit Valley the hourly ADT feed's first run read 24 files (2,880 rows) and kept 2,736 unique events; every hourly
run after it reads only the hour's new file.

## Common mistakes

| What you see | Why, and what to do |
|---|---|
| Every run reads every file again | **Which objects** is `all`. Set it to `last_run`. |
| A file seems to be read twice | Two schedules run the same pipeline: `last_run` counts per schedule. Keep one schedule. |
| After a failed run the same files come again | By design: a failed run moves nothing on, so the next run retries those files. Fix the cause and run again. |
| A dropped file starts nothing | **A file arrives** is not ticked, **Which files** does not match the name (`ADT-…` against `adt-*`: case counts), or the schedule is inactive. |
| The run started by a file read the whole folder | **The run's own files first** is off. |
| **Upload to bucket** cannot be added | It is a workspace administrator's step. |
| The timetable runs at the wrong hour | Schedule times are server time (Chicago), as **Next runs** says. |

articles.title: A form whose submissions start a pipeline
articles.summary: Build a five-field triage form, a pipeline that reads each submission and warns the charge nurse about abnormal vitals, and link the two with When submitted, start.
articles.who: A workspace administrator builds the form and the pipeline; anyone the form is shared with fills it in
articles.popular: Start a pipeline when a form is sent
articles.md:
A form can start a pipeline. Each submission is kept, written to the workspace inbox as a JSON file, and the schedule
the form names runs with it: the pipeline's first step reads the answers as one row, a column per field. Here a nurse's
triage answers are checked the moment they are sent, and only an abnormal reading sends a notice.

## What you'll build

- A form, **Nurse triage (recipe)**, with the fields `mrn`, `temp_c`, `hr`, `spo2` and `notes`.
- A pipeline, **Nurse triage, abnormal vitals**: **Read CSV/JSON/Parquet** (the submission) → **Compute** (the
  `abnormal` flag) → **Filter** (abnormal only) → **Send Notification** to the charge nurse.
- A schedule that runs **Only when started**, named in the form's **When submitted, start**.
- Two test submissions: one abnormal (a notice), one normal (no notice).

Summit Valley's *Nurse triage* form starts *Journey 5 · Nurse triage and abnormal vitals* the same way; its form
settings and notification step are the figures.

## What you need first

- The charge nurse as a person in the workspace (Rosa Alvarez). Find her number: open **Administration › Users**, open
  her page; the number at the end of the page's address (`/administration/users/1045`, say) is what **People** takes.
- The sample files:
  - [triage-test-entries.csv](/help/samples/form-trigger/triage-test-entries.csv): the two entries to type, and what
    each should do.
  - [triage-submission-sample.json](/help/samples/form-trigger/triage-submission-sample.json): a submission as the
    pipeline receives it, for **Test with sample**.

## Build it

### The pipeline and its schedule

1. **Build › Pipelines** → **New pipeline** → **Add steps yourself**, **Name** `Nurse triage, abnormal vitals`,
   **Create and add steps**.
2. Add **Read CSV/JSON/Parquet**: **Key** `submission`, **Name** `The triage submission`, **Bucket** and **File** left
   empty (it reads the run's own file: the submission), **Format** `json`.
3. Add **Compute**: **Key** `score`, one formula, **Column** `abnormal`, **Formula**:

```The abnormal flag
if(number(spo2) < 92 or number(hr) > 110 or number(temp_c) > 38.5, true, false)
```

   Tick **Empty when it cannot be worked out**, so a blank answer does not fail the run.
4. Add **Filter**: **Key** `abnormal_only`, one condition: **Column** `abnormal`, **Is** `eq`, **Value** `true`.
5. Add **Send Notification**: **Key** `tell`.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| **Title** | `Abnormal vitals: {{mrn}}` |
| **Message** | `SpO2 {{spo2}}, HR {{hr}}, temp {{temp_c}}. {{notes}}` |
| **Severity** | `WARNING` |
| **To** | `users` |
| **People** | the charge nurse's number, one per line |
| **Send** | `has_rows` |
| **Link** | `/review/all` |

6. **Save**. Open **Build › Pipelines › Schedules & triggers** → **New schedule**: **Schedule name** `Nurse triage
   (form)`, **Pipeline** `Nurse triage, abnormal vitals`, **When it runs** **Only when started**. **Create schedule**.

![The Send Notification step](rcp-b-triage-step "Summit Valley's Journey 5: the notice's title, message, WARNING, to one named person, only when there are rows")

### The form

1. **Get data in › Forms** → **New form**. On **Settings**, **Name** `Nurse triage (recipe)`.
2. On **Build**, add the fields:

| Type | Label | Key | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Text** | MRN | `mrn` | yes |
| **Number** | Temperature (°C) | `temp_c` | yes |
| **Number** | Heart rate (beats a minute) | `hr` | yes |
| **Number** | SpO2 (%) | `spo2` | yes |
| **Long text** | Notes | `notes` | no |

3. On **Settings**: **Status** **Active**; **When submitted, start** **Nurse triage (form)**; **Approval** **None: no
   approval**.
4. **Save**, then **Publish**.

![A form's Settings: Active, and the schedule it starts](rcp-b-form-settings "Summit Valley's Nurse triage form: Active, When submitted, start Journey 5, no approval, and its dataset")

> **Tip:** The keys are the column names the pipeline sees. Type them exactly as in the table; `{{mrn}}` in the notice
> only works because the key is `mrn`.

## Check it worked

1. Fill in the form twice (its **Fill in**), with the two entries of `triage-test-entries.csv`:
   - SV-000117, 38.9 °C, 112, 91, *Short of breath on exertion*
   - SV-000124, 36.8 °C, 78, 98, *Comfortable*
2. **Forms › Submissions** lists **2** submissions of *Nurse triage (recipe)*, each **Run started** with its run's number.
3. Both runs **Completed**. In the first, **Filter** keeps `1 → 1` and the notice is sent; in the second `1 → 0`, so
   **Send Notification** sends nothing.
4. Rosa Alvarez's bell has one notice, **Abnormal vitals: SV-000117**, *SpO2 91, HR 112, temp 38.9*, opening
   **Review**.
5. The Forms list shows **Nurse triage (form)** in the **Starts** column.

## Common mistakes

| What you see | Why, and what to do |
|---|---|
| The submission says **Received** and no run | **When submitted, start** is **Nothing: keep the submission**, or was not saved. |
| **Run not started**, with a reason under **Details** | The schedule is inactive, or a run of it is still going (it waits its turn). Read the reason. |
| The pipeline reads the wrong file | **Bucket** or **File** is filled in on the read step. Leave both empty to read the submission. |
| No notice for an abnormal entry | **People** holds a name instead of the person's number, or **Send** is `always` on an empty run. |
| `abnormal` is empty for a submission | An answer was blank or not a number, so the formula could not be worked out; the row is not kept by **Filter**. Make the fields **Required**. |
| The form cannot be filled in | Only an **Active**, published form takes submissions. |

> **Note:** Not yet verified end to end: Summit Valley's own form-started triage run (Journey 5) is still waiting to be
> run in the showcase, so the counts above are what the steps do, not a run seen there.

articles.title: Backfill last month, with the cost estimate first
articles.summary: Make a daily denials pipeline period-aware with {{run.date}}, give it one billed run, read the backfill's preview and estimate for September, start it three at a time and check the 30 runs.
articles.who: Anyone who may run the schedule starts a backfill; a workspace administrator sees the cost estimate and builds the pipeline

where.label: Build › Pipelines › Schedules & triggers › a schedule's ⋮ › Backfill…

articles.popular: Rerun a pipeline for every day of last month
articles.md:
A new daily pipeline only knows about today. A **backfill** runs its schedule once for each day of a past range, a few
at a time, and tells each run which day it is for as `{{run.date}}`. Before it starts, the backfill shows how many runs
it will make and what they should cost, worked out from the schedule's billed runs. This recipe fills September for a
daily count of claim denials.

## What you'll build

- A pipeline, **Denials by day**: **Read CSV/JSON/Parquet** (September's remittances) → **Filter** (denied, on the
  run's day) → **Aggregate** (denials per payer) → **Upload to bucket** (`rcm/denials/{{run.date}}.csv`).
- An active schedule, **Denials by day**, daily at `03:00`.
- One backfill: **1 Sep – 30 Sep 2026**, one run per **Day**, **3** at once: **30** runs and **30** files.

Summit Valley's *Denials by month (backfill a quarter)* is the worked example: backfill #1 ran 25 days of October, three
at once, 25 of 25 completed.

## What you need first

- A storage connection (its alias in **Bucket**; the examples use `summit-valley-s3`).
- The sample file [remits-2026-09.csv](/help/samples/backfill/remits-2026-09.csv): 900 synthetic remittance lines, 30 a
  day for each day of September 2026 (`claim_id`, `payer`, `status`, `paid`, `denial_reason`, `remit_date`). 98 are
  denied.
- Upload it to the folder `remits/` of your bucket (**See results › Analysis › Files**, **New folder**, **Upload**).
- To see the estimate: a workspace administrator's sign-in.

## Build it

### Make the pipeline period-aware

1. **Build › Pipelines** → **New pipeline** → **Add steps yourself**, **Name** `Denials by day`, **Create and add steps**.
2. Add **Read CSV/JSON/Parquet**: **Key** `remits`, **Bucket** your alias, **File** `remits/remits-2026-09.csv`.
3. Add **Filter**: **Key** `denied`, **Keep a row that meets** `all`, two conditions:

| Column | Is | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | `eq` | `denied` |
| `remit_date` | `eq` | `{{run.date}}` |

4. Add **Aggregate**: **Key** `by`, **Group by** `payer`, one aggregation: **Compute** `count`, **As column**
   `denials`.
5. Add **Upload to bucket**: **Key** `keep`, **Bucket** your alias, **Object key** `rcm/denials/{{run.date}}.csv`,
   **Format** `csv`.
6. **Save**.

> **Tip:** `{{run.date}}` is the day a run is for: today for an ordinary run, the period's day in a backfill. A pipeline
> that does not use it gives every period the same data. See [Placeholders](#pl-placeholders).

### Schedule it, and give it one billed run

1. **Schedules & triggers** → **New schedule**: **Schedule name** `Denials by day`, **Pipeline** `Denials by day`,
   **On a timetable**, **Daily**, every `1` day at `03` : `00`. Keep it **Active**. **Create schedule**.
2. On the list, the schedule's **⋮** → **Run now**. Today has no September rows, so the run completes with **Filter**
   `900 → 0`. It is billed like any run, and gives the estimate something to go by.
3. Wait a few minutes: usage is rolled up every few minutes.

### Read the preview, then start

1. On the list, the schedule's **⋮** → **Backfill…**.
2. **Range**: **Dates**, the range picker, **1 Sep 2026** to **30 Sep 2026**. **One run per**: **Day**.
3. **How it runs**: **At once** `3`. Leave **Run again the periods that already have a completed run** off.
4. Read the **Preview**: **30** will run, **0** already done, skipped, **30** days in all, and the 30 dates.
5. Read the **Cost estimate**: the average of the schedule's billed runs in the last 30 days, times 30 runs. Decide
   whether to go on.
6. Choose **Start: 30 days**. The backfill opens in **Run & review › Runs › Backfills**.

![The backfill panel: range, runs at once, preview and estimate](rcp-b-backfill "Backfill…: the dates, one run per day, how many at once, the parameters, the preview of 14 days and the cost estimate")

## Check it worked

1. **Runs › Backfills** shows the backfill: **2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30 · 30 days · 3 at once**, its bar filling, then
   **Completed**, **30 of 30**.
2. Its page shows the **Estimate** it started with and **Billed so far** once the runs are priced.
3. The folder `rcm/denials/` holds **30** files, `2026-09-01.csv` to `2026-09-30.csv`. Together they count all **98**
   denials.
4. `2026-09-15.csv` has **3** rows: Prairie Health Plan (fictional) **2**, Granite Mutual (fictional) **1**, Self-pay
   **1**.
5. `2026-09-12.csv` has no rows: no claim was denied that day. Its run still **Completed**.
6. The schedule's own daily run at 03:00 went on beside the backfill.

![The Backfills page](rcp-b-backfills "Runs › Backfills at Summit Valley: Denials by month, 25 of 25 completed, three at once")

## Common mistakes

| What you see | Why, and what to do |
|---|---|
| **Backfill…** is greyed out, or the preview says *The schedule is switched off* | Only an active schedule is backfilled. **Activate** it first. |
| *Nothing to estimate from* | No run of this schedule (or pipeline) was billed in the last 30 days. Run it once, wait a few minutes, open **Backfill…** again. |
| Every day's file is the same | The pipeline does not use `{{run.date}}`, so each run reads the same rows. |
| Every file is empty | The dates in the file are another format (`09/15/2026` against `2026-09-15`), or the range is not the month in the file. |
| *0 will run, 30 already done, skipped* | Those days already have a completed run. Tick **Run again the periods that already have a completed run** to redo them. |
| A backfill cannot start: too many open | A workspace runs at most 3 open backfills at a time. Wait for one to finish, or cancel one. |
| Some periods failed | Fix the cause, then **Retry failed** on the backfill: only the failed days run again. |

> **Note:** An estimate is not a price. Each run is billed for what it really uses.

> **Note:** Not yet verified end to end: this one-file version was not run at Summit Valley. Its backfill read a folder
> per day (`remits/daily/{{run.date}}/`) instead, and its daily progress pipeline filters on `{{run.date}}` the same
> way as step 3; both backfills completed.

articles.title: Teams with a lead, and a pipeline's results reviewed by a team
articles.summary: Make the Physicians, Senior physicians and Radiology teams with their leads, then hold an imaging worklist pipeline's results until someone in Radiology approves them, one run at a time.
articles.who: A workspace administrator makes teams, names leads and sets the pipeline's review; the team's members decide
articles.popular: Have a team review a pipeline's results
articles.md:
A **team** lets work go to whoever in it is free. A pipeline's **review** holds each run's results until a person
approves them: the run completes, but reads **Completed · waiting for review** until then. Point the review at a team
and every member sees the task; with **Requires individual review**, each run must be opened and decided on its own,
never in bulk.

## What you'll build

- Three teams: **Physicians** (lead Dr. Anika Patel, members Dr. Minh Nguyen and Dr. Chidi Okafor), **Senior
  physicians** (lead Dr. Chidi Okafor) and **Radiology** (lead Dr. Lena Schmidt). The other recipes use them too.
- A pipeline, **Imaging worklist**, whose results wait for **Radiology**, one run at a time.
- One run, approved by Dr. Schmidt, its status **Completed · approved**.

Summit Valley's *Journey 8 · Chest X-ray triage with radiologist review* is reviewed the same way by its Radiology team;
its review settings are the figure.

## What you need first

- The people, added under **Administration › Users** (see [Add a person](#adm-people)). The list, with fictional
  addresses: [people-and-teams.csv](/help/samples/team-run-review/people-and-teams.csv).
- The sample [imaging-worklist.csv](/help/samples/team-run-review/imaging-worklist.csv): 12 synthetic imaging studies
  (`study_id`, `mrn`, `modality`, `urgency`, `ordered_at`), 3 of them `urgent`. Upload it to the folder `imaging/` of
  your bucket (**See results › Analysis › Files**).

## Build it

### Make the teams

1. Open **Administration › Teams** and choose **New team**. **Name** `Physicians`, **Description** `Attending
   physicians`. **Make team**.
2. In the team's panel, under **Add a person**, choose Dr. Anika Patel, **As** **Lead**, **Add**. Then Dr. Minh Nguyen and
   Dr. Chidi Okafor, each **As** **Member**.
3. **New team** `Senior physicians`: Dr. Chidi Okafor as **Lead**.
4. **New team** `Radiology`: Dr. Lena Schmidt as **Lead**.
5. The tiles now count **3** teams, **4** people in teams and **3** leads.

![A team's panel](rcp-b-teams "The team's panel: about, members with Member or Lead, Add a person, and where the team is used")

A lead adds and removes the team's members from then on; only an administrator names leads, renames or archives a team.

### Find the team's number

The review below names the team by its number. Open **Administration › Users**, open Dr. Lena Schmidt, and under
**Teams** click **Radiology**: the Teams page opens with an address ending `?team=14` (your number differs). Note it.

### The pipeline

1. **Build › Pipelines** → **New pipeline** → **Add steps yourself**, **Name** `Imaging worklist`, **Create and add
   steps**.
2. **Read CSV/JSON/Parquet**: **Key** `list`, **Bucket** your alias, **File** `imaging/imaging-worklist.csv`.
3. **Compute**: **Key** `first`, **Column** `review_first`, **Formula** `if(urgency == 'urgent', true, false)`.
4. **Sort**: **Key** `ordered`, **Sort by** `review_first` `desc`, then `ordered_at` `asc`.
5. **Upload to bucket**: **Key** `keep`, **Object key** `imaging/worklist/{{date}}-{{run}}.csv`, **Format** `csv`.
6. Open the **Settings** tab, section **Review**. Under **Results need review by** tick **Our team**; under
   **Individual review** tick **Requires individual review (never approved or rejected in bulk)**.
7. Open the **YAML** tab. At the end, under `settings:`, the review reads `review:` with `required: [internal]` and
   `individual: true`. Add the two `reviewers` lines, with your team's number:

```The review in the YAML tab
  review:
    required:
    - internal
    reviewers:
      kind: team
      value: '14'
    individual: true
```

8. **Validate**, then **Save**. A team number that is not one of your workspace's active teams is refused.

![A pipeline whose results wait for its team](rcp-b-review-settings "Settings › Review: Our team, and Requires individual review")

> **Tip:** Who is asked, the reminders and the due time for every run review are set once, in **Build › Approval
> workflows › Pipeline run review**. Its approver, *The reviewers named on the request*, is the team you named here.

## Check it worked

1. **Run now** on the pipeline. The run's steps read `0 → 12`, `12 → 12`, `12 → 12`, `12 → 12`, the 3 urgent studies
   first in the file, and its status reads **Completed · waiting for review**.
2. Sign in as Dr. Lena Schmidt. **Review › Approvals** → **My teams** has one task about the run. Open it: **What to
   review** shows the run's first fields and **Open the run**.
3. Choose **Approve**, with a note under **What you checked**, for example `Urgent studies first: checked`.
4. The run's status becomes **Completed · approved**; the task moves to **Done**, under her name.
5. Dr. Minh Nguyen, who is not in Radiology, has no task for it.
6. Start a second run and try to approve it with others in bulk: it is skipped: *Its pipeline requires individual
   review: decide this run on its own.*

## Common mistakes

| What you see | Why, and what to do |
|---|---|
| The task goes to the administrators | No `reviewers` in the YAML, or the team has no members: the review falls back to the administrators. |
| *That team is not in this workspace.* when you save | The number is not an active team of this workspace. Check it from the person's page again. |
| A team with **No lead** | Nobody was added **As** **Lead**: only administrators can then change its members. |
| The lead cannot rename the team | By design: leads change members; administrators name leads, rename and archive. |
| You cannot approve the run | You started it. No one decides their own request: someone else in the team decides. |
| A failed run has no review | Only a completed run has results to decide. |

> **Note:** Not yet verified end to end at Summit Valley: its teams were made without leads (every team there shows
> **No lead**), and the X-ray run's review is waiting to be run in the showcase.

articles.title: An approval workflow with a condition, a deadline, escalation and a stand-in
articles.summary: A care-plan sign-off where the attending physician approves within 4 hours (or it escalates to the team), a High risk adds the senior team, and a colleague can decide on the physician's behalf.
articles.who: A workspace administrator designs and publishes the workflow; the people it names decide; anyone who may start it makes a request
articles.popular: Add a second approval only when the risk is high
articles.md:
An approval workflow says who decides, by when, and what happens next. This one is small enough to build in ten
minutes and shows the four things most workflows need: a **deadline** with a reminder, **escalation** when nobody
decides in time, a **condition** that adds a second approval only when it matters, and decisions made **on behalf of**
someone who is away.

## What you'll build

A workflow, **Care plan sign-off** (key `care-plan-signoff`), with four steps:

1. **Approval** *Attending physician approves*: Dr. Anika Patel, due in **4** hours, a reminder **2** hours before,
   overdue to the **Physicians** team.
2. **Condition** *High risk?*: `risk` is `High` → step 3; otherwise step 4.
3. **Approval** *Senior physician approves*: the **Senior physicians** team, due in **8** hours.
4. **Notify** *Tell the requester*.

And two requests that take the two branches. Summit Valley's *Patient journey* has the same attending approval and
condition (on the care plan's own risk); its steps and a request's history are the figures.

## What you need first

- The teams **Physicians** (Dr. Anika Patel, Dr. Minh Nguyen, Dr. Chidi Okafor) and **Senior physicians** (Dr. Chidi
  Okafor): see [Make the teams](#rcp-team-run-review).
- Someone to start the requests who is not one of the approvers (the workspace administrator): no one approves their
  own request.
- The two test requests, with what each should do: [test-requests.csv](/help/samples/approval-condition/test-requests.csv).

## Build it

### The workflow

1. Open **Build › Approval workflows** and choose **New workflow**.
2. **Name** `Care plan sign-off`, **Key** `care-plan-signoff` (it cannot change later), **What it approves** `care plan`,
   **Description** `The attending physician signs off a care plan; a senior physician too when the risk is High.`
   **Create and design**.
3. **Add a step** → **Approval**. Set:

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| **Name** / **Key** | `Attending physician approves` / `attending` |
| **Who approves** | **A person**, Dr. Anika Patel |
| **Due in (hours)** | `4` |
| **Remind before (hours)** | `2` |
| **When overdue, it goes to** | **Everyone in a team**, Physicians |
| **A rejection needs a reason** | ticked |
| **If rejected** | **The request ends, rejected** |

4. **Add after** → **Condition**: **Name** `High risk?`, **Key** `high-risk`, **Field of the request** `risk`, **Test** **is**, **Value**
   `High`. Leave its branches for now.
5. **Add after** → **Approval**: **Name** `Senior physician approves`, **Key** `senior`, **Who approves** **Everyone in a team**, Senior
   physicians, **Due in (hours)** `8`, **A rejection needs a reason** ticked.
6. **Add after** → **Notify**: **Name** `Tell the requester`, **Key** `tell-requester`, **Tell** **The requester**, **Message**
   `The care plan for {{mrn}} is signed off.`
7. Select the condition again: **If yes, go to** *Senior physician approves*, **If no, go to** *Tell the requester*.
8. On *Tell the requester* (the last step), leave **If the request ends here, it ends as** at **As its latest approval
   went**.
9. Choose **Publish version 1**, with **What changed** `First version`.

![An approval step with a deadline and escalation](rcp-b-approval-step "Summit Valley's Patient journey: the attending physician's approval, a person, due in 4 hours, reminded 2 hours before, overdue to the Physicians team")

![The condition that adds the senior approval](rcp-b-condition "The condition: careplan.risk is High; yes to the senior physician, no to the medication check")

### Cover for someone who is away

An **out of office** lets a stand-in act on the tasks assigned to someone, for at most 90 days; every decision then
records both people. Dr. Patel names Dr. Minh Nguyen for the days she is away (she sets her own; an administrator may
set it for her). See [Out of office](#adm-out-of-office) for the rules.

> **Note:** There is no console page for setting an out of office yet; Summit Valley's was set by Dr. Patel through the
> platform. Until there is one, hand a single task over with **Pass on**: in **Review › Approvals**, open the task,
> choose **Pass on**, pick Dr. Nguyen under **Pass it to**, and choose **Pass on**. The history then says it was passed
> on, not decided for her.

## Check it worked

Start the two requests as the administrator: **Review › Approvals** → **My requests** → **New request**, **Workflow**
**Care plan sign-off**, and under **What it is about** **Add a field** for each value:

| Title | Fields |
|---|---|
| `Care plan · SV-000117` | `mrn` = `SV-000117`, `risk` = `High` |
| `Care plan · SV-000124` | `mrn` = `SV-000124`, `risk` = `Low` |

Choose **Start the request** for each. Then:

1. Dr. Patel (or Dr. Nguyen standing in) has two tasks in **Review › Approvals** → **Waiting for me**, each *due* 4 hours
   after it opened.
2. Approve **SV-000124**: its history says *high-risk: no* (conditions show by their key), then the notify step, and the request ends **Approved**.
   Nobody in Senior physicians is asked.
3. Approve **SV-000117**: *high-risk: yes*, and a task appears for Senior physicians under **My teams** for Dr. Okafor.
   When he approves, the request ends **Approved**, and you are told *The care plan for SV-000117 is signed off.*
4. Leave a third request undecided: 2 hours before it is due a reminder goes to Dr. Patel, and after 4 hours its history
   says *overdue, escalated to* the Physicians team, whose members now see it under **My teams**.
5. A decision made by a stand-in reads, in the request's **History**:

```A request's history
Attending physician approves: approved by Dr. Minh Nguyen (for Dr. Anika Patel)
```

![A decision made on someone's behalf](rcp-b-on-behalf "My requests at Summit Valley: Elena Marsh's journey, approved by Dr. Minh Nguyen (for Dr. Anika Patel), then high-risk: yes")

## Common mistakes

| What you see | Why, and what to do |
|---|---|
| The senior approval is never asked | The field name or value does not match: the condition reads `risk`, the request has `Risk`, or `high` against `High`. Type them exactly. |
| Every request asks the senior team | **If no, go to** still points to the senior approval. Set it to *Tell the requester*. |
| *went to the administrators* in the history | The approver is the requester, or the team has nobody who can decide. No one approves their own request. |
| Nothing escalates | **Due in (hours)** is empty: no deadline, no reminder, no escalation. |
| A request still uses the old steps | It started on the earlier version. Requests keep the version they started on; new ones take the latest published. |
| The change has no effect | It is still a draft: choose **Publish version N**. |
| Dr. Nguyen sees nothing while Dr. Patel is away | No out of office covers those dates (it does not chain, and it ends when cancelled). Use **Pass on** for the task. |

> **Note:** Not yet verified end to end: *Care plan sign-off* itself was not run at Summit Valley. Its pieces were, in the
> *Patient journey* (request 2051): the 4-hour attending approval decided by Dr. Nguyen for Dr. Patel, the condition on
> a High risk, and the senior physician's approval. The reminder and escalation were not seen there, because every task
> was decided in time.

articles.title: Report Studio at a glance
articles.summary: What Report Studio makes, its six tabs, who may do what, and the path from a template to a signed PDF.
articles.who: Anyone whose page access includes Reports overview; each tab needs its own page (see the table below)
articles.popular: Make your first signed report
articles.md:
Report Studio turns your data into finished, branded reports: a discharge summary for one patient, a monthly medication
safety report for a pharmacy, a statement for each guarantor. You design a **template** once, fill it with data from a
pipeline's run, a file or a sample, and every time you generate it you get a new **version** with its PDF and HTML.
Nothing is overwritten. A person approves a version, and the approval signs the PDF digitally in their name, so anyone
can check later who approved it and that it has not changed since.

In the menu it is **See results › Reports**.

![The Reports overview](rs-overview "Reports › Overview: this month's versions, templates waiting to be published, recent reports and generation jobs")

## The workflow
1. **Brand it once.** Upload your logo, letterhead, signatures and stamps in **Assets & branding**, and make a brand
   profile so every report has the same header, footer, colours and logo. See [Branding and assets](#rs-branding).
2. **Make a template.** Start from a starter or your own on **Templates**, lay it out in the designer and try it with
   test data. See [Templates and the library](#rs-templates) and [The designer](#rs-designer).
3. **Publish it.** A published version never changes; reports always record the exact version they were made from.
4. **Generate.** By hand with **New report** ([Create a report](#rs-create)), or on every run of a pipeline with a
   **Generate report** step ([Reports from a pipeline](#rs-pipeline)).
5. **Approve and sign.** Someone allowed to approve, who did not generate that version, chooses **Approve and sign**.
   See [Approve, sign and verify](#rs-approve).
6. **Share, verify, keep.** Download the PDF, check its signature with **Verify signature**, and let the workspace's
   retention rules decide how long older versions stay ([Retention and page limits](#rs-limits)).

## The six tabs

| Tab | What it is for |
|---|---|
| **Overview** | Versions made this month, published templates, how many generated without a problem, what needs attention; recent reports, generation jobs, connected pipelines and template activity |
| **Templates** | Every template of the workspace and the starters: make, copy, import, publish, archive |
| **Library** | Every report and its versions, and the generation jobs; **From pipelines** lists the files pipelines made |
| **Data** | Browse what a report can read: pipeline outputs, storage buckets, uploads; see a schema and the first rows |
| **Assets & branding** | Logos, images, letterheads, signatures and stamps; brand profiles |
| **Settings** | Who approves reports and publishes templates, two approvals, retention preview, the page limit (workspace administrators) |

## Who may do what
Each part of Report Studio is a page in page access (**Administration › Page access**), so an administrator can give a
reviewer the Library and approval without letting them change templates.

| Page in page access | Lets a person |
|---|---|
| **Reports overview** | open Report Studio and its Overview |
| **Report templates** | make and edit templates and drafts |
| **Publish report templates** | publish a draft (or decide a request to publish one) |
| **Report data** | browse and upload report data on the Data tab |
| **Generate reports** | create reports and generate new versions |
| **Reports** | read the Library and download reports |
| **Report assets and branding** | upload logos and images, edit brand profiles |
| **Upload signatures and stamps** | upload, replace and retire signatures and stamps |
| **Approve and sign reports** | approve report versions (signing them) and approve signatures and stamps |

Workspace administrators have all of them. **Settings** is for workspace administrators only.

> **Note:** Whoever generated a version never approves it, and whoever uploaded a signature or stamp never approves it.
> Give the workspace at least two people who may approve.

## Example
At Summit Valley Health System (a fictional hospital group), the admission pipeline's last step makes Elena Marsh's
**Discharge summary** from the care team's approved draft. Dr. Minh Nguyen, standing in for Dr. Anika Patel, chooses
**Approve and sign**; the PDF now carries his digital signature, the records stamp and a QR code that opens the
report's page for anyone signed in to check it.

articles.title: Templates and the library
articles.summary: Find, start, copy, import, publish and archive templates; drafts and versions; the starters.
articles.who: Anyone with Report templates; publishing needs Publish report templates
articles.popular: Start a template from a starter
articles.md:
A **template** is a report's design: its layout, the data fields it reads and how it looks. It has **versions**. You
change a **draft**; when it is right you **publish** it as the next version, and that version never changes again.
Reports pin the exact version they were made from, so a report made in March still reads as it did in March after the
template has moved on.

![The Templates tab](rs-templates "Reports › Templates: the workspace's templates and the starters, as cards or a table")

## Find a template
1. Open **Reports › Templates**.
2. Narrow the list with the tabs **All**, **This workspace**, **Starters** and **Shared with me**, the search (name,
   description or tag), **All categories**, **All states** (Published, Never published, With a draft) and **Anyone**
   (Made by me, From a starter, Copies and imports). Tick **Archived** to see archived templates too.
3. Switch between **Cards** (a thumbnail of the first page) and **Table** (category, versions, origin, pages, updated).

## Start a template
- **From a starter.** On a starter card choose **Use starter**: it is copied into your workspace as a new template with a
  draft, ready to change. Starters are kept by the platform and labelled **Report Studio starter**.
- **From nothing.** Choose **New template**, give it a name, and the designer opens on an empty draft.
- **From another template.** In a template's menu (⋮) or on its page choose **Make a copy (new template)**.
- **From a file.** **Import JSON** reads a template another workspace exported with **Export JSON**.

## A template's page
Click a template's name to open its page. It shows the current published version or draft, **Test with data**, **Create
report**, its **Versions** (each with **Test** and **Copy**), its **Test samples** and **Data it needs**: the template's
data contract, every field it reads with its type and whether it is required.

![A template's page](rs-template-page "A template's page: versions, test samples and the data the template needs")

- **Edit draft** (or **New draft from vN**) opens the designer.
- **Discard the draft** throws the unpublished changes away; the published versions stay.
- **Archive** takes the template out of the lists and keeps it; reports made from it are not touched.
- **Delete template** is offered only for a template no report was ever made from.

## Publish
In the designer, **Publish vN** turns the draft into version N. If you may not publish, **Ask for approval** sends the
draft to the people who publish templates, in their **Review › Approvals**: they publish it there, or send it back
saying why. A workspace administrator decides who publishes, and whether **Publishing needs a second person**, in
**Reports › Settings** ([Approve, sign and verify](#rs-approve--who-approves)).

> **Tip:** Keep the test data you checked a template with: on its page or in the designer's test data, choose
> **Keep as a test sample**. The next person who changes the template tests it against the same data.

## Limits
| What | Limit |
|---|---|
| Components in one template | 500 |
| Items a **Repeat for each** lays out | 1,000 |
| Text in one text block | 10,000 characters |
| Published versions | as many as you publish; none is ever changed |

articles.title: Lay out a template in the designer
articles.summary: Components, layers and data fields; page settings, watermark, letterhead; undo, autosave and checks.
articles.who: Anyone with Report templates (editing a draft); publishing needs Publish report templates
articles.popular: Lay out a report template
articles.md:
The designer is where a template's draft is laid out: the components on the left, the page in the middle, the settings
of what you selected on the right. It draws the page as the PDF will print it, filled with your test data as you go.

![The designer](rs-designer "The designer: Components, Layers and Data on the left, the page with its ruler, Page settings on the right")

## Open it
1. In **Reports › Templates**, choose **Edit draft** on a template, or **New draft from vN** on a published one (a
   published version is never edited: your changes go into a new draft).
2. The header shows the template's name, **Draft vN** or **Published vN**, and whether your changes are saved
   (**Saving…**, **All changes saved**, **Unsaved changes**). The draft saves itself as you work.
3. **Preview** draws the whole report as a PDF with the test data; **Validate** runs the checks.

## Add and arrange components
1. On the **Components** tab, drag a component onto the page, or click it to add it after the selected block. **Find a
   component** searches the list. The groups are **Text**, **Data**, **Metadata**, **Layout**, **Media** and
   **Approval**; [Components](#rs-components) describes each one.
2. **Page parts** adds a **Header** or **Footer** (printed on every page) and a **Page break**. **Pages** lists the
   pages, with their first heading; click one to jump to it.
3. Click a block on the page to select it. Its settings open on the right, grouped as content, data, format, style and
   layout. A selected block has a handle: drag it to move the block.
4. The **Layers** tab shows every block as a tree. Drag to reorder; the arrow keys select the block above or below, and
   **Alt** + an arrow moves it.
5. **Undo** (Ctrl+Z) and **Redo** (Ctrl+Y) are in the toolbar, beside the zoom (50 % to 200 %), **Fit** and full screen.

## Bind data
A component shows data through a **binding**: a path into the report's data, such as `primary.patient.name` or a list
such as `primary.labs`. The **Data** tab lists the test data's fields with their types: click one to use it in the
selected block. A field that holds pictures shows **Show as image**, which adds an **Image from data** (or an **Image
grid** for a list).

> **Tip:** Add test data first ([Data and test samples](#rs-data)). The page then fills with real-looking values and the
> checks tell you about a binding that reads nothing.

## Page settings
Click **Page settings** in the toolbar (or click outside every block) to set the whole report:

- **Page**: **Size** (A4, A3, A5, Letter, Legal), **Orientation**, and the four margins in millimetres (16 by default).
- **Type and colour**: **Font** (Noto Sans, Noto Serif, Noto Sans Mono, DejaVu Sans), **Text size** (9 to 12 pt) and the
  **Main colour**.
- **Watermark**: **DRAFT**, **COPY**, **CONFIDENTIAL**, **VOID**, **SAMPLE** or **Own words…** (up to 40 characters), its
  strength, angle, pages, layer and colour, and **Only when** a condition holds (for example `isReprint = true`).
- **Page background**: a soft **Tint** on every page or the first, and a **Letterhead** from your approved assets.
- **Every download after the first says COPY**.
- **Brand** (in the toolbar): the workspace default, a brand profile, or **No branding**.

> **Note:** Previews always say DRAFT across the page, so a preview is never mistaken for the real report.

## Checks and publishing
The bar at the bottom reads **Template structure valid** (or **Template has errors**), how many problems the bindings
have with the test data, and how many data fields the template uses. Click it to see the **Checks**. A draft with
structure errors cannot be published. When it is right, choose **Publish vN**, or **Ask for approval** if someone else
publishes ([Templates and the library](#rs-templates--publish)).

If someone else saved the same draft while you had it open, the designer says so and offers **Reload** or **Save as a
copy**: nothing of yours is lost.

## Example
Summit Valley's **Patient health chart** has a heading bound to the patient's name, a row of **Metric** tiles (records,
lab results, vital readings), a **Chart** of SpO2 and heart rate, a **Table** of labs, an **Image grid** of imaging and
wound photos, and sections for medicines and the care plan, on Letter pages in the Summit Valley standard brand.

articles.title: The AI designer
articles.summary: Draft a template from words, suggest mappings and charts, explain the checks, write a paragraph; accept or dismiss.
articles.who: Anyone who may edit the template's draft; the workspace needs an active model connection
articles.md:
In a draft's designer, the right-hand pane has an **AI assistant** that proposes changes to the template. It never
saves, publishes or sends anything itself: every proposal is shown first, as a list of changes and on the page, and
is applied only when you choose **Accept**. **Undo** takes an accepted change back.

![The AI assistant in the designer](rs-ai-panel "The AI assistant: its five actions, the words you give it and a proposal to accept or dismiss")

## What it can do

| Action | What you get |
|---|---|
| **Draft the template** | Describe the report in plain words (its sections, values, tables and charts); the draft replaces the page body, the header and footer stay |
| **Suggest mappings** | For each field the template reads that the test data does not have, the data's matching field, with how sure the AI is |
| **Suggest charts** | One to three charts chosen by the test data's field types, added before the footer |
| **Explain the checks** | The checks' problems in plain words, with a fix to apply where one reads a field the data has |
| **Write a paragraph** | A short paragraph of the data's own values, placed after the selected block and labelled "Drafted with AI" |

## Use it
1. Open the draft in the designer and add test data ([Data and test samples](#rs-data)); mappings and charts need it.
2. In **AI assistant**, choose an action, write what you want **In plain words** where it asks, and choose the action's
   button. A local model can take a minute; **Stop waiting** gives up.
3. Read the proposal: what is **Added**, **Changed** and **Removed**, the mappings with how sure each is (hover a row
   for why), and the notes from the checks. **Show on the page** draws it on the page with the new blocks outlined;
   nothing in the draft changes yet.
4. Choose **Accept** to apply it (it is saved at once), or **Dismiss**. **Earlier proposals** keeps the list.

> **Privacy:** Only the test data's field names and types are sent to the model, unless you tick **Include sample
> values** (at most 20 records, identifying values masked) for **Write a paragraph**. The proposal says what was sent
> and which model answered. Which models may see which data is set in **Administration › Data policies**
> ([Which models may see which data](#ai-data-levels)).

> **Warning:** A proposal is refused once the draft was saved after it was made ("The draft was saved since this was
> proposed"): ask again. A paragraph states only the data's own values; read it before you publish, as you would any
> text.

## Good to know
- The assistant uses the workspace's model connection; when none is active the pane says **Not available here now**.
- Its calls count as AI usage in **Billing › Cost & usage** ([What AI costs](#ai-costs)).
- It is offered on drafts only: a published version opens read only.

articles.title: Data and test samples
articles.summary: What a report can read — a pipeline's output, a step's own input, a bucket file, an upload, several files — and test samples.
articles.who: Report data to browse and upload on the Data tab; anyone editing a template may add test data
articles.md:
A report is a template filled with data. The data is one JSON document (or a CSV, read as rows); the template's
bindings are paths into it. You choose the data twice: while designing (the **test data**, so the page fills as you
work) and when you generate (the real data, matched to the template's fields).

## Where data can come from

| Source | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Pipeline run** | An output a pipeline's run kept: pick the schedule, the run and the output. **Use a newer run** jumps to the latest |
| **This step's input** | In a pipeline's own report design: the rows the Generate report step read in a recent run |
| **Bucket file** | A JSON or CSV file in one of your storage buckets, read only |
| **Uploads** | A JSON or CSV file uploaded on **Reports › Data** (with the Report data page) |
| **Paste JSON** | Text you paste; read at once and never stored unless you keep it as a test sample. **It is CSV** reads a header row and rows |
| **Samples** | Test samples kept with the template |
| **Several files** | Up to 8 files side by side in one document, each under a name you give (`summary`, `details`); the report reads `$.summary`, `$.details[0]` |

Everything is read **as you**: a run, bucket or file you cannot open elsewhere in the console is refused here too.

## Browse data on the Data tab
1. Open **Reports › Data**. The three cards say what you may read: **Pipeline outputs**, **Storage buckets** and
   **Documents and uploads**.
2. In **Sources**, pick a run (**Pipeline schedule**, then **Inspect**), a bucket file or an upload.
3. The right side shows the **Schema** (each field, its type, whether it can be empty), the **Sample rows** (up to
   100) and which templates can read it. **Report data starts at** sets the starting point in the JSON: paths below are
   relative to it.
4. **Upload a file** (JSON or CSV) keeps a file for reports; **Keep in Sources** keeps a run's output to find again.

![The Data tab](rs-data "Reports › Data: what you may read, a source's schema and its first rows")

> **Note:** Browsing here never changes a report or a pipeline. To change the data, change the pipeline and run it
> again.

## Add test data to a template
1. In the designer, choose the test-data button in the toolbar (or **Add test data** on the **Data** tab).
2. Pick a source as above; the page fills at once. The **Data** tab then lists the fields to click and bind.
3. To keep it, choose **Keep as a test sample**: it is saved with the template, so whoever changes it next tests against
   the same data. A template's page lists its **Test samples**.

## A pipeline step's own input
When a **Generate report** step designs its report in the step (**Design the report here**), the designer opens on the
rows that step read in the pipeline's latest run (**This step's input**). A copy is frozen with the design: the first
500 rows, sensitive columns masked. If the run has expired, pick a newer run or paste sample JSON.

## Limits
| What | Limit |
|---|---|
| Pasted data | 5 MB |
| Several files | 8 files, each at most 2,000 rows |
| Sample rows shown on the Data tab | 100 |
| A step's frozen input | the first 500 rows, sensitive columns masked |

> **Privacy:** Use synthetic or de-identified data for test samples: a sample is kept with the template and anyone who
> may edit the template sees it.

articles.title: Branding and assets
articles.summary: Logos, images and letterheads; signatures and stamps with their custodian, approval and grants; brand profiles.
articles.who: Report assets and branding for logos, images and brand profiles; Upload signatures and stamps for those; approving needs Approve and sign reports
articles.popular: Upload a signature and get it approved
articles.md:
**Assets & branding** holds the pictures reports use and the brand profiles that make every report look the same. It
has three tabs: **Assets**, **Brand profiles** and **Signatures and stamps**.

![Assets & branding](rs-assets "Reports › Assets & branding: approved logos, a letterhead, a signature and a stamp, and the workspace's default brand profile")

## Upload a logo, image or letterhead
1. Open **Reports › Assets & branding** and choose **Upload asset**.
2. Choose the **Kind**, give it a **Name** (and optionally a title, description and category) and pick the **File**: SVG,
   PNG or JPG, up to 10 MB. Each picture is checked by its content and re-encoded; an SVG is drawn into a PNG first.
3. A logo or image can be used at once; a new upload of it is a new version, and old reports keep the version they used.

## Signatures and stamps
A signature has two parts. The **picture** is only how it looks on the page. The **digital signature** is added to the
PDF when its owner approves a report: it records who approved and when, and any later change to the file breaks it.

1. A person with **Upload signatures and stamps** (the custodian) uploads it, choosing the **Kind** Signature or Stamp.
   A signature names who it **Belongs to**.
2. It **waits for an approver**, who is never the person who uploaded it. The approver decides it on the asset's page
   (**Approve vN** or **Reject vN**) or in **Review › Approvals**.
3. Only the person a signature belongs to, or someone they grant it to (**Grant use to…** on the asset's page), may place
   it on a template. A stamp needs a grant too.
4. On the asset's page, **Placement on a template** adds it to a template's draft: choose the template, the position
   (**Last page · end** or **Before the footer · movable**), the width and alignment, and an optional stamp beside it,
   then **Add to the template's draft**.

![A signature's page](rs-asset-signature "A signature's page: its approved version, where it is used, who may place it, and its digital signature")

> **Warning:** A signature picture is not a signature. Only an approval signs the PDF. Never let the picture stand for
> an approval that did not happen.

## Replace and retire
- **Upload new version** replaces a picture. For a signature or stamp the new version needs approval; the current one
  stays in use until then.
- **Retire** stops new use; old reports and their history stay. The asset's page shows where it is used first.
- **Delete** is offered only for an asset nothing ever used.

## Brand profiles
A brand profile is the optional defaults every report can share: **Logo**, **Heading font** and **Body font**, the
colours, **Organisation name**, **Contact email**, **Website**, **Phone**, the **Header**, **Footer** and
**Confidentiality line** (they may name `{{report.period}}`, `{{contact.email}}` and `{{website}}`), the approved
signatures and stamps templates may choose from, and **Digitally sign PDFs when approved**.

1. Choose **New brand profile**, fill in what you want (every field is optional; an empty one inherits), watch the **Live
   preview**, and **Save draft**.
2. **Publish vN** (publishing a profile needs an approver), then **Make the workspace default**.
3. New versions apply to future reports only.

**Which setting wins**, highest first: an allowed override on a single report, the template's setting, the brand
profile, the workspace default, the platform default. The confidentiality line, signatures and stamps are fixed to
approved settings.

> **Tip:** The colours are checked for contrast: the page says when text and background pass WCAG AA.

## Example
Summit Valley's custodian (the workspace administrator) uploaded **Dr. Anika Patel signature** and the **Summit Valley
Medical Center · Clinical records** stamp; Jordan Reyes, the second administrator, approved them. The **Summit Valley
standard** profile is the workspace default, with the logo, the letterhead, the teal main colour and "Confidential:
synthetic demonstration data · {{report.period}}" as the confidentiality line.

articles.title: Charts, tables, QR codes and other components
articles.summary: Every component the designer offers, with what it shows and its limits — tables, charts, metrics, images, conditions, repeats, QR codes.
articles.who: Anyone who may edit the template's draft
articles.popular: Add a chart to a report
articles.md:
Components are the blocks a template is made of. Each reads data through its **binding** (a path such as
`primary.labs`) and has its own settings on the right of the designer.

## Text

| Component | What it shows |
|---|---|
| **Heading** | A title, level 1 to 3, typed or bound to a field |
| **Text** | Paragraphs with `{{data.paths}}` filled in; simple Markdown (bold, italic, bullets); up to 10,000 characters |
| **Label and value** | A label and one bound value, formatted (currency, number, date …) |
| **List** | Bullets from a list in the data, or typed items, one per line |

## Data

| Component | What it shows |
|---|---|
| **Table** | The rows of a list in the data; columns with labels and formats; **Show only rows where** filters them; a long table goes on page after page, repeating its header |
| **Chart** | Bar, horizontal bar, stacked, line, area, pie, doughnut or scatter from a list in the data; a target line, value labels and a legend; drawn as vectors, the same in the HTML and the PDF |
| **Metric** | A KPI tile: the value, its change against a previous value or a target (up or down, good or bad), thresholds and a sparkline |

To make a chart: add **Chart**, bind it to a list (for example `primary.vitals`), set the category field (the time or
the name along the axis) and one or more series fields, and pick the chart type.

![A chart's settings](rs-chart "A Chart component selected: its list, category and series fields on the right")

## Media and approval

| Component | What it shows |
|---|---|
| **Image or logo** | An approved logo or image from Assets & branding; the template pins its version |
| **Image from data** | The picture a field names (a bucket file or a run's file), read as the person generating, re-encoded to its printed size; when it is missing, a placeholder or nothing |
| **Image grid** | A picture per item of a list, 1 to 6 to a row, with a caption; rows never split across pages |
| **Signature** | An approved signature picture, placed only by its owner or with their grant ([Branding and assets](#rs-branding--signatures-and-stamps)) |
| **Stamp** | An approved stamp picture (needs a grant) |

## Layout

| Component | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Section** | Groups blocks under an optional title |
| **Row and columns** | Side-by-side columns, a quarter to the whole width |
| **Show only when** | Shows its blocks only when a condition on the data holds (a value above a threshold, a flag set); the designer shows why a block is hidden |
| **Repeat for each** | Its blocks once for each item of a list (at most 1,000), bound as `item.field` |
| **Divider**, **Spacer** | A rule, vertical space |
| **Header**, **Footer**, **Page break** | Printed on every page; a new page in the PDF |

## Metadata and the QR code

| Component | What it shows |
|---|---|
| **QR code** | **Verify this report** (this version's page in the console; whoever scans it must be signed in to the workspace), the report id, a short value from the data, or fixed text; sharp at any size |
| **Page number**, **Generated at**, **Report id**, **Template version**, **Data source**, **Generated by**, **Confidentiality** | Facts of the report itself: "Generated at" is in the workspace's time zone, on a 24-hour clock; "Report id" reads like RPT-0048 · v1 |

> **Tip:** Put a **QR code** set to verify this report in the footer of anything you sign: a reader scans it and lands
> on the version's page, where **Verify signature** checks their copy ([Approve, sign and verify](#rs-approve--verify-a-signed-pdf)).

## Limits
| What | Limit |
|---|---|
| Components in one template | 500 |
| Items in a **Repeat for each** | 1,000 |
| Rows a preview prints in one table | 200 (the real report prints them all, within the page limit) |
| A picture embedded in a template | 512 KB and 4,096 pixels a side |
| An uploaded asset | 10 MB |

articles.title: Create a report in the console
articles.summary: The four steps of New report — template, data and mapping, preview and checks, generate — and generating again.
articles.who: Anyone with Generate reports
articles.popular: Create a report from a pipeline run
articles.md:
**New report** makes a report by hand from a published template and the data you pick. It has four steps, shown at
the top: **Template**, **Data and mapping**, **Preview and check** and **Generate**.

## 1. Template
1. Choose **New report** (on the Overview or the Library), or **Create report** on a template.
2. Pick a published template. Only published versions make reports; they never change. Give the report a **Report name**.

## 2. Data and mapping
1. Under **Data source**, pick where the data comes from: a **Pipeline run**, a **Bucket file**, **Uploads**,
   **Paste JSON**, **Samples** or **Several files** ([Data and test samples](#rs-data)). **What the source holds** shows a
   **Sample**, the **Schema** and the **JSON**.
2. Under **Match template fields**, each field the template reads has a **Source field**. Every required field needs
   one; nothing is guessed. The status reads **Matched**, **Missing** or **Optional**, and the count says how many of
   them are matched.
3. Choose **Preview and check** (or **Preview with problems** to see what goes wrong).

![Data and mapping](rs-new-mapping "Create a report, Data and mapping: the data source on the left, the template's fields matched on the right")

> **Warning:** A required field the data does not have is never filled in for you. Add it to the pipeline's output and
> run the pipeline again, or match the field the data names differently.

## 3. Preview and check
The **Preview** shows the pages ("Not generated"; "—" marks a missing value; a preview prints at most 200 rows a
table). The **Checks** say how many are **blocking**, how many are warnings and how many passed. Warnings don't block;
fix a blocking problem with **Fix the data mapping →**.

On the right:

- **Branding**: the brand profile (the template's, the workspace default, or another published one), and whether its
  approval will sign the PDF.
- **Outputs**: **PDF** (print-ready) and **HTML** (opens in any browser, self-contained); **Why (optional)**, a note kept
  with the version; **Mark this version as COPY** (COPY on every page).
- **Generate vN** makes the version. The template version and the data are recorded with it.

## 4. Generate
The job shows its progress. When it finishes, **Open the report**: version N is ready and earlier versions are kept.
If it fails, no version is made and the message says why; **Back to mapping** to fix it.

## Generate again
On a report's page, **Generate again** makes the next version: pick the **Template version** and the **Data** (the
frozen data of the current version, or **Other data: a newer run, a file, pasted JSON**), tick **Mark this version as
COPY** or **Ask for approval when it is ready**, and choose **Check and generate vN**. An approved version stays; the
new one needs its own approval.

## Limits
- Generating is limited to 30 a minute a person, and previews to 30 a minute (the designer's live page to 120); past
  that you are asked to wait a few seconds.
- The workspace's page limit applies to every report ([Retention and page limits](#rs-limits)).

## Example
At Summit Valley, Claire Martin (finance controller) creates **Budget vs actual · 2026-10** from the October budget run:
she picks the template, then the budget pipeline's latest run and its output, checks that every required field reads
**Matched**, reads the preview, and generates v1 as PDF and HTML.

articles.title: Reports from a pipeline
articles.summary: The Generate report step — a design inside the step or a saved template, one report per run or one per row — and where the reports go.
articles.who: Anyone who may edit the pipeline; the reports are the workspace's, in Reports › Library
articles.popular: Make a report on every run of a pipeline
articles.md:
A **Generate report** step makes a report every time its pipeline runs: one report per run, or one per row (a statement
for each guarantor, a report for each recording). Each report is a version in **Reports › Library**, approved and
signed there like any other, and its PDF is also kept with the run's outputs.

![The Generate report step](step-outputs "A Generate report step using a saved template: its version, report name and formats")

## Add the step
1. Open the pipeline in **Build › Pipelines**, add a **Generate report** step after the step whose rows it reports on
   (**Reads**), and open its settings.
2. Choose where the design comes from:
   - **Design the report here**: a design that belongs to this step, made from the step's own data. Save the pipeline
     first, then **Design the report**: the designer opens on the rows this step read in the pipeline's latest run.
     Publish the design for the step to run it. **Save as a template** turns it into a normal template.
   - **Use a saved template**: pick a published **Template** of the workspace.
3. **Version** (or **Version the step runs**): **The latest published version**, or a version number to pin.
4. **Report name**: placeholders fill from the run, for example `Reconciliation · {{date}}`, and with one report per row
   from the row's columns, for example `Call · {{file_name}}`. Empty: the design's name and the run.
5. **Formats**: **PDF** and/or **HTML** (as the design says when empty). **Period** is what the report covers, its
   `{{report.period}}`. **Brand profile**: empty means the workspace default.
6. **JSON columns**: columns that hold JSON text, read as the lists and objects they hold, so a table can show them.
7. **One report per row** (off by default): each row its own report, named from its columns; **At most reports** (20 by
   default) caps them.
8. **When the checks refuse it**: `FAIL_TASK` (the default: the step fails) or `CONTINUE_WITH_WARNING` (the step
   completes with no report and a warning on the run).

```Report name, one per row
Statement · {{guarantor_name}}
```

## Where the reports go
- **Reports › Library** lists each report with the template and the run it came from (**pipeline run #NNNN**).
- The run's **Outputs** tab keeps the PDF; **View** opens it in place.
- **Reports › From pipelines** lists the files recent runs made (PDFs, JSON, CSV) with their pipeline and run.
- With **Ask for approval of every new version** on (Reports › Settings), each version waits in **Review › Approvals**.

> **Tip:** A retry of a run makes only the reports it still needs: a report already made for an item whose data and
> design are unchanged is reused.

## Limits
| What | Limit |
|---|---|
| Reports one step makes | at most 200 (**At most reports** 20 by default) |
| One step's time limit | 900 seconds |
| Pages in one report | the workspace's page limit (300 unless lowered) |

When a report would pass the page limit, it is not made, and the failed job offers what applies: **Make one report per
row**, **Lower the table's rows**, **Export the data as CSV** or **Raise the limit** ([Retention and page limits](#rs-limits)).

## Example
Summit Valley's **Patient statements, one per guarantor** pipeline reads the balances, groups them by guarantor and
makes one **Patient statement** per row, named `Statement · Guarantor <name>`: one run, eighteen statements, each its
own report in the Library.

articles.title: Approve, sign and verify
articles.summary: Ask for approval, approve and sign in Review › Approvals or on the report, two approvals, who approves, and Verify signature.
articles.who: Approve and sign reports, and not the person who generated the version
articles.popular: Approve and sign a report
articles.md:
An approval is a person's decision about what they have read. When it is made, the PDF is signed digitally in the
approver's name with the time, using the workspace's certificate: anyone can later check who approved which file and
that it has not changed since.

## Ask for approval
- On a report's page, choose **Ask for approval** on the current version, or tick **Ask for approval when it is ready**
  when you generate.
- Or let the workspace ask for every version: **Reports › Settings › Ask for approval of every new version**.

The version then waits in the approvers' **Review › Approvals**. A newer version replaces the request.

## Approve and sign
1. Open **Review › Approvals** (or the report's page). The task shows the first page and the next ones.
2. Read it. Choose **Approve and sign**, or **Reject**, which needs a reason the person who asked reads.
3. The version now reads **Signed**, with your name and time under **Approved and signed**.

![A signed report](rs-report-page "A report's page: the current version, approved and signed, its PDF and HTML, and where it came from")

> **Note:** Whoever generated a version never approves it (the page says "You generated it; someone else approves it").
> Only a report's **current** version can be approved; an older one never approved reads **Superseded**.

## Two approvals
With **Two approvals** on (Reports › Settings), a second person approves after the first: the first chooses **Give the
first approval of vN**, and the PDF is signed when the second approves, naming both.

## Who approves
In **Reports › Settings**, a workspace administrator sets **Who approves**: **Automatic: the team whose people may
approve**, **The workspace administrators**, or a team you name. **Who publishes** works the same for templates, and
**Publishing needs a second person** stops anyone publishing a draft they edited last or asked to have published. All of
these are off at first.

![Report settings](rs-settings "Reports › Settings: who approves and publishes, retention preview and the page limit")

## Verify a signed PDF
1. On the report's page choose **Verify signature** (or **check signature** beside the approval).
2. **Check version N** checks the stored PDF; **Check a file someone sent** checks a copy you were sent.
3. **The signature holds** when the file is that version as approved, unchanged since; otherwise **Not verified** and
   why. The panel lists who signed, when, the certificate, whether anything changed or was added after signing, and
   whether a stored approved version of this workspace has this file.

![Verify signature](rs-verify "Verify signature: the signature holds, signed by Dr. Minh Nguyen, nothing changed since")

> **Note:** Adobe Reader shows the signature as intact with "validity unknown" until a trusted certificate replaces the
> platform's test certificate. **Verify signature** does not need that trust.

> **Warning:** The signature proves who approved which file and that it has not changed since, not that its content is
> right. Read before you approve.

## Good to know
- A brand profile with **Digitally sign PDFs when approved** off approves without signing; the page says why it is not
  signed.
- Signatures and stamps waiting for approval wait in **Review › Approvals** too.
- Downloads are signed links that work for five minutes, for the person who asked.

articles.title: Versions, COPY, void, archive and delete
articles.summary: Every generate is a new version; mark COPY, void a version you no longer stand behind, archive or delete a report.
articles.who: Generate reports to void, archive or delete; Reports to read the Library
articles.md:
A report keeps every version it ever had. Generating again never overwrites anything: it adds the next version, with
the template version and the frozen data it was made from. This is what lets a signed report stay a record.

## Read a report's versions
Open a report in **Reports › Library**. The **Versions** table lists each one: **Current**, when and by whom it was
generated, the template version and data, whether it is **Signed**, **Approved**, **Waiting** or **Superseded**, and its
files (view or download the PDF and HTML). **Activity** lists everything done to the report, and **Where version N came
from** traces the template, the data, the generation job, the approval and the report.

![The Library](rs-library "Reports › Library: every report with its template, version, files, status and signature")

## Mark a copy
- **Mark this version as COPY** (when you generate) prints COPY on every page of that version.
- A template's **Every download after the first says COPY** marks every download after the first.

## Void a version
Void a version you no longer stand behind, for example one made from the wrong month's data.

1. In **Versions**, choose **Void** on the version.
2. Write **Why it is void** (required) and choose **Mark VOID**.

The version and its files are kept as they are. Every download of it from then on is a copy marked VOID with your
reason, and carries no signature; the signed original is kept and still verifies. This cannot be taken back.

## Archive and delete
- **Archive** takes a report out of the Library and keeps it, with its versions.
- **Delete** removes a report, its versions and files for good, and only while no version of it was approved: an
  approved report is a kept record, so void the version or archive the report instead. In the Library you can tick
  several reports and **Delete** them at once; approved ones cannot be ticked.

> **Warning:** Delete cannot be undone. Stored files the storage does not remove stay until an operator removes them;
> the message after a delete says so.

## Good to know
- Who can see a report: everyone in the workspace who may open Reports, and no one outside it (the **Access** tab).
- **Share** gives a link to the report's page for people of the workspace; downloads are links that work for five
  minutes, for the person who asked.
- The Library, Templates and Assets lists page and search on the server, so a large library opens as quickly as a small one.

articles.title: Retention and page limits
articles.summary: How many pages one report may have, what to do over the limit, and what retention removes — and never removes.
articles.who: Workspace administrators set the page limit and retention; a platform administrator alone raises the ceiling
articles.md:
## The page limit
Every report has a most pages: the workspace's own, 300 unless its administrators set fewer. Every page counts, a long
table's too, in **New report**, a preview and a pipeline's **Generate report** step.

1. Open **Reports › Settings › Report size**.
2. Set **Most pages in one report** (1 up to the workspace's ceiling) and **Save**. The line under it says the limit now
   and the most this workspace may have.

Only the platform administrator can let a workspace go past 300, up to the platform's hard maximum of 2,000 pages.

### Over the limit
A report over the limit is not made. The message names the limit and who can raise it, and the failed job and the
report's page offer what applies:

- **Make one report per row**: opens the pipeline's Generate report step at **One report per row**.
- **Lower the table's rows**: opens the template in the designer on its first long table, repeat or image grid.
- **Export the data as CSV**: the run's data as a file instead of a report.
