**Limits.** At most 1,000 objects a step. Time limit 600 seconds.

## Read API

**What it does.** Runs one of the workspace's saved API requests and takes its answer as rows.

**When to use it.** A partner's or public API: a FHIR server, a drug recall list, a scheduling system.

**Settings.**

- **API request** (required), **Environment** (none: the collection's default) and **Collection version** (pin to a
  published version; empty for the request as it is now).
- **Variables**: the request's variables by name; run placeholders and `{{column}}` from the first row of the step's
  input are filled in.
- **Rows at**: where the rows are in the answer, as a dot path (`data.items`; `entry[].resource` takes the resource of
  every element). Empty: the pages' items, else the body.
- **Columns**: when set, each row is only these columns, each **From the row at** a dot path (such as
  `valueQuantity.value`) **As column**. A path over one list (`results[].term`) makes a row per item.
- **At most rows**: stop after this many.

**Example.** **Drug recalls (openFDA enforcement, offset paging)** reads the public recall list, page by page, keeping
the product, the reason and the class of each recall.

**Limits.** Paging is the saved request's own. Time limit 300 seconds; tried three times on a passing error.

## Read Database

**What it does.** Runs one read-only query on one of the workspace's database connections and takes its rows.

**When to use it.** Your own systems' data, read in place: orders, encounters, a stock table.

**Settings.**

- **Connection** (required): one of the workspace's database connections.
- **Query** (required): one read-only statement: `SELECT`, `WITH`, `VALUES` or `TABLE`. Placeholders such as
  `{{run.windowStart}}` are filled in.
- **At most rows**: stop after this many.

**Example.** **Pharmacy store orders from the shop database** reads the orders placed since the start of the run's
window every hour.

**Limits.** A query is at most 20,000 characters. Database connections are read-only: no step writes to your database.
Time limit 300 seconds; tried twice.

## Read documents

**What it does.** Reads a document type's documents (their fields, status and approval) as rows: all of them, those
approved since the last run, or those approved in a date range; or the documents whose approval started this run.

**When to use it.** Referrals, lab reports, consent forms: anything read by **Documents** and checked by a reviewer.

**Settings.**

- **Document type**: the type whose documents to read. Empty: the documents whose approval started this run.
- **Documents**: `Approved`, `Review` (waiting in the review queue) and/or `Rejected`; Approved when empty.
- **Which approved documents**: `all`, or `last_run` (only those approved since this schedule's last completed run).
- **Approved from**, **Approved to**: a date (2026-10-01) or date and time; placeholders are filled in. The last day is
  included.
- **One row per row of table**: name a table of the type (such as `line_items`) to get one row per table row, the
  document's own values beside it. Empty: each table as JSON text in one column.
- **Only these columns**, **At most rows**.

**Example.** **Lab result PDFs: one row per test** reads the type **Lab result** since the last run, one row per line of
its results table. **Consent forms by date range** reads from `{{param.from}}` to `{{param.to}}`.

**Limits.** Time limit 900 seconds; tried three times.

## Read runs

**What it does.** Reads a pipeline's runs in this workspace, one row each with its review: status, decision, reviewer,
comment, when, and how long the run and the review took.

**When to use it.** Turnaround boards, model-against-reviewer comparisons, a discharge summary that lists what ran.

**Settings.** **Pipeline** (its id, such as `XRAY_TRIAGE`; empty: this run's own pipeline), **Runs of the last (days)**
(30), **Include runs still queued or running** (off), **At most rows** (10,000, the oldest first; the step warns when
there were more).

**Columns.** run_id, job_id, pipeline_id, attempt, status, message, input_key, input_name, run_date, created_at,
started_at, ended_at, duration_seconds, review_status, review_decision, reviewer_id, reviewer_name, review_comment,
review_reason, review_decided_at, review_wait_minutes.

**Limits.** An administrator's step: runs name their reviewers and carry their comments. At most 3,660 days.

## Sample rows

**What it does.** Rows written in the step itself, each an object of column and value.

**When to use it.** To build and test a pipeline before real data exists; **Test with sample** adds this step for you.
See [Try a pipeline](#pl-try).

**Limits.** At most 1,000 rows. Remove it before the pipeline reads real data.

articles.title: Shape steps: choose, clean and work out columns
articles.summary: Select columns, Filter, Transform, Compute, Fill missing values, Split column, Remove duplicates, Sort and Limit / top N.
articles.who: A workspace administrator adds steps

where.label: Build › Pipelines › a pipeline › Steps › Add step

articles.md:
Shape steps change the rows a step reads: which columns there are, which rows stay, what each value is. They do their
work on the platform itself and call nothing outside it. In the builder they are the **Transform** stage.

![The Filter step's settings](step-shape "Filter: keep a row that meets all of its conditions")

## Select columns

**What it does.** Keeps the columns it names, in that order, optionally renamed.

**Settings.** **Columns**: a list of names to keep, or pairs of old and new names to keep and rename. **Fail on a
missing column** (off): fail the step when the input has no such column; otherwise the column is empty.

**Example.** **Referral intake** keeps patient_name, dob, reason, urgency and referring_npi, with **Fail on a missing
column** on, so a referral missing a field stops the run.

## Filter

**What it does.** Keeps the rows that meet all (or any) of its conditions; the others are dropped.

**Settings.**

- **Keep a row that meets**: `all` or `any` of the conditions.
- **Conditions**: each a **Column**, an **Is** and a **Value** (or **Values** for `in` and `not_in`), with **Ignore
  case**. **Is** is one of `eq`, `ne`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `contains`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `in`,
  `not_in`, `is_null`, `not_null`, `is_empty`, `not_empty`.

**Example.** **Appointment reminders for tomorrow** keeps the rows whose `is_tomorrow` is true.

**Limits.** 50 conditions; 1,000 values in one `in` list.

## Transform

**What it does.** Makes each row's columns from its old ones by simple operations.

**Settings.** **Mappings**, each a **Column** to make and an **Operation**: `copy` (**From column**), `constant`
(**Value**), `concat` (**From columns** with a **Separator**), `upper`, `lower`, `trim`, `cast` (**Cast to** text,
integer, number or boolean; **Empty when it cannot cast**), `coalesce` (the first of **From columns** with a value, else
**Value**) and `replace` (**Replace** … **With**). **Keep the other columns** (off): pass the input's columns on too;
otherwise only the mapped ones.

**Example.** **Shift roster clean-up** puts wards in upper case, trims roles, casts hours to whole numbers (leaving
the ones that cannot be read empty) and keeps every other column.

## Compute

**What it does.** Adds columns worked out from each row by a formula; a formula may also replace a column.

**Settings.** **Formulas**, each a **Column** and a **Formula**, with **Empty when it cannot be worked out**.

**Formulas.** Arithmetic and comparisons, and the functions `abs`, `ceil`, `coalesce`, `concat`, `date_add(date, amount,
unit)`, `date_diff(from, to, unit)`, `date_trunc(date, unit)`, `days_between`, `floor`, `if(condition, then,
otherwise)`, `is_null`, `json_get(json, path)`, `json_array_length`, `json_keys`, `max`, `min`, `mod`, `number`,
`regex_extract(text, pattern)`, `round(x, places)`, `text` and `today()`. A unit is second, minute, hour, day (the
default), week, month, quarter or year; a date is YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.

```A Compute formula
round(occupied * 100 / beds, 1)
```

**Text in quotes.** Text in a formula goes in quotes: `'Current'`. To put a quote inside it, write it twice:
`'it''s'` is the text *it's*. A run value or parameter placed inside quotes, such as `'{{param.reviewed_by}}'`, is
safe even when it holds a quote (a reviewer named O'Brien): it stays one text and never ends the quotes early.

**Example.** **Bed occupancy by ward** works out `occupancy_pct` with the formula above; **ER waiting times** works out
`wait_min = date_diff(arrived_at, seen_at, minute)`.

**Limits.** 50 formulas a step; a formula is at most 1,000 characters.

## Fill missing values

**What it does.** Fills the empty cells of the columns you name, with a value or with the last value above them.

**Settings.** **Columns to fill**, each a **Column**, **Fill with** `value` (the **Value** below) or `previous` (the
column's last value above; none above stays empty). **Blank text is empty** (on): text of only spaces counts as empty.

**Example.** **ICU vital-sign gaps carried forward** sorts by patient and time, then carries each patient's last heart
rate and oxygen reading forward and writes "unknown" where the device is missing.

**Limits.** 100 columns a step. Sort first: `previous` follows the rows' order.

## Split column

**What it does.** Cuts a text column at a separator, into named columns or into one row per part.

**Settings.** **Column**, **Separator** (`,`), **Into** (`columns` or `rows`), **New columns** (for columns, the parts'
names in order; for rows, one name for the part), **Trim spaces** (on), **Keep the column** (off), **Skip empty parts**
(on).

**Example.** **Shift roster clean-up** splits "Last, First" into `last_name` and `first_name`; **Online orders JSON feed**
splits each order's SKUs into one row per SKU.

**Limits.** 50 new columns.

## Remove duplicates

**What it does.** Keeps one row per key, the first or the last of each, in the input's order.

**Settings.** **Key columns** (empty: rows equal on every column), **Keep** `first` or `last`, **Ignore case** (also
ignores spaces around text).

**Example.** **Duplicate patient records (master index)** keeps one record per last name, first name and date of birth,
ignoring case: 5,000 rows become 4,880.

## Sort

**What it does.** Orders the rows by one or more columns.

**Settings.** **Sort by**: each a **Column**, a **Direction** (`asc` smallest first, `desc` largest first) and **Empty
values** (`last` or `first`). The first column decides; the next breaks ties. Numbers sort as numbers (also when a CSV
holds them as text) before text; ISO dates sort in date order; rows equal on every column keep their order.

**Limits.** Any number of rows. 10 sort columns. Time limit 1,800 seconds.

## Limit / top N

**What it does.** Keeps the first N rows, or the top N by an order, optionally after skipping some.

**Settings.** **Rows to keep** (required), **Skip first** (0; offset 100 and rows 100 is the second hundred), **Top N
by** (empty: the first rows in their order, and the rest is not read; set: the top rows in that order, reading every
row).

**Example.** **30-day readmission watch-list** keeps the 50 patients with the highest risk score.

articles.title: Combine steps: join, stack, group and reshape
articles.summary: Join, Append (union), Aggregate, Pivot (rows to columns), Unpivot (columns to rows) and Run pipeline.
articles.who: A workspace administrator adds steps; Run pipeline is an administrator's step

where.label: Build › Pipelines › a pipeline › Steps › Add step

articles.md:
Combine steps bring the rows of several steps together, or turn many rows into fewer. A combining step names the
earlier steps it brings in by their keys, so the order of the steps and their keys matter.

![The Join step's settings](step-combine "Join: the claims joined to the remittances on the claim id, keeping every claim")

## Join

**What it does.** Joins the rows it reads (the left side) with an earlier step's output (the right side) on equal keys.

**Settings.**

- **Join with** (required): the earlier step whose output is the right side.
- **On**: pairs of **Left column** and **Right column** that must be equal.
- **Keep**: `inner` (matched rows only) or `left` (every row of the input, the right side's columns empty where nothing
  matched).
- **Prefix for clashing columns** (`right_`): put before a right-side column whose name the left side already has. The
  right side's key columns are dropped.

**Example.** **Payment reconciliation** joins each claim to its remittance on `claim_id`, keeping every claim (`left`)
and prefixing the remittance's columns with `remit_`, so unpaid claims stay in the list.

**Limits.** 10 key pairs.

## Append (union)

**What it does.** Stacks the rows of two or more earlier steps, matching columns by name.

**Settings.**

- **Steps to stack** (required): the earlier steps, in this order.
- **Columns**: `all` (every column any step has; missing ones are empty) or `common` (only the columns every step has).
- **Source column**: a column to add holding the key of the step each row came from.
- **Column types**: a column's kind (number, text, boolean) to convert every step's values to. **Convert mismatched
  values** (on) converts a value of another kind, failing when it cannot.

**Example.** **Journey 9 · Care-plan draft** stacks the patient's record, labs, triage and imaging results, with a
**Source column** named `stage`, before asking the model for a draft plan.

**Limits.** 2 to 20 steps.

## Aggregate

**What it does.** Groups rows by columns and computes a figure per group.

**Settings.**

- **Group by**: the columns that make a group. Empty: one row for all the input.
- **Aggregations**: each a **Compute** (`count`, `count_distinct`, `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `first`, `last` or
  `list`), **Of column** (every operation but count needs one) and **As column**. `list` is the group's distinct values
  as one text, joined by ", ".

**Example.** **Bed occupancy by ward** counts beds, sums occupied beds and finds the longest stay per ward.

**Limits.** 20 group columns; 1 to 50 aggregations.

## Pivot (rows to columns)

**What it does.** Turns rows into columns: one row per group, one column per value of a column.

**Settings.** **Row per** (the columns that make one output row, such as a patient id), **Names from** (its values
become the new columns' names), **Values from** (what fills them), **When a group has several** (`first`, `last`,
`sum`, `count`, `min`, `max` or `avg`), **Only these** (the new columns to make, in order; others are left out).

**Example.** **Journey 15 · Cohort stages** makes one row per patient with a column per stage of the journey, each the
time that stage ended.

**Limits.** 200 new columns. Time limit 1,800 seconds.

## Unpivot (columns to rows)

**What it does.** Turns columns into rows: each named column becomes a row with its name and value, the other columns
repeated.

**Settings.** **Columns to turn into rows** (required), **Name column** (`name`), **Value column** (`value`), **Keep
empty values** (off).

**Example.** **Budget vs actual by cost centre** turns a budget sheet with a column per month into one row per cost
centre and month, so it can be joined to the actuals.

**Limits.** 200 columns.

## Run pipeline

**What it does.** Calls another pipeline of the workspace with parameters, once or once per row, waits for its run and
takes its answer as rows.

**When to use it.** A piece of work several pipelines need, built once. Settings, results and limits are in
[Call another pipeline](#pl-run-pipeline).

**Limits.** An administrator's step; at most 3 calls deep; each call is a run, billed like any run.

articles.title: Check and enrich: Validate, Enrich and Call API
articles.summary: Hold rows to a data contract, add fields from an API per row, and send rows to another system once, per row, in batches or with a file.
articles.who: A workspace administrator adds steps; Call API is an administrator's step

where.label: Build › Pipelines › a pipeline › Steps › Add step

articles.popular: Call an API for each row
articles.md:
These steps talk to the workspace's data contracts and saved API requests. **Validate** checks rows; **Enrich** adds to
them from an API; **Call API** sends them somewhere and keeps each answer so later steps can branch on it. The
requests themselves (address, method, authentication, paging) are saved in the workspace's API collections.

![The Call API step's settings](step-check "Call API: one call per appointment to the payer's eligibility request")

## Validate

**What it does.** Checks each row against a data contract and fails, drops or flags the rows that do not hold.

**Settings.**

- **Contract**: one of the workspace's data contracts; or **Contract name**: a contract by name (the workspace's, else a
  system contract).
- **Contract version**: a version to hold to; empty for the contract's active version.
- **Rows that do not hold**: `fail` the step, `drop` the rows, or `flag` them: every row goes on with `_valid` (true or
  false) and `_errors`.

**Example.** **ADT feed** drops invalid events; **Claims file validation** flags the claim lines, then one branch keeps
the rejects (a **Filter** on `_valid` is false) and another the clean rows.

**Limits.** Time limit 300 seconds; tried twice on a passing error.

## Enrich

**What it does.** Calls a saved API request once per row and adds fields of its answer as columns.

**Settings.**

- **API request** (required), **Environment**, **Collection version**.
- **Variables**: the request's variables by name, filled from the row: `{{customer_id}}`.
- **Fields** (required): each **From the answer at** a dot path (`data.score`) **As column**. A path over a list
  (`results[].term`) makes one row per item.
- **When a call fails**: `fail` the step, `skip` the row, or `null` (keep it with the fields empty).
- **At most calls**: 100 unless you say.

**Example.** **Adverse event signals** asks a public drug-safety API for each of 20 drugs' most reported reactions, one
row per reaction.

**Limits.** At most 500 calls a step. Time limit 1,800 seconds.

## Call API

**What it does.** Sends to a saved request (POST, PUT) once, per row or in batches, with a file an earlier step made if
asked, and keeps the status and fields of each answer.

**Settings.**

- **API request** (required), **Environment**, **Collection version**.
- **Send**:
  - `each`: one call per row; `{{row}}` is the row as one JSON object.
  - `batch`: one call per **Rows per call** rows (50 unless you say); `{{rows_json}}` is them as one JSON array,
    `{{batch}}` of `{{batches}}`.
  - `once`: one call for the step, filled from the run and the first row.
- **Columns sent**: what `{{row}}` and `{{rows_json}}` hold: these columns, each renamed with **As** (a dot nests:
  `patient.id`). None: every column.
- **Variables**: the request's variables, filled from the row and the run (`{{patient_id}}`, `{{row}}`, `{{run}}`,
  `{{call_key}}`).
- **Fields**: each **From the answer at** a dot path (`id`, `result.status`, `errors[0].message`) **As column**.
- **Results at** (batch): a dot path to the answer's list of per-row results; each row's fields are read from its item,
  by position.
- **Ok only when**: conditions on the answer's body beyond a 2xx status, each **The answer at**, **Is**, **Value**.
- **When a call is not ok**: `fail` the step, or `continue` with the row's status and error for later steps to branch
  on.
- **Column prefix** (`api_`): the answer's columns are `api_status`, `api_ok` and `api_error`.
- **Calls at once** (1): `each` and `batch` calls made together, at most 8; answers keep the rows' order, and a busy
  service is backed off.
- **At most calls** (100): with `each`, an input needing more calls fails before any is made.

### Send a file an earlier step made

Under **A file from an earlier step**, name the step (**From step**: a **Save File**, **Generate report** or **Convert
file** step of this run), the **File name** when it made several, and where to **Put in** a file kept with the run (a
storage connection; empty for the workspace's file drop). The request's file or multipart body then gets
`{{file_bucket}}`, `{{file_key}}`, `{{file_name}}` and `{{file_format}}`.

### Send a report in PDF, HTML or Markdown

Under **A report from an earlier step**, name the **Generate report** step (**From step**) and the **Formats sent**:
`pdf` (the report's PDF, the signed one once it is approved and signed, as base64 in `{{report_pdf}}`), `html` (its page
in `{{report_html}}`) and `md` (Markdown made from that page in `{{report_md}}`; never signed). The request also gets
`{{report_label}}` (RPT-0093), `{{report_version}}` and `{{report_signed}}`. With **Send** `each` and a report step that
made one report per row, each row sends its own report; sent `once` or in batches, the report step must have made one
report of all the rows. A report made without the format asked for (a PDF-only report has no HTML, so no Markdown) fails
the step before any call, saying so. The rows still go as JSON (`{{row}}`, `{{rows_json}}`) as always.

**Before you run.** With sample rows first ([Test with sample](#pl-try)), the panel shows **What the first call sends**.

**Examples.** **Eligibility checks before tomorrow's visits** calls the payer once per appointment, four at a time, and
continues on a failed call so a **Filter** can list them for staff. **Appointment reminders** sends 50 rows a call to an
SMS service. **Clearinghouse submission** sends the claim file a **Save File** step made, once.

**Limits.** At most 500 calls; **Rows per call** up to 1,000. Time limit 1,800 seconds; one try unless the panel says
otherwise. An administrator's step.

> **Warning:** Call API reaches outside the platform. Send only the columns the other system needs (**Columns sent**),
> especially for sensitive data.

articles.title: AI and media steps: prompts, recordings, files, pages and images
articles.summary: AI prompt, Transcribe audio, Convert file, Split pages, Read text from pages, Measure image and Measure mask.
articles.who: A workspace administrator adds steps; the models a step may use follow the workspace's data policy

where.label: Build › Pipelines › a pipeline › Steps › Add step

articles.popular: Ask an AI model about each row
articles.md:
These steps work on what is not yet a row of data: a recording, a document, a scanned page, a photo, or a question for a
model. Most of them work one file or one row at a time, so a run's **Items** view shows each file with how it went.

Several of them read files in the same way. **Bucket** names the storage connection the files are in, and **File key
column** names the column that holds each row's file key. Leave both empty to work on the list a **Read S3** step made
before it, or on the files the run was started for (a file that arrived in the inbox).

A form's file field works as it is in any of these key columns -- **Image key column**, **Mask key column** or **File key
column**: name the field itself (`photo`, `signature`, `recording`), not a hidden `photo_key`. The step reads the file
from where the form stored it, under the name it was uploaded with. A field holding several files is read by its first
(the run is warned how many rows held more), and a field with no file says so for that row.

> **Warning:** A model's answer is a DRAFT for a person to check. Put an [Approval](#step-people) step, or the
> pipeline's review, after an AI step whose answer matters.

![The AI prompt step's settings](step-ai "AI prompt: a saved vision prompt run on each wound photo, its answer split into fields")

## AI prompt

**What it does.** Runs one of the workspace's saved prompts on each row, optionally with the row's image, and adds the
answer as columns.

**Settings.**

- **Prompt** (required): a saved prompt of this workspace. Its model connection runs it.
- **Variables**: the prompt's variables by name, filled from the row (`{{record_id}}`). A variable not named here is
  filled from the row's column of its name; a required one with no value fails that row.
- **Image**: a **Bucket** and an **Image key column** to send each row's image (png, jpg, webp or gif) to a vision
  model with the prompt.
- **Answer column** (`ai_output`), and **Fields**: each **From the answer at** a dot path into a JSON answer (`status`,
  `result.score`) **As column**.
- **When a row fails**: `fail` the step, `skip` the row, or `null` (keep it with the answer empty).
- **Calls at once** (1, at most 8) and **At most rows** (50).

**Example.** **Journey 7 · Wound photo** sends each photo to the vision prompt "Wound description (DRAFT)" and keeps the
stage, tissue and exudate as columns for the wound-care nurse to approve.

**Limits.** At most 500 rows a step; an image at most 8 MB. Time limit 3,600 seconds. Which models may see the data is
set by the workspace's data policy for the pipeline's sensitivity.

## Transcribe audio

**What it does.** Turns each row's recording (mp3, m4a, wav, ogg, flac or webm) into text with the platform's
transcriber.

**Settings.** **Bucket**, **File key column**, **Timestamps** (off; on also adds `segments`: each stretch of speech with
its start and end, as JSON), **When a file fails** (`fail`, `skip`, or `null`: kept with the transcript empty and the
reason in `transcribe_error`), **Calls at once** (1), **At most files** (20).

**Adds.** `file_name`, `file_stem`, `transcript`, `language`, `duration_seconds` and, with timestamps, `segments`.

**Example.** **Care-call insight, one report per call** transcribes each home-health call recording two at a time,
then asks a prompt for the call's summary, symptoms and actions.

**Limits.** A recording up to 500 MB; at most 1,000 files a step. Time limit two hours.

## Convert file

**What it does.** Converts each row's file with the platform's converter and writes the result to a bucket or keeps it
with the run.

**Settings.**

- **Bucket**, **File key column**.
- **Convert to** (`pdf`): a document to pdf, txt, docx, odt, rtf, md or html; a spreadsheet to pdf, csv, xlsx or ods; a
  presentation to pdf or pptx; images to png or jpg.
- **Write the result to**: `bucket` (an object at **Output key** in **Output bucket**; empty: the file's own bucket) or
  `run` (a file kept with the run, in its outputs).
- **Output key** (`converted/{{file_stem}}.{{format}}`), **When a file fails** (`fail`, `skip` or `null`), **At most
  files** (20).

**Adds.** `converted_key`, `converted_pages`, `converted_bytes` and `convert_status`.

**Example.** **Letters archived as PDF** converts each night's new letters to PDF under `archive/`, skipping a corrupt
file and carrying on.

**Limits.** A file up to 500 MB; at most 1,000 files. Time limit 3,600 seconds.

## Split pages

**What it does.** Splits each row's PDF into pages: one row per page with its text, each page's image kept with the
run. Every page becomes a sub-item of its document, with its own status and retry.

**Settings.** **Bucket**, **File key column**, **Image resolution (dpi)** (100, from 72 to 200), **A page needs at least
characters** (1; a page with less text failed, as a scanned page needs OCR; 0: never), **When a page or file fails**
(`null` unless you say), **At most documents** (20) and **At most pages a document** (200).

**Adds.** `page`, `page_count`, `page_text`, `page_chars`, `page_image`, `page_status`, `page_error`.

**Limits.** A PDF up to 200 MB; at most 100 documents and 2,000 pages a document. Time limit 3,600 seconds.

## Read text from pages

**What it does.** Reads the text on page images that **Split pages** made, with the platform's own OCR, and says how
sure it is. A page it is not sure enough of is marked **Check by hand** and sent to **Review** with its image beside
the text.

**Settings.**

- **Pages from** (required): the earlier step whose page images are read, usually **Split pages**.
- **Image column** (`page_image`), **Text layer column** (`page_text`), **Language** (`eng`, English).
- **Which pages**: `no_text_layer` (only scans and photos; pages with their own text keep it and are not read or billed)
  or `every_page`.
- **A text layer has at least (characters)** (16): a page with fewer characters has no text layer and is read.
- **Flag a page when sureness is below (%)** (80, from 50 to 99), and **Who checks the pages** (a role or a team; empty:
  the workspace's administrators).
- **When a page cannot be read** (`null`), **At most pages** (200).

**Adds.** `ocr_text`, `ocr_sureness` (0 to 100), `ocr_source` (`ocr` or `text-layer`), `ocr_words`, `ocr_status` (`ok`,
`check` or `failed`), `ocr_note` and `ocr_rotation` (how far the page was turned to be read upright).

**Example.** **Faxed referrals: split pages and read them** splits each fax, reads only the scanned pages, and sends the
handwritten page the OCR is unsure of to the records team.

**Limits.** At most 2,000 pages. Each page read is billed (OCR pages). Time limit two hours.

## Measure image

**What it does.** Measures the object in each row's photo against the ruler in it (1 cm ticks), in code, not by a
model: length, width and area in cm.

**Settings.** **Image** (required): a **Bucket** and an **Image key column** (png or jpg). **What to measure**:
`contrast` (the largest region outside the ruler whose colour differs markedly from the background) or `red_region` (a
red region on a lighter background, leaving out a lighter, pinker halo). The output column names (`scale_found`,
`px_per_cm`, `length_cm`, `width_cm`, `area_cm2`, `measure_note`), **When a photo cannot be read** (`null`: sizes empty
and the reason in the note), **At most rows** (50).

**Example.** Wound photos taken with a paper ruler beside the wound: the step gives the size, and the change since the
last visit is worked out by **Compute**.

**Limits.** At most 500 rows.

## Measure mask

**What it does.** Measures the region a segmentation mask marks (the marked pixels light on a dark background), in
pixels: area, share of the image, bounding box and region count. A mask has no scale, so no cm or mm.

**Settings.** **Mask** (required): a **Bucket** and a **Mask key column**. **Marked from brightness** (128, from 1 to
255), **Column prefix** (such as `lesion_`), **When a mask cannot be read** (`null`), **At most rows** (50).

**Adds.** `mask_width`, `mask_height`, `area_px`, `area_pct`, `box_x`, `box_y`, `box_width`, `box_height`, `regions`,
`largest_region_px` and `measure_note`.

**Example.** **Breast ultrasound: lesion size from the mask** measures each frame's lesion mask, with the prefix
`lesion_`.

**Limits.** At most 500 rows.

articles.title: The Approval step: a person decides in the middle of a run
articles.summary: Pause a run until its reviewers approve; what they see, who they are, how long they have, and what a rejection does.
articles.who: A workspace administrator adds the step; the reviewers it names decide in Review › Approvals

where.label: Build › Pipelines › a pipeline › Steps › Add step

articles.md:
An **Approval** step pauses the run at that point until its reviewers approve. Approved, the run goes on with the same
rows, unchanged; rejected, or not decided in time, the run fails, with the reason the reviewer gave. Use it where a
person must look before anything leaves: before a report is signed, before a file is sent, after an AI step whose answer
matters.

It is one of two ways a person approves a pipeline's work. The other, the pipeline's **review** (its **Settings** tab),
waits on the whole run's results after the last step. See [Pipeline settings](#pl-settings--review-whether-a-person-approves-the-results).

![The Approval step's settings](step-people "Approval: what the wound-care team sees, and how long they have to decide")

## Set up an Approval step

1. Add **Approval** from **Add step** where the run should wait.
2. **Task title**: what the reviewers' task says. It fills from the run and the first row, such as
   `Wound {{mrn}}: {{area_cm2}} cm²` or `Approve {{rows}} results of run {{run}}`.
3. **What to check**: the instructions shown on the task.
4. **Fields**: name and value pairs shown on the task, such as `Abnormal` = `{{abnormal_count}}`.
5. **Reviewers**: **Reviewers are** `role` or `team`, and **Role or team**: `TENANT_ADMIN` (the workspace's
   administrators) or `TENANT_USER` (every member) for a role, or the team's id. Empty: the pipeline's review reviewers,
   else the workspace's administrators.
6. **Decide within (hours)**: 72 unless you say. Nobody deciding in this time fails the run.
7. Choose **Apply**, then **Save**.

## What the reviewers do

The task appears in **Run & review › Review › Approvals** for the people the step names, with its title, instructions,
fields and the number of rows. They open it, check the rows, and approve or reject; a rejection may need a reason. How
reminders and overdue tasks are handled is set in **Approval workflows › Pipeline step approval**.

> **Note:** When the pipeline's settings have **Requires individual review**, its Approval steps' requests are never
> approved or rejected in bulk with others.

## Example

In Summit Valley's **Journey 7 · Wound photo**, after the photo is measured and described, the step "Wound care approves
the measurement" asks the Wound care team, with the title `Wound {{mrn}}: {{area_cm2}} cm²`, to decide within 24 hours.
Only then is the wound report made. In **Controlled substance count reconciliation**, pharmacist Avi Cohen rejects a
count with a reason, and the run fails naming it.

## Limits

| What | Limit |
|---|---|
| Decide within | 1 to 720 hours (72 by default) |
| Task title | 200 characters |
| What to check | 2,000 characters |
| A field's value | 500 characters |

articles.popular: Save a pipeline's results as a file
articles.md:
An output step sends the rows somewhere and passes them on unchanged, so a pipeline can keep a file, make a report and
tell people, one step after another. In the builder they are the **Write** stage; the overview strip's **Outputs** part
lists them.

Two of them write one file for all the rows, or one file per row: **Save File** and **Upload to bucket**. With **One
file per row**, each file is named from its row's columns, as in `{{file_stem}}-insight.json`, and **JSON columns**
(columns holding JSON text, such as an AI answer's lists) are written as lists and objects rather than as text.

![The Generate report step's settings](step-outputs "Generate report with a saved template, named after the run's date")

## Save File

**What it does.** Keeps the rows as a CSV, JSON or JSON Lines file with the run, in its outputs.

**Settings.** **File name** (required; letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_`; placeholders filled in), **Format** (`csv`,
`json` or `jsonl`), **One file per row** (off), **At most files** (100, one file per row), **JSON columns**.

**Example.** **Duplicate patient records** keeps `mpi-unique.csv`; **Care-call insight** keeps
`insights/{{file_stem}}.json`, one per call.

**Limits.** A file name at most 128 characters; at most 1,000 files a step. The file is kept as long as the run's
outputs are.

## Upload to bucket

**What it does.** Writes the rows as a CSV, JSON or JSON Lines object in one of the workspace's buckets, for a dashboard,
another system or a later pipeline.

**Settings.** **Bucket** (required), **Object key** (required; `{{run}}`, `{{date}}`, `{{time}}`, `{{pipeline}}` and the
other placeholders filled in; one file per row: the row's columns too), **Format**, **One file per row**, **At most
files** (100), **JSON columns**.

**Example.** **Bed occupancy by ward** uploads `ops/beds/occupancy.csv` for the bed board each morning.

**Limits.** A row's values cannot add folders to a key. At most 1,000 objects. An administrator's step; tried three
times on a passing error.

## Generate report

**What it does.** Makes a Report Studio report from the rows and keeps its PDF with the run. The report is a version in
**Reports › Library**, approved and signed there like any other report.

**Settings.**

- **Report design**: **Design the report here** (a design made inside this step from the step's own data) or **Use a
  saved template** (a published template of the workspace).
- **Template** and **Version**: **The latest published version**, or a version number to pin.
- **Report name**: placeholders fill from the run (`Reconciliation · {{date}}`), and with one report per row from the
  row's columns. Empty: the design's name and the run.
- **Formats**: **PDF** and/or **HTML**; as the design says when empty. The PDF is kept with the run.
- **Period**: what the report covers, as its `{{report.period}}`.
- **Brand profile**: a published brand profile; the workspace's default when empty.
- **JSON columns**: columns holding JSON text, read as the lists and objects they hold, so a table in the design can show
  them.
- **One report per row** (off): each row its own report and its own version in Reports, named from its columns.
  **Calls at once** and **At most reports** (20) apply.
- **When the checks refuse it**: `FAIL_TASK` (the step fails) or `CONTINUE_WITH_WARNING` (the step completes with no
  report and a warning on the run).

Designing reports, templates, approval and signatures are described in the Report Studio chapter.

**Example.** **Payment reconciliation** makes the "Reconciliation" report from the saved template each morning;
**Patient statements, one per guarantor** makes one statement per guarantor, 18 in all.

**Limits.** At most 200 reports a step. Time limit 900 seconds.

## Render PDF

**What it does.** Prints the rows as a simple PDF report kept with the run. A big table prints its first rows and keeps
the full data as a CSV beside the PDF.

**Settings.** **File name** (required; `.pdf` is added), **Title**, **Header fields** (label and value pairs above the
table), **Columns**, **Page** (`auto` turns the page for more than six columns; `portrait`; `landscape`), **Watermark**
(such as DRAFT), **Report template** (the default layout when empty), **Rows in the PDF** (5,000), **Attach the full
data** (on), and **Sections**: several tables in one report, each with its **Section title**, **Shows** (`table`, or
`statistics` per column: rows, empty, distinct, min, max, sum, mean and the most frequent values), **Rows of** (an earlier
step), **Columns**, **Note**, **Most frequent values** and **Histograms** (numeric columns drawn as ten bins).

**Example.** **ER waiting times: door to doctor** prints one table per triage level and a statistics section with a
histogram of waiting minutes, watermarked INTERNAL, in landscape.

**Limits.** Up to 50,000 rows printed; 20 sections; 10 histograms. For a designed, approved and signed report, use
**Generate report**.

## Send Notification

**What it does.** Sends a notice about the run to people's notification bell.

**Settings.** **Title** (required; `{{rows}}`, `{{pipeline}}`, `{{run}}`, `{{date}}` and the first row's `{{column}}`
filled in), **Message**, **Severity** (`INFO`, `SUCCESS`, `WARNING` or `ERROR`), **To** (`owner`: the schedule's owner;
`admins`; `everyone`; or `users` with **People** chosen by name), **Send** (`always`, `has_rows` or `no_rows`), **Link**
(a console path the notice opens, starting with /).

**Example.** **Bed occupancy by ward** tells the administrators "No census rows for {{date}}" only when the census was
empty (`no_rows`).

**Limits.** At most 500 people. Time limit 120 seconds.

## Send webhook

**What it does.** Posts the rows, or a summary of them, to one of the workspace's registered webhooks: signed, retried
and logged.

**Settings.** **Webhook** (required; an active webhook of this workspace that takes the `run.step.sent` event type, set
up in **Developers › API Clients**), **Send** (`summary`: the row count, the columns and the fields; or `rows`), **Columns**
(for rows), **At most rows** (500; more fails the step, nothing is cut), **Fields** (name and value pairs sent with it),
**Wait for the first try (s)** (10), **Fail unless delivered** (off).

**Example.** **Remote monitoring: readings over threshold** sends each over-threshold reading to the care team's pager
and fails the step if the pager has not taken it within 20 seconds.

**Limits.** At most 5,000 rows; a wait of at most 60 seconds; the webhook is retried in the background either way. An
administrator's step.

## Write Database is switched off

**Write Database** is listed in **Settings › Task Registry**, but it cannot be added to a pipeline: "Writing to a
database is not part of this release: database connections are read-only."

Pipelines read your databases with **Read Database** and never write into them. A mistake in a pipeline, or a model's
draft answer, can then never change a system of record. To get results back into your own systems, use an output that
your systems pick up and check: **Upload to bucket**, **Send webhook**, **Call API** (to an API your system offers), or
the platform's API, from which your systems read a run's results.

articles.title: Every step at a glance
articles.summary: One table of every step, its main settings, its defaults and its limits, and the settings every step shares.
articles.who: Anyone who builds or reads pipelines
articles.md:
This page is the short form of the step reference: every step the console's **Add step** offers, grouped as in this
chapter. The full settings, with examples, are in each group's article. **Settings › Task Registry** lists the same
steps for your workspace, with how many pipelines use each and whether it is on.

![The Task Registry](step-registry "Settings › Task Registry: every step task, its kind, what it reads and makes, and whether it is on in this workspace")

## Settings every step has

| Setting | What it does | When blank |
|---|---|---|
| **Key** | Names the step's rows; what a later step reads | Required |
| **Name** | What the run's timeline calls it | The key |
| **Reads** | The output it works on | The latest output before this step |
| **Tries** | How many times it is tried; 1 to 10 | The step's own default (below), else 1 |
| **Seconds between tries** | 0 to 3,600 | The step's own default |
| **Timeout (seconds)** | Each try's time limit, 1 to 86,400 | The step's own (below), else the pipeline's default timeout (600) |
| **If it fails** | **Fail the run**, **Continue with the next step** or **Skip the rest and complete** | The pipeline's **If a step fails** |

A step that only reads or works on rows, and an output that writes the same thing again on a repeat (Save File, Upload
to bucket, Generate report, Render PDF), is also tried again by itself on a passing error when you set no tries.

## Read

| Step | Main settings | Defaults | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|
| Read CSV/JSON/Parquet | Bucket, File, Format, CSV and JSON options, Only these columns | Format auto; 3 tries; 600 s | Empty bucket and file: the run's own file |
| Read S3 | Bucket, Prefix, Read as, The run's own files first, Which objects | list; 100 objects; all; 3 tries; 600 s | 1,000 objects |
| Read API | API request, Environment, Variables, Rows at, Columns | 3 tries; 300 s | 100 columns |
| Read Database | Connection, Query, At most rows | 2 tries; 300 s | One read-only statement, 20,000 characters |
| Read documents | Document type, Documents, Which approved documents, Approved from/to, One row per row of table | Approved; all; 3 tries; 900 s | |
| Read runs | Pipeline, Runs of the last (days), Include runs still queued or running | 30 days; 10,000 rows | Administrators only; 3,660 days |
| Sample rows | Rows | | 1,000 rows |

## Shape

| Step | Main settings | Defaults | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|
| Select columns | Columns (or old and new names), Fail on a missing column | Off | |
| Filter | Keep a row that meets, Conditions | all | 50 conditions, 1,000 values in a list |
| Transform | Mappings (copy, constant, concat, upper, lower, trim, cast, coalesce, replace), Keep the other columns | copy; off | 200 mappings |
| Compute | Formulas, Empty when it cannot be worked out | Off | 50 formulas, 1,000 characters each |
| Fill missing values | Columns to fill (value or previous), Blank text is empty | value; on | 100 columns |
| Split column | Column, Separator, Into, New columns, Trim spaces, Keep the column, Skip empty parts | `,`; columns; on; off; on | 50 new columns |
| Remove duplicates | Key columns, Keep, Ignore case | Every column; first; off | 1,800 s |
| Sort | Sort by (column, direction, empty values) | asc; empty last | 10 columns; 1,800 s |
| Limit / top N | Rows to keep, Skip first, Top N by | 0 skipped | |

## Combine

| Step | Main settings | Defaults | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|
| Join | Join with, On, Keep, Prefix for clashing columns | inner; `right_` | 10 key pairs |
| Append (union) | Steps to stack, Columns, Source column, Column types | all; convert on | 2 to 20 steps |
| Aggregate | Group by, Aggregations | One group for all | 20 group columns, 50 aggregations |
| Pivot (rows to columns) | Row per, Names from, Values from, When a group has several, Only these | first | 200 columns; 1,800 s |
| Unpivot (columns to rows) | Columns to turn into rows, Name column, Value column, Keep empty values | name; value; off | 200 columns |
| Run pipeline | Pipeline, Call, Parameters, Answer from, Fields | once; final; 20 calls; 10,000 rows; 3,600 s | Administrators only; 100 calls; 3 deep |

## Check and enrich

| Step | Main settings | Defaults | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|
| Validate | Contract (or Contract name), Contract version, Rows that do not hold | Active version; fail; 2 tries; 300 s | |
| Enrich | API request, Variables, Fields, When a call fails | fail; 100 calls; 1,800 s | 500 calls |
| Call API | API request, Send, Columns sent, Variables, Fields, Ok only when, When a call is not ok, A file from an earlier step | each; 50 rows per call; fail; `api_`; 1 at once; 100 calls; 1,800 s | Administrators only; 500 calls; 1,000 rows per call; 8 at once |

## AI and media

| Step | Main settings | Defaults | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|
| AI prompt | Prompt, Variables, Image, Answer column, Fields, When a row fails | `ai_output`; fail; 1 at once; 50 rows; 3,600 s | 500 rows; 8 at once; image 8 MB |
| Transcribe audio | Bucket, File key column, Timestamps, When a file fails | Off; fail; 1 at once; 20 files; 7,200 s | 1,000 files; 500 MB a recording |
| Convert file | Bucket, File key column, Convert to, Write the result to, Output key | pdf; bucket; 20 files; 3,600 s | 1,000 files; 500 MB a file |
| Split pages | Bucket, File key column, Image resolution, A page needs at least characters | 100 dpi; 1; 20 documents; 200 pages; 3,600 s | 100 documents; 2,000 pages; 200 MB a PDF |
| Read text from pages | Pages from, Which pages, Flag a page when sureness is below, Who checks the pages | no_text_layer; 80 %; 200 pages; 7,200 s | 2,000 pages; billed per page read |
| Measure image | Image, What to measure, output columns | contrast; 50 rows | 500 rows |
| Measure mask | Mask, Marked from brightness, Column prefix | 128; 50 rows | 500 rows |

## People

| Step | Main settings | Defaults | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|
| Approval | Task title, What to check, Fields, Reviewers, Decide within (hours) | 72 hours; the workspace's administrators | 720 hours |

## Outputs

| Step | Main settings | Defaults | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|
| Save File | File name, Format, One file per row, JSON columns | csv; off; 100 files | 1,000 files; name 128 characters |
| Upload to bucket | Bucket, Object key, Format, One file per row, JSON columns | csv; off; 100 files; 3 tries; 600 s | Administrators only; 1,000 objects |
| Generate report | Report design, Template, Version, Report name, Formats, Period, Brand profile, One report per row | Design here; latest; 20 reports; 900 s | 200 reports |
| Render PDF | File name, Title, Header fields, Columns, Page, Watermark, Sections | auto; 5,000 rows; full data attached; 900 s | 50,000 rows; 20 sections |
| Send Notification | Title, Message, Severity, To, Send, Link | INFO; owner; always; 120 s | 500 people |
| Send webhook | Webhook, Send, Columns, At most rows, Fields, Wait, Fail unless delivered | summary; 500 rows; 10 s; off; 120 s | Administrators only; 5,000 rows; 60 s wait |
| Write Database | | | Switched off: database connections are read-only |

## Data a step can hold

By default, a step that holds its rows in memory (such as **Join**, **Enrich** or **AI prompt**) stops at 50,000 rows,
200 columns or 1,000,000 cells, and at 50 MB for a file. Steps that stream their rows instead (the file reads, **Filter**,
**Select columns**, **Compute**, **Sort**, **Aggregate**, **Remove duplicates**, the file outputs and others) keep them on
disk and are held only to much larger safety limits, so a file of a million rows can be read, filtered and aggregated.
A step that reaches a limit fails and says so; it never cuts rows silently.

articles.title: How to use this guide
articles.summary: The test accounts you need, synthetic data only, how to record a result and what to do when a check fails.
articles.who: Testers, and the workspace administrators who set up their accounts
articles.popular: Prepare the accounts for a manual test
articles.md:
This chapter is a checklist for someone who tests the ETL Console by hand, area by area: sign-in, people and access,
connections, documents, forms, pipelines, schedules, AI, runs, reviews, reports, dashboards, the API, billing, security
and settings. You do not need to know how the console is built. Each area is one article; each check is one row of a
table with what to do, what you should see, and a box to tick.

Read this article once before you start. Then work through the areas in order: the later ones use what the earlier ones
made (a connection, a form, a pipeline, a run).

## How a check reads
| Column | What it holds |
|---|---|
| **#** | The check's number, such as **QA-07.03**: area 07, check 03. A number never changes once printed; new checks are added at the end of their area. |
| **Check** | What is being tested, in a few words |
| **Steps** | What to do, in order. Names in **bold** are exactly what the screen shows. "As A" says which test account to sign in as (see below). |
| **Expected** | What you should see. A check passes only when everything in this cell is true. |
| **Pass / Fail** | Tick one box: ☐ Pass or ☐ Fail |

An expected result marked **(not yet verified)** describes a behaviour that is planned or built but has not been seen
working end to end yet. Test it like any other and record what you see: your result is how it becomes verified.

## The test accounts
Ask a workspace administrator to make these accounts before you start (see [Add a person](#adm-people--add-a-person)).
Use them only for testing. In this guide each has a short letter, used in the **Steps** column.

| Letter | Account | Role and access | In the example workspace |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | Workspace administrator | **Workspace administrator** | Summit Valley admin |
| **A2** | A second administrator | **Workspace administrator**, a different person: approves what A made, since nobody approves their own work | Jordan Reyes, operations director |
| **R** | Reviewer | **Workspace member** on a profile that opens **Review**, **Runs**, **Forms › Submissions**, **Dashboards** and **Reports**, in at least one team | Dr. Anika Patel (Clinician profile, Physicians team) |
| **V** | Viewer | **Workspace member** on a profile that opens only **Runs › Analytics** and **Dashboards** | Summit Valley viewer (Viewer profile) |
| **F** | Front desk | **Workspace member** on a narrow profile that opens **Forms** and nothing else (made before you start: [Make an access profile](#adm-access-profiles--make-an-access-profile)) | a front-desk clerk on a profile named *Front desk* |
| **RS** | Researcher | **Workspace member** whose profile opens **Analysis** (Ask your data, Analytics Studio, Data Catalog) and **Dashboards** | Dr. Hana Ito (Researcher profile) |
| **X** | Someone in a second workspace | **Workspace administrator** of another workspace, for the isolation checks | the administrator of Meridian Finance & Retail |

> **Tip:** Keep each account in its own browser profile or private window, so you can switch between A, R and V without
> signing out each time.

> **Warning:** Never test as a real person's account, and never as the platform's owner account. Make test accounts.

## Synthetic data only
Every file, form answer, patient, invoice and number you use in a test must be made up. Use the sample files of the
Recipes chapter or your own synthetic ones: names like *Elena Marsh*, record numbers like
`SV-000117`. Never type a real patient's details into a form, a reason box, a pipeline's name or a test value. See
[Working with health data](#sec-health-data).

## Before you start
Run these checks first. If one fails, stop and fix it: the other areas depend on it.

| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-01.01 | Every test account signs in | Sign in as A, A2, R, V, F, RS and X in turn | Each reaches **Home**; the name at the top right is that account's | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-01.02 | The roles are right | As A, open **Administration › Users** and find each test account | A and A2 read **Workspace administrator**; R, V, F and RS read **Workspace member** with the profile given above | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-01.03 | The menus differ by role | Sign in as A, then R, then V, and compare the menus on the left | A sees every group, including **Administration & billing**; R sees **Run & review** and **See results** but neither **Pipelines** nor **Administration & billing**; V sees only **Home**, **Runs** and **Dashboards** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-01.04 | The second workspace is someone else's | As X, look at the workspace name and the menu | X's pages show X's own workspace; none of A's pipelines, forms or runs is listed anywhere | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-01.05 | The data is synthetic | Look through the files and forms you are about to use | No real person's name, record number, address or card number appears | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Record a result
1. Tick **☐ Pass** or **☐ Fail** in the last column.
2. Write the date beside the box, on the 24-hour clock if you note a time (2026-10-27 14:05).
3. Write a short note when anything was not exactly as expected, even on a pass: a slow page, a confusing word.
4. At the top of each area, write who tested it and on which day.

```A result line
QA-07.03 · Pass · 2026-10-27 · tested as A in Summit Valley · note: the step took 40 s
```

## When a check fails
1. **Keep what you see.** Do not refresh or retry yet.
2. **Take a screenshot** of the whole window, with the address bar. Do not include a password or a secret.
3. **Note the run.** If the check ran a pipeline, open the run's page (**Run & review › Runs**, then the run number) and
   copy its number and the message under its summary, word for word. The **Steps** tab marks the step that failed; see
   [A run's page](#run-page).
4. **Note the exact message** the screen showed, in quotes, and the time.
5. **Write what you expected and what you saw**, in one line each.
6. Then try once more. If it passes the second time, record a **Fail** with the note "passed on a second try": a check that
   fails now and then is still a fault.

```A failure note
QA-10.06 · Fail · 2026-10-27 15:40 · tested as A
Run: #2042 · Message: "Step 3 <report> failed: ..." · Screenshot: qa-10-06.png
Expected: the run retries from step 3. Saw: the retry was refused with "...".
```

> **Note:** A failure is not your fault and never a reason to change the data or the settings to make a check pass. Record
> it as it is.

## Example
A tester at Summit Valley Health System works through this chapter over two days. On day one, signed in as the Summit
Valley admin (A), she does areas 02 to 08; on day two, areas 09 to 18, switching to Dr. Anika Patel (R) for the review
checks and to the viewer (V) for the role checks. One check fails: she keeps the run number and the message, takes a
screenshot, and hands the sheet to the workspace's administrators.

articles.title: Test area 02: sign-in and two-factor
articles.summary: The first sign-in, wrong passwords and lockout, two-factor sign-in and recovery codes, idle sign-out and the sign-in history.
articles.who: Testers; most checks as the administrator (A) and a member (R or F)
articles.md:
These checks cover how people get in: a new account's first sign-in, what happens after wrong passwords, two-factor
sign-in with an authenticator app, recovery codes, idle sign-out, and the records the console keeps of every sign-in.

**Before you start:** an authenticator app on a phone (any of them), the accounts of [How to use this guide](#qa-guide),
and the workspace on the platform's default sign-in rules (**Administration › Sign-in security** shows **Use the
platform's defaults** with nothing of your own). Some checks lock or reset a test account: use F or a spare test account,
never A.

Tested by ______ on ______

![The sign-in page](qa-sign-in "Sign in: Username and Password, Sign in with your company, Request a workspace")

## The first sign-in
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-02.01 | The sign-in page | Open the console's address while signed out | The page shows **Username**, **Password** and **Sign in**, and **Request a workspace** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-02.02 | A new account gets a one-time password | As A, **Administration › Users** › **New user**: a new test person, **Password** left empty, **Role** Workspace member; **Create** | The person is listed as **Invited**; a one-time password is emailed to the address given | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-02.03 | The first sign-in asks for your own password | Sign in as the new person with the one-time password | **Your profile** opens with **Choose your own password.**; opening any other page brings you back to **Your profile** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-02.04 | The password rules are shown and enforced | On **Your profile**, type a short new password, then one that meets the rules; choose **Password rules** | The rules under **New password** tick as each is met; **Change password** works only when all are met; **Password rules** lists the minimum length (12 by default) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-02.05 | The one-time password stops working | Choose **Change password**, sign out, sign in with the emailed password | The emailed password is refused; the new one signs in | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-02.06 | A member cannot open sign-in security | As R, go to `/administration/security` | **This page isn't available to you**: the page is for administrators | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Wrong passwords and lockout
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-02.07 | A wrong password is refused | Sign in as F with a wrong password | The sign-in is refused and F stays on the sign-in page | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-02.08 | Lockout after repeated failures | Try a wrong password for F five times in a row (the default **Lock after**) | The account is locked; a right password is refused until the lock ends (15 minutes by default); A is told of the lock | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-02.09 | The administrator unlocks it | As A, **Administration › Users**: find F (its row shows **Locked**), row menu › **Unlock** | F can sign in at once with the right password | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-02.10 | The administrator resets a password | As A, F's row menu › **Reset password**, type one that meets the rules, **Reset password** | A notice offers **Copy password** for two minutes; F signs in with it and is asked to choose their own straight away | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Two-factor sign-in
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-02.11 | Turn on two-factor sign-in | As R, avatar › **My security** › **Set up two-factor login**; scan the QR code; type the code under **Code from the app**; **Turn on** | 10 recovery codes appear with **Copy** and **Download**; **Two-factor login** then reads **On**, with the date | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-02.12 | Sign in with a code | Sign out; sign in as R | After the password, **Two-factor login** asks for the code; the app's current code signs in | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-02.13 | A wrong code is refused | Sign in as R and type a wrong 6-digit code | The code is refused; a wrong code counts toward the lockout like a wrong password | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-02.14 | A recovery code works once | Sign in as R, choose **Use a recovery code instead**, use one code; then try the same code again | The first try signs in and **Recovery codes left** drops by one; the second try is refused | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-02.15 | New recovery codes replace the old | **My security** › **New recovery codes**, type the password, **Make new codes**; try an old code | A new set of 10 appears; an old code no longer signs in | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-02.16 | A profile can require it | As A, **Administration › Page access**: on F's profile tick **Require two-factor sign-in** and save; sign in as F | F's sign-in shows **Set up two-factor login** after the password; once set up, **Turn off** is not offered on F's **My security**. Untick the profile's box afterwards | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-02.17 | The administrator resets two-factor | As A, R's row menu › **Reset two-factor login**, confirm | R is signed out everywhere; R's old app codes and recovery codes stop working | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-02.18 | The users list shows who has it | As A, **Administration › Users**, the tiles **2FA on** and **2FA off** | Choosing a tile filters the list; R and F are under the right one | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Sessions and records
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-02.19 | Idle sign-out | As A, set **Sign out after** to 5 minutes and **Save rules**; sign in as F and leave the console alone | A warning comes a minute before; then F is signed out with **You were signed out because the console was not used for a while.** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-02.20 | A password change ends other sessions | Sign in as F in two browsers; change the password in one; use the other | The other session is signed out with **Your password was changed. Please sign in with the new password.** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-02.21 | Where you're signed in | As F, **My security** › **Where you're signed in**: **End session** on another session | That session is signed out at once; the list no longer shows it | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-02.22 | Sign-in history | As A, **Administration › Sign-in security** › **Sign-in history**; filter by outcome; **Export CSV** | The successful and failed sign-ins of QA-02.07 to 02.14 are listed with **When**, **Person**, **Outcome**, **Method** and **Reason**; the CSV holds the same rows | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-02.23 | Each person sees their own sign-ins | As R, **My security** › **Sign-in history** | Only R's own sign-ins are listed | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-02.24 | Back to the defaults | As A, **Use the platform's defaults** on **Sign-in security** | **Rules in force** reads the platform's defaults again (12 characters, lock after 5 for 15 minutes) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-02.25 | Another workspace's sign-ins are not shown | As X, open X's own **Sign-in security** › **Sign-in history**; search for R's address | None of A's workspace's sign-ins is listed | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

> **Note:** Single sign-on needs your company's identity provider and is not tested here. When your workspace uses it,
> add the checks for **Sign in with your company** at the end of this area, as described in
> [Single sign-on](#sec-sign-in--single-sign-on).

## Example
At Summit Valley the tester locks the front-desk test account on purpose (QA-02.08), sees the Summit Valley admin told of
it, and unlocks it from **Users** (QA-02.09). Dr. Anika Patel's test account turns on two-factor sign-in, uses one
recovery code, and makes a new set.

articles.title: Test area 03: people, access and teams
articles.summary: Roles, page access profiles, a page opened or withheld for one person, delegates, teams and their leads, and what a member may not open.
articles.who: Testers; most checks as the administrator (A), with R, V and F to see what changed
articles.popular: Check what each role may open
articles.md:
These checks cover who may open what: the two roles, page access profiles, a page or tab opened or withheld for one
person, delegates who grant access without being administrators, and teams. A page left out of someone's access is off
their menu, and the server refuses its data too, so several checks open a page by its address on purpose.

**Before you start:** the test accounts of [How to use this guide](#qa-guide), and one spare test member (called F2
below) you may deactivate. Changes to someone's access reach them at their next sign-in or when their session refreshes:
sign out and in again as that person before you judge a check.

Tested by ______ on ______

## Roles and people
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-03.01 | A person's page | As A, **Administration › Users**, F's row menu › **Edit** | F's page shows **Profile**, **Role and access**, **Sign-in security**, **Activity**, **Notifications** and **Danger zone** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-03.02 | What they can see | On F's page, read **What they can see** under **Role and access** | It lists F's menu: **Home** and **Forms** only | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-03.03 | Nobody changes their own role | As A, open your own page on **Users** | Your own role cannot be changed: the choice is not offered, or saving it is refused | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-03.04 | Nobody removes their own account | As A, look for **Deactivate** and **Delete** on your own row and page | Neither works on your own account: not offered, or refused with a reason | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-03.05 | Deactivate keeps the account | As A, F2's row menu › **Deactivate**, confirm; try to sign in as F2 | F2's row reads **Inactive**; F2 cannot sign in; F2's work and history are still listed | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-03.06 | Activate brings it back | As A, F2's row menu › **Activate**; sign in as F2 | F2 signs in again, with the same profile as before | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-03.07 | Find people by standing | As A, choose the tiles **Active**, **Invited**, **Administrators** and **Members** in turn | Each filters the list to those people; the counts match the rows shown | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-03.08 | A member cannot open Users | As R, go to `/administration/users` | **This page isn't available to you** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Page access profiles
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-03.09 | Make a profile | As A, **Administration › Page access** › **New profile**: **Profile name** `QA desk`, tick only **Forms** under **Pages this profile opens**; read **What this person will see**; **Create profile** | The preview shows **Home** and **Forms**; the new card is listed with 0 people | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-03.10 | Move a person onto it | On F2's page, **Page access profile** `QA desk`, **Save changes**; sign in as F2 | F2's menu holds **Home** and **Forms** only | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-03.11 | A held profile cannot be deleted | As A, `QA desk` card menu › **Delete** | It is refused while F2 holds it; after moving F2 back, **Delete** removes it | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-03.12 | A page outside your access | As F, go to `/runs/latest` | **… isn't part of your access**, naming F's profile, with **Request access** and **Dashboard** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-03.13 | Request access reaches the administrators | On that page choose **Request access** | The button reads **Asked**; A's bell has a new notification naming F and the page | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-03.14 | Check a person | As A, **Page access** › **Check a person**, pick V | It lists V's pages (Runs › Analytics, Dashboards) and anything opened or withheld for V alone | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

![A page outside your access](qa-not-your-access "A member who follows a link to a page their profile leaves out: the page says so and offers Request access")

## One person's pages and tabs
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-03.15 | Open a tab for one person, for a while | As A, **Page access** › **Grant pages and tabs** › **A person**: **Person** V, **For** 7 days, **Reason** `QA check`; tick **Runs by date** under **Queue** | The change applies at once; after signing in again, V's **Runs** shows the **By date** tab | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-03.16 | Withhold a tab | Same panel, **Person** R: untick the **Failed** tab of **Queue**; sign in as R and go to `/runs/failed` | The tab is off R's **Runs**; the address is refused | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-03.17 | Every change is recorded | As A, **Grant pages and tabs** › **Changes** | QA-03.15 and 03.16 are listed with **When**, **Who** (A), **What** (**Opened a tab**, **Withheld a page** or a tab), the **Person**, **Until** and **Why** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-03.18 | Back to their profile | **People × pages**: reset V's and R's exceptions | **Changes** lists **Back to their profile** for each; their menus are their profile's again | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Delegates
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-03.19 | Make a delegate | As A, **Grant pages and tabs** › **Delegates**: **Member who may grant** R, **To whom** **Only people I choose** (F), **For** 30 days, **Why** `QA check`; **Delegate** | The delegation is listed **Active** with its **Until** date | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-03.20 | What the delegate sees | Sign in as R, open **Administration › Page access** | Only **Grant access for the people you manage**, who delegated it and until when, **A person** and **Changes** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-03.21 | A delegate's limits | As R, try to grant F a page R does not hold, and to grant something to A or to R | R can grant only to F and only pages R holds; a grant to A or to R is not possible | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-03.22 | End a delegation | As A, **End** on the delegation | It stops at once; **Changes** lists **Ended a delegation**; R's **Page access** is gone at R's next sign-in | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Teams
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-03.23 | Make a team with a lead | As A, **Administration › Teams** › **New team**: **Name** `QA team`; **Make team**; in its panel add R as **Lead** and F as **Member** | The panel lists both; the tiles count one more team and one more lead | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-03.24 | A lead manages the members | As R, **Review › Approvals** › **My teams** › **See who is in your teams**: remove F, add F again | Both work; the team panel shows the change | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-03.25 | A member cannot change a team | As F (a member, not the lead), try to add or remove someone in `QA team` | The change is not possible: only the lead and administrators change a team | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-03.26 | Teams open no pages | Compare F's menu before and after joining `QA team` | The menu is the same: teams do not open pages | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-03.27 | Where a team is used, and archiving | As A, **New team** `QA old team`; in its panel read **Where it is used**; **Archive team** | **Where it is used** is empty for a new team; the team moves to the archived ones (shown with the state filter). Keep `QA team`: later areas use it | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Another workspace
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-03.28 | Another workspace's people are not listed | As X, **Administration › Users**, search for R's and F's addresses | Neither is found | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-03.29 | Another workspace's profiles and teams are not listed | As X, **Page access** and **Teams** | Only X's own profiles and teams; `QA desk` and `QA team` are not there | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Example
At Summit Valley the tester opens **Runs › By date** for the viewer for seven days with the reason `QA check`, sees it in
the viewer's menu after signing in again, and finds the grant under **Changes** with her name and reason. Owen Wright,
HR's delegate, can move people between existing profiles but is never offered an administrator.

articles.title: Test area 04: connections and API collections
articles.summary: Storage and database connections, API collections with secrets, tests, paging, versions and imports, data contracts, sources, and the addresses the console refuses.
articles.who: Testers; as the administrator (A), with V and X for the access and isolation checks
articles.md:
These checks cover how the workspace reaches data: storage connections, read-only database connections, API
collections (their sign-in, environments, tests, paging and versions), imports from Postman, data contracts and sources.
Secrets are never shown back, and addresses inside a private network are refused, whoever asks.

**Before you start:** a test bucket and keys for it (a sandbox or development bucket, never production), a read-only
test database user if your platform has a test database, a public keyless API to call (the examples use the public
FHIR sandbox `https://r4.smarthealthit.org`), and a small Postman v2.1 collection export.

Tested by ______ on ______

## Storage
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-04.01 | Add a storage connection | As A, **Connections › Storage** › **New storage connection**: **Provider**, **Name**, **Alias** `qa-test-s3`, bucket and keys; **Create** | The connection is listed **Active**; **Credentials** reads **Stored** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-04.02 | Test it | Its menu › **Test connection** | **Last test** reads **OK** with the time; the **Tested OK** tile counts it | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-04.03 | The secret is never shown back | Open it with **Edit** | The secret key field is empty; saving with it empty keeps the stored key (test again: **OK**) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-04.04 | A bad alias is refused | **New storage connection** with **Alias** `qa test/1` | Refused: letters, numbers, `.`, `_` and `-` only | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-04.05 | Wrong keys fail the test | Edit the connection with a wrong secret key; **Test connection** | **Last test** reads **Failed**; hovering says why; the **Failing** tile counts it. Put the right key back | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-04.06 | Switch a connection off | **Edit** › **Status** **Inactive** | It stays listed as inactive and is not counted **In service** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-04.07 | The Storage tab is the administrators' | As V, go to `/connections/storage` | The page is refused | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Databases
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-04.08 | Add a read-only database connection | As A, **Connections › Databases** › **New connection**: **Host**, **Port**, **Database**, **User**, **TLS**, **Password**; **Test connection**; **Create** | The dialog says the test worked; the connection is listed; the password is never shown again (**Replace** / **Keep**) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-04.09 | Only a reading query runs | **Connections › Sources** › **New source**, **Reads from** **Database**, query `DELETE FROM orders`; **Test connection**, **Preview** | Refused before it runs: one statement starting with `SELECT`, `WITH`, `VALUES` or `TABLE` | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-04.10 | A reading query previews | Change the query to `SELECT * FROM orders` (or a table you have); **Preview** | The first rows are shown, capped; nothing is written to the database | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## API collections
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-04.11 | Make a collection | As A, **Connections › API collections** › **New collection**: **Name** `QA public APIs`, **Sensitivity** **Public**, **Default auth** **None**; **Create** | The collection opens on its **Overview**, version **v1** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-04.12 | An environment with a secret | **New environment** `Sandbox`, **Default** ticked; variable `baseUrl` = `https://r4.smarthealthit.org`; variable `token` = `abc`, **Secret** ticked; **Create** | `token` shows **••• configured**; its value is never shown, even to A | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-04.13 | A plain credential is refused | **Add API**; on **Headers** add `Authorization` = `Bearer abc` (a plain value); **Save** | Refused: a credential must be a `{{variable}}` | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-04.14 | Add and test an API | **Add API**: **Method** GET, **URL** `{{baseUrl}}/Patient`; **Save & test** | The test line reads **OK**, `HTTP 200`, the time and size; **Body** shows the answer | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-04.15 | Paging | On its **Settings**, **Paging** **Next URL in the answer**, **Next URL at** `$.link[?(@.relation=='next')].url`, **Items at** `$.entry`, **Most pages** `3`; **Save & test** | The test line reads "N items over 3 pages" and says it stopped at the page cap with more to fetch | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-04.16 | A private address is blocked | Add an API with **URL** `http://192.168.1.40/fhir`; **Test** | **Blocked**: nothing is sent | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-04.17 | Each save is a version | Save the API again with a small change; open **History** | The collection is at the next version; **History** lists both, the newest **current** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-04.18 | Pin a source to a version | **Connections › Sources** › **New source**, **Reads from** **API**: the collection, the API, the older **Version**; **Save**; then save the API once more | **Used by** on the collection shows the source pinned to the older version, with **behind** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-04.19 | A used API cannot be deleted | Try to delete the API the source uses | Refused; the console lists what uses it and the version each one pinned | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-04.20 | Import a Postman collection | **Import**, **Postman**, pick the `.json` export; **Import** | The **Import report** counts **Imported**, **Converted**, **Needs a look** and **Skipped**; **Open collection** opens a new collection with **Source** Postman | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-04.21 | An import never changes an existing collection | Import the same file again | A second, separate collection is made; the first is unchanged | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Data contracts and sources
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-04.22 | Make a contract from a sample | As A, **Connections › Data contracts** › **New from sample**: **Name** `qa_lab_result`, paste `{"loinc":"2345-7","value":5.4,"result_id":"R1"}`; **Propose schema**; tick **Required** on all three; **Save v1** | The contract is listed with **Active** and **Latest** v1 | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-04.23 | A payload that breaks it | Open it; **Validate a payload**: `{"value":"high"}`; **Validate** | Each problem is listed by **Path**, **Rule** and **Message** (the missing `loinc` and `result_id`, `value` not a number); nothing is recorded | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-04.24 | A new version waits until activated | **New version from sample**, **Save version**; then **Activate** it | Before **Activate**, checks still use v1; after, v2 is active and v1 reads **Retired** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-04.25 | What your pipelines read | **Connections › Sources** › **What your pipelines read** | Each place a pipeline reads is listed with **Kind** and **Read by**, each pipeline a link | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Access and isolation
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-04.26 | A viewer has no Connections | As V, look for **Connections** in the menu, then go to `/connections/api-collections` | Not in the menu; the address is refused | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
