| QA-04.27 | Another workspace cannot see them | As X, open **Connections**: Storage, Databases, API collections, Data contracts | None of A's connections, collections or contracts is listed | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-04.28 | Another workspace cannot open one by its address | As A, copy the address of `QA public APIs`; as X, open it | The collection does not open for X; none of its APIs or variables is shown (not yet verified) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Example
At Summit Valley the tester's test of **FHIR: patients** reads **OK**, `HTTP 200`, 100 items over four pages, and a test
against the hospital's own `http://192.168.1.40/fhir` reads **Blocked**. The `lab_result` contract refuses a result
without its LOINC code by path.

articles.title: Test area 05: documents
articles.summary: Document types and starters, upload and Email-in, duplicates, the file drop, review and corrections, rules, bulk review, approved data and what an approval starts.
articles.who: Testers; as the administrator (A) and a reviewer whose access includes Review › Documents (R), with F, V and X for access and isolation
articles.md:
These checks follow a document from the moment it arrives to its approved data: the types it is matched to, the ways it
comes in, how it is read, how a person checks and decides it, and what its approval starts. A model's reading is a draft:
nothing reaches approved data until a person passes it, or the type's auto-approve line does with every key field
confirmed by its lookup.

**Before you start:** a few synthetic PDFs: two referral letters, one invoice whose lines do not add up to its subtotal,
and a copy of one referral under another file name. An email account you may send from, if your platform has Email-in.
A small CSV, a synthetic photo (JPEG) and a file with a wrong extension (a text file renamed `photo.jpg`) for the file
drop.

Tested by ______ on ______

## Types and intake
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-05.01 | Add types from the starters | As A, **Documents › Document types** › **Add from starters**: tick **Referral** and **Invoice**; **Add** | Both are listed as **This workspace**, **Active**; opening the starters again shows them **Added** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.02 | A type's key is fixed | **New document type**: **Name** `QA wound form`, **Key** `qa_wound_form`, a few fields; **Save**; open it with **Edit** | The key cannot be changed; **Save as the next version** makes v2 and **Versions** lists both | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.03 | Upload documents | **Documents › Intake › Upload** › **Upload documents**: drop the two referrals; **Upload** | The dialog says what became of each; **What arrived** lists them as **Taken**, channel **Upload**, each linked to its document | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.04 | They are read and matched | **Documents › Documents in** | Each shows its **Type** (**Referral**), **Fields** with how many are **to check**, **Confidence** and **State** (**In review** or **Auto-approved**) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.05 | The same file twice is kept once | Upload the copy of a referral under another file name | **What arrived** lists it as **Duplicate**, naming the earlier document; no second document is made | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.06 | Email-in | **Intake › Email-in**: **Turn on** if needed; copy the address; mail a referral PDF to it | **What arrived** lists the attachment with channel **Email**, the sender and the subject | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.07 | A new Email-in address shuts out the old | **New address**; mail the old address again | The workspace has a new address; the mail to the old one makes no document | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## The file drop
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-05.08 | Set it up | As A, **Intake › File drop** › **Set up the file drop** (or **Change**): pick a storage connection; **Turn on the file drop** | **Settings** names the connection, **Where files land** (`intake/<date>/<arrival>-<file name>`) and the **Size limit** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.09 | Drop files | Drop the CSV and the photo on **Drop files here** | **This session's uploads** shows each **Uploaded** with its SHA-256; **Arrivals** lists them with **Uploaded by** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.10 | A file whose contents do not match its name is refused | Drop the text file renamed `photo.jpg` | **Refused**, with why; it is not stored and not in **Arrivals** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.11 | The file drop is not read as a document | Look at **Documents in** after QA-05.09 | The dropped files are not listed there: the file drop only stores files for pipelines | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Review and decide
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-05.12 | The queue | As R, **Review › Documents** | The documents not approved on their own are listed, oldest first, with **To check**, **Least sure**, **Waiting since** and **Claimed** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.13 | Claim a document | Open one; **Claim** | **Claimed** shows R; as A, the same document is read-only, **Claimed by** R | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.14 | A field shows where it was read | Choose a field flagged **check** | Its box is drawn on the page; ↓ and ↑ move between fields | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.15 | Correct and keep the correction | Type over a value; **Save corrections** | **Corrections** lists the field, what it was, what it is now, R and the time | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.16 | A reject needs a reason | **Reject** (or R); leave **Why** empty; then type a reason and **Reject** again | It cannot be sent without a reason; with one, the document reads **Rejected** and the reason is kept | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.17 | Approve | Open the other referral; **Approve & next** (or A) | It reads **Approved**; the next document opens | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.18 | The shortcuts do nothing while typing | Click into a field and type the letter `a` | The letter is typed; nothing is approved | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.19 | A rule that fails | As A, on **Invoice** add the rule **A table column adds up to a field** (lines to subtotal), **Save as the next version**; upload the invoice that does not add up; open it as R | **Rule check** shows the rule with a cross and **fails**, with its message | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Bulk review
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-05.20 | Bulk approve is off by the policy | As A, **Administration › Data policies** › **Bulk review**: **Allow bulk approve of documents** off; **Save review policy**. As R, tick two documents, **Approve** | Each is skipped with *Bulk approve is off in this workspace* | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.21 | Bulk approve, rules failing left out | Turn it on (with **Include documents whose rules fail** off). As R, tick several documents including the invoice; **Approve** | The panel says how many will be approved and skips the invoice with its reason; a comment is optional; the button names the count (**Approve 3**) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.22 | Over 25 needs the count typed | Select more than 25 documents (or **Select all matching**); **Approve** | The panel asks you to type the number before it can be sent | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.23 | A bulk reject needs a comment | Tick two; **Reject** with no comment | It cannot be sent; with a comment, each is rejected and lists the comment | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Approved data and what it starts
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-05.24 | The approved row | **Documents › Approved data**, pick **Referral** | A row for the approved referral, **Approved** **By a reviewer**, with R's correction in its value | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.25 | Download it | **CSV**, then **JSON Lines** | Both files hold every approved row of the type | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.26 | A rejected document is not there | Look for the rejected referral | It has no row in approved data | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.27 | What a type's approval starts | **Document types**, the column **When approved, starts…** | **Nothing yet** for a type no schedule starts on; after [QA-08.16](#qa-triggers), the schedule's name, linked | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Choice words a page writes
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-05.31 | A lab printout's H, L and N | **Document types**, the lab result type › **Edit**: on the **Flag** column, **Options written as** `High = H; Low = L; Normal = N`; **Save as the next version**; add a lab PDF whose flags are printed `H`, `L` and `N` | The flags read **High**, **Low** and **Normal**, each pointing at its letter on the page, with no "Not one of" problem | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.32 | A word for two options is refused | **Options written as** `High = H; Low = H`; **Save** | Refused: the word `H` is given to both High and Low | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |


## Auto-approve and key fields
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-05.33 | Confidence alone never approves | As A, read a clean **Insurance card** with every value sure (no lookup on its type) | **State** **In review**; the document says **Not approved on its own: ...** with what is missing | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.34 | The type says why auto-approve is off | **Document types**, open **Insurance card** | **Auto-approve is off: every document of this type goes to review**, naming each key field (**Payer**, **Member ID**) with no lookup; the list shows **Off: every document reviewed** under **Auto-approve at** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.35 | Key fields with lookups turn it on | **Edit**: add a **Lookup** on **Payer** and on **Member ID** against a payer list in your bucket; **Save**; read a card whose payer and member ID are on the list | The panel says **Documents are approved on their own when...**; the card is **Approved**, **On its own** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.36 | A key value not on the list waits | Read a card whose payer is not on the list | **In review**; the payer says **Not in** the list | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.37 | A table's column cannot be a key field | **Edit** a type with a table | The **Key** box is on the document's fields only, never on a table's columns | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Access and isolation
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-05.28 | No Documents for the front desk | As F, go to `/documents/in` and `/review/documents` | Both are refused (**… isn't part of your access**) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.29 | Another workspace cannot open a document | As A, copy the address of a document's review screen; as X, open it | **This document isn't here**: it may have been removed, or the link belongs to another workspace | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-05.30 | Another workspace's lists | As X, **Documents in**, **Review › Documents**, **Approved data** | None of A's documents is listed | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Example
At Summit Valley the referral `referral-upload-8.pdf` arrives once as **Taken**, and the same file uploaded again is
listed as **Duplicate**, naming the first: no second document is made. Greta Fischer rejects a referral that has no
referral date, with her reason, and approves the clinic's corrected letter.

articles.title: Test area 06: forms and share links
articles.summary: Build, publish and fill in a form, show or require a field when, submissions and their export, what a submission starts, and share links with their limits.
articles.who: Testers; the administrator (A) builds, the front desk (F) fills in, with R, V and X for access, share links and isolation
articles.popular: Test a form's share link
articles.md:
These checks cover forms from both sides: the administrator who builds one and decides what a submission starts, and
the person at the front desk who only fills it in. They also cover **share links**: a link that opens one form for
someone who sees nothing else, with an expiry, a cap on submissions, and an option to require signing in.

**Before you start:** the front-desk account F (a profile that opens **Forms** only), and a private browser window with
nobody signed in, for the share-link checks. Use made-up answers only: a patient `Test Patient`, MRN `SV-000999`.

Tested by ______ on ______

## Build and publish
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-06.01 | Make a form | As A, **Forms** › **New form**; **Settings**: **Name** `QA intake`; on **Build** add **Text** (MRN, **Required**), **Choice** (Payer: `Self-pay`, `Medicare`, `Other`), **Text** (Member ID), **Yes / no** (Any allergies?), **Long text** (Allergies), **Signature**; **Save** | The form is saved as **Draft** with its six fields | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-06.02 | A field's key rules | Give a field the **Key** `submitted_by`, then `1mrn` | Both are refused: lower-case letters, digits and `_`, starting with a letter, and not a name the submission uses itself | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-06.03 | Show a field when | **Logic**: Allergies **Show only when** Any allergies? **is** **Yes**; Member ID **Also required when** Payer **is not** `Self-pay`; **Save** | The tab reads **Logic (2)**; on **Build** each of the two fields says it has a rule | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-06.04 | Preview the rules | **Preview**: answer Any allergies? **No**, then **Yes**; Payer `Self-pay`, then `Medicare` | Allergies appears only on **Yes**; Member ID becomes required only when the payer is not Self-pay; nothing is sent | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-06.05 | A draft takes no submissions | As F, open **Forms** | `QA intake` is not offered to fill in while it is a draft | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-06.06 | Publish and activate | As A, **Publish**; set **Status** **Active** in **Settings**; **Save** | The form reads **Published** with its version, and **Active** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Fill in
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-06.07 | The front desk sees the active form | As F, open **Forms** | `QA intake` is listed and its name is a link; F's menu holds nothing but **Home** and **Forms** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-06.08 | A required field stops the form | Open it; leave MRN empty; **Submit** | It is not sent; the MRN field says it is needed | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-06.09 | Sign and submit | Answer every field; sign in the box and choose **Use this signature**; **Submit** | The page says **Submitted**, with **Fill in another** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-06.10 | The front desk cannot read submissions | As F, go to `/forms/submissions` | Refused (**… isn't part of your access**) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-06.11 | The front desk cannot build | As F, look for **New form**, and try to open the form's builder | F cannot make or change a form | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Submissions and what they start
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-06.12 | The submission is listed | As A, **Forms › Submissions**, pick `QA intake` | A row with **Submitted by** F, the time, **Status** **Received** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-06.13 | Read it | **View** on the row | Each answer under its label; the signature as a file; the line under the answers names the form's version | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-06.14 | An old submission keeps its version | Change the form (add a field), save; **View** the first submission again | It is still shown with the fields of the version it answered | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-06.15 | Export | **Export CSV** | Every submission of the form, one row each | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-06.16 | A submission starts a pipeline | In **Settings**, **When submitted, start**: a schedule **Only when started** (see [QA-08](#qa-triggers)); **Save**; as F, submit again | The forms list shows the schedule under **Starts**; the new submission's **Status** reads **Run started** #N, linked to its run | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-06.29 | A photo field feeds an image step as it is | A form with a **File** field `photo`; a pipeline it starts with **Measure image** (or **AI prompt** with an image) whose **Image key column** is `photo` -- the field itself, not `photo_key`; submit with a photo | The run measures (or describes) the photo; no "is not a png or jpg image" with the field's text | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-06.17 | A submission starts a workflow | In **Settings**, **Approval**: a published workflow (see [QA-11](#qa-approvals)); **Save**; submit again | The submission shows its **Stage** and **Approval** (**Pending**) with **Open request** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Share links
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-06.18 | Sharing by link starts off | As A, the form's **Settings** › **Share by link** | It reads **Sharing by link is off for this workspace** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-06.19 | Make a single-use link | Turn sharing on; **Label** `QA desk tablet`, **Works for** 1 day, **Submissions** **One (single use)**, **Only signed-in members** unticked; **Make link**; **Copy** | The link is shown once; the list shows it with **Status**, **Used** 0 and **Expires** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-06.20 | The link opens the form and nothing else | In the private window (nobody signed in), open the link; fill in and submit | Only the form is shown, with no menu; it is sent; **Forms › Submissions** lists it | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-06.21 | A single-use link works once | Open the same link again | It no longer opens the form: **This link no longer works** (not yet verified) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-06.22 | A link for signed-in members only | Make a link with **Only signed-in members** ticked; open it in the private window | **Sign in to fill this in** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-06.23 | Another workspace's member cannot use it | Open that link signed in as X | **This form is for another workspace** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-06.24 | Revoke a link | **Revoke** on a link; open it | **Link revoked.**; the link no longer opens the form (not yet verified: which message it shows) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-06.25 | Sharing off stops every link | Turn sharing by link off; open any link of this workspace | No link opens the form; the setting says no link opens anything now | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Access and isolation
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-06.26 | A viewer has no forms | As V, go to `/forms/builder` | Refused | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-06.27 | Another workspace cannot open the form | As A, copy the address of the form's **Fill in** page; as X, open it | **Form not found.** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-06.28 | Rebuild dataset files | As A, if the form keeps a dataset: row menu › **Rebuild dataset files** › **Rebuild files** | The dialog says where the files are written; no answer changes | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

> **Privacy:** Do not use a share link without **Only signed-in members** for a form that asks for patient or personal
> data unless your organisation has approved it. In this test the answers are made up.

## Example
At Summit Valley the tester's front-desk account fills in `QA intake` with a made-up patient and signs it; Forms ›
Submissions lists it as **Received**, by name. A single-use link opened in a private window takes one submission, and
the Meridian administrator opening a signed-in-only link is told **This form is for another workspace**.

articles.title: Test area 07: pipelines and steps
articles.summary: Make a pipeline, add and set up steps, try it on sample rows, validate, save versions, run it once, placeholders and run parameters, and the steps that are refused.
articles.who: Testers; the administrator (A) builds, with R, V and X for access and isolation
articles.popular: Test a pipeline end to end on sample rows
articles.md:
These checks build one small pipeline by hand and run it, so every number is known in advance: three wards go in, their
occupancy is worked out, the full ones are kept, and a file is saved. Then they check versions, the definition as text,
placeholders, run parameters, and what may not be added.

**Before you start:** a storage connection (from [QA-04](#qa-connections)). Copy the sample rows below exactly.

```Sample rows for QA-07
[
  { "ward": "4B", "beds": 20, "occupied": 18 },
  { "ward": "ICU", "beds": 12, "occupied": 12 },
  { "ward": "5A", "beds": 24, "occupied": 10 }
]
```

Tested by ______ on ______

## Make it
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-07.01 | New pipeline offers three ways | As A, **Build › Pipelines** › **New pipeline** | **Describe it to the AI Assistant**, **Add steps yourself** and **Copy an existing pipeline** are offered side by side | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-07.02 | Make an empty pipeline | Under **Add steps yourself**, **Name** `QA occupancy`; **Create and add steps** | The pipeline opens on **Steps**, empty; the overview strip says what is missing | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-07.03 | Sample rows first | **Test with sample**; paste the sample rows; **Use these rows** | A **Sample rows** step is first, holding three rows; the console checks the pipeline at once | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-07.04 | Add a Compute step | **Add step from the Task Registry…**, type `compute`, pick **Compute**; **Formulas**: **Column** `pct`, **Formula** `round(occupied * 100 / beds, 1)`; **Apply** | The step is added at the end; nothing is saved yet (the save bar says there are unsaved changes) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-07.05 | Add a Filter step | Add **Filter**: **Conditions** **Column** `pct`, **Is** `gte`, **Value** `80`; **Apply** | The step is in the draft after **Compute** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-07.06 | Add a Save File step | Add **Save File**: **File name** `qa-occupancy-{{date}}.csv`, **Format** `csv`; **Apply** | The overview strip's **Outputs** reads **Set** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-07.07 | A bad step key is refused | Open a step's panel; change **Key** to `Full Wards` | Refused: lower case letters, digits and `_` only | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-07.08 | Validate | **Validate** in the save bar | "The definition is valid." | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-07.09 | A problem is placed on its step | Clear the **File name** of **Save File**; **Validate** | The bar counts one problem; **Save File** shows a red **Problems** pill with the message. Put the name back | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Save and run
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-07.10 | Save makes a version | **Save** | The version pill reads **v1**; **History** lists v1 with **Saved** and **By** A, marked **Current** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-07.11 | Run it once | **Run now** (it gives the pipeline an on-demand schedule) | The run panel lists each step with its status; **Rows in → out**: Sample rows 3, Compute 3 → 3, Filter 3 → 2, Save File 2 → 2; the run is **Completed** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-07.12 | The file is named from the date | Open the run's page › **Outputs** | `qa-occupancy-` and today's date (Chicago) `.csv`, kept **With the run**; **View** shows wards 4B (90) and ICU (100) only | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-07.13 | A change is a new version; the run keeps its own | Change the filter's value to `95`; **Save**; open the run of QA-07.11 again | The pill reads **v2**; the earlier run still shows two rows and names the version it ran | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-07.14 | Discard drops unsaved changes | Change a step; **Discard** | Every tab is back as saved | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-07.15 | The definition as text | Open **YAML**, then **JSON** | Both show the same steps with their keys, tasks and settings as the builder | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-07.16 | Invalid JSON is not applied | On **JSON**, delete a closing brace; leave the tab | The builder keeps the steps it had and says why | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-07.17 | The flow map | **Flow** beside **List** | Each step is a box with arrows where its rows come from; clicking a box opens its panel | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Placeholders, parameters and settings
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-07.18 | A run parameter | **Settings** › **Run parameters** › **Add a parameter**: **Name** `min_pct`, **Type** **Number**, **Default** `80`; in the filter, **Value** `{{param.min_pct}}`; **Save**; run | The run keeps 4B and ICU, as with the plain value | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-07.19 | An unknown placeholder stays as written | Set **File name** to `qa-{{nosuch}}.csv`; **Save**; run | The kept file is named with `{{nosuch}}` left as written, so the mistake shows | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-07.20 | Data sensitivity shows on the list | **Settings** › **Data sensitivity** **Internal**; **Save**; open **Build › Pipelines** | The **Data** column of `QA occupancy` reads Internal | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-07.21 | A copy is independent | **New pipeline** › **Copy an existing pipeline**: `QA occupancy`, **Copy it**; change a step in the copy and save; open the original | The copy starts **Inactive**; the original's steps are unchanged | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-07.22 | A pipeline in use cannot be deleted | On **Build › Pipelines**, `QA occupancy`'s **⋮** menu | **Delete** is not offered while a schedule runs it ("In use") | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## What may not be added
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-07.23 | Write Database is switched off | **Add step from the Task Registry…**, type `database` | **Read Database** is offered; **Write Database** is marked **(disabled)**, its hint: writing to a database is not part of this release, database connections are read-only | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-07.24 | An input too large for a calling step | Add **Call API** after the sample rows, with any saved API request, **Send** `each` and **At most calls** `2`; run; then remove the step | The step fails before any call is made: the input needs 3 calls and the step makes at most 2; the message says so | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Access and isolation
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-07.25 | A viewer cannot open pipelines | As V, go to `/pipelines/list` | **Pipelines isn't part of your access**, with **Request access** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-07.26 | A member cannot change a pipeline | As a member whose profile opens **Pipelines** (if your workspace has one), open `QA occupancy` | The steps can be read but not saved: building and changing pipelines is the administrators' | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-07.27 | Another workspace cannot open it | As A, copy the pipeline's address; as X, open it | **Pipeline #N does not exist or was deleted.** (not yet verified from another workspace) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-07.28 | Another workspace's list | As X, **Build › Pipelines**, search `QA occupancy` | Not found | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Example
At Summit Valley the tester's `QA occupancy` run reads 3 rows, keeps 4B and ICU, and saves
`qa-occupancy-2026-10-27.csv` with the run. Changing the filter to 95 saves v2; the first run still names v1 and still
shows two rows.

articles.title: Test area 08: schedules and triggers
articles.summary: Timetables and cron lines, Run now and Run with…, pausing and skipping, starting on a file, a form or an approved document, one run at a time, and backfills.
articles.who: Testers; the administrator (A), with V and X for access and isolation
articles.md:
These checks cover everything that starts a run: a timetable, **Run now**, **Run with…** with its own values, a file in
the inbox, a form's submission, an approved document, and a backfill over past days. A schedule never runs over itself:
a start that comes while its last run is still going is refused or recorded, never lost silently.

**Before you start:** the pipeline `QA occupancy` of [QA-07](#qa-pipelines), with its run parameter `min_pct`. The file
drop set up ([QA-05.08](#qa-documents)). Two small CSV files named `qa-in-1.csv` and `other.csv`. Times on the schedule
editor are server time (Chicago) on the 24-hour clock.

Tested by ______ on ______

## Timetables
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-08.01 | Make a daily schedule | As A, **Schedules & triggers** › **New schedule**: **Schedule name** `QA daily`, **Pipeline** `QA occupancy`, **On a timetable**, **Daily**, every 1 day at 06:00 | **What you will get** says it in a sentence; **Next runs** lists the next five, each at 06:00 | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-08.02 | A cron line | Change **How often** to **Advanced (cron)**, **Cron expression** `30 8 * * 1-5` | **Next runs** lists only weekdays, each at 08:30 | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-08.03 | Save it inactive | Turn the switch at the foot off; **Create schedule** | The schedule is listed and not active; **Run now** is not offered ("Activate this schedule to run it") | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-08.04 | Activate and Deactivate | **⋮** › **Activate**; later **Deactivate** across a slot time | Slots that pass while it is off are recorded as **Missed** and not replayed on **Activate** (not yet verified) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-08.05 | Skip the next run asks first | **⋮** › **Skip next run** | It asks first, naming the run; after confirming, that run is recorded as **Skipped** and later runs stay on time | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-08.06 | Retries and priority | Open **Advanced**: **Priority** `10`, then `3`; **Attempts** `11`, then `2` | 10 and 11 are refused (priority 1 to 9, attempts 1 to 10); 3 and 2 save | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Run now and Run with…
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-08.07 | Run now | **⋮** › **Run now** | The run is queued; the row's **Run status** follows it to **Completed** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-08.08 | Not twice at once | Choose **Run now** and, while that run is queued or running, try again | **Run now** is not offered, or the start is refused with *A job can't be run while its last run is still in flight* | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-08.09 | Run with… its own values | **⋮** › **Run with…**: `min_pct` `95`; **Run** | The run keeps one ward (ICU); the schedule's default stays 80 and the next run uses it | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-08.10 | A bad value is refused before the run | **Run with…**: `min_pct` `high` | Refused before anything starts: the value must be a number | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-08.11 | Run several at once | Tick two schedules; **Run selected**; confirm | Each starts its own run; a schedule already queued or running could not be ticked | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Starting on arrival
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-08.12 | A file arrives | Open `QA daily`; **Also starts when** › **A file arrives**, **Which files** `qa-*.csv`, **Files per run** `1`; save | **What you will get** says "Also when a file arrives in the inbox matching …" | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-08.13 | A matching file starts a run | Drop `qa-in-1.csv` on **File drop** | A run starts; on **Runs › Latest** its **Started by** is **File arrived** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-08.14 | Another file does not | Drop `other.csv` | No run starts for it | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-08.15 | A form starts it | Link `QA intake` to this schedule ([QA-06.16](#qa-forms)); submit the form | A run starts, **Started by** **Form submitted** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-08.16 | An approved document starts it | **Also starts when** › **A document is approved**, **Which documents** **Referral**; save; approve a referral in **Review › Documents** | A run starts, **Started by** **Document approved**; **Document types** shows the schedule under **When approved, starts…** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-08.17 | A rejected document starts nothing | Reject a referral | No run starts | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Backfills
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-08.18 | The preview | `QA daily`'s **⋮** › **Backfill…**: **Dates** 7 days, **One run per** **Day**, **At once** 2 | **Preview** says how many periods **will run** and are **already done, skipped**, lists each date, and (for A) shows a **Cost estimate** or says there is nothing to estimate from | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-08.19 | Start and follow | **Start: 7 days** | **Runs › Backfills** shows it with its range, 2 at once, a bar of done, failed and running, and its status | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-08.20 | Pause, resume, cancel | **Pause**, then **Resume**; start another and **Cancel** it | Each takes effect; the cancelled one is listed under **Cancelled** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-08.21 | An inactive schedule cannot be backfilled | **Deactivate** `QA daily`; **Backfill…** | The preview says *The schedule is switched off; switch it on to backfill it.* | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Access and isolation
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-08.22 | A viewer has no schedules | As V, go to `/pipelines/schedules` | Refused | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-08.23 | Another workspace's list | As X, **Schedules & triggers**, search `QA daily` | Not found | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-08.24 | Another workspace's file drop starts nothing here | As X, drop a file named `qa-in-2.csv` on X's own file drop | No run of A's `QA daily` starts | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Example
At Summit Valley **Denials by month (backfill a quarter)** backfilled 1 to 25 October, one run per day, three at once:
25 runs, all completed. **Four runs at once** shows the rule of one run per schedule: the first start ran, the other
three were refused while it was in flight and ran in turn.

articles.title: Test area 09: AI
articles.summary: Model connections, prompts and their tries, AI steps, the AI Assistant and its hard rules, Ask your data, the file chat and transcription; every answer a DRAFT.
articles.who: Testers; the administrator (A), with R, V and X for access and isolation
articles.popular: Test the AI Assistant's hard rules
articles.md:
These checks cover every place the console asks a model: prompts, AI steps in pipelines, the AI Assistant, Ask your data,
the file chat and transcription. Four rules hold everywhere and are tested on purpose:

- **A model's answer is a DRAFT** for a person to check, never a decision.
- **The AI Assistant refuses to write to a database.** Write Database is switched off: the assistant says so and offers
  a file, a bucket or a webhook instead; it never offers to go ahead.
- **It never invents a file, a collection or a column.** When you name one the workspace does not have, it says so and
  draws nothing that reads it.
- **It asks before it acts.** Anything that changes something comes back as a card to confirm.

**Before you start:** a working model connection (a local model is fine; answers may take a minute). A synthetic file in
storage, such as `qa/orders.csv` with columns `order_id`, `status`, `amount`. A short synthetic recording (`.mp3` or
`.m4a`) for transcription. AI calls are billed like any other work, tries included.

Tested by ______ on ______

## Models and prompts
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-09.01 | Test a connection | As A, **Settings › Model connections**, the connection's **Test connection** | **Last test** reads passed and lists the models the provider offers | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-09.02 | A key is never shown back | **Edit connection** | The key field is empty; leaving it blank keeps the stored key | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-09.03 | The caps' limits | **Edit connection**: **Calls in flight** `0`, then `65`, then `1` | 0 and 65 are not accepted (1 to 64); 1 saves | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-09.04 | Write a prompt and try it | **Build › Pipelines › Prompts** › **New prompt**: **Name** `QA summary (DRAFT)`, a **Message template** with `{{note}}`, a **Sample value**; **Run** under **Try it** | The answer appears with the tokens in and out and the time; **Show rendered input** shows exactly what was sent; **Recent runs** lists the try | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-09.05 | A JSON answer outside its schema is held | Set **The answer** to **JSON object** with an **Output schema** whose `stage` has `enum` `["1","2"]`; ask for something the model cannot fit (for example "answer stage 7"); **Run** | After one repair round an answer that still does not fit shows **Held for review**, with the held answer; it is never used | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-09.06 | Versions | **Save as v2**, then **Save & activate** | v2 is kept without becoming current until **Save & activate**; the list shows the active version | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-09.07 | An inactive connection stops AI | **Make inactive** on the default connection; try the prompt and Ask your data; then **Make active** | While inactive, both are refused; after **Make active**, they work again | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## AI in a pipeline
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-09.08 | Add an AI step | In a copy of `QA occupancy`, add **AI prompt** after **Filter**: **Prompt** `QA summary (DRAFT)`, **Answer column** `summary`; **Apply**; **Save**; **Run now** | The run completes; its page has an **AI answers** tab listing two answers with the prompt, its version, **Answered**, the time and the tokens | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-09.09 | Too many rows are refused before any call | Set the AI step's **At most rows** to `1`; run | The step fails before any call is made, saying the input has more rows than it may send | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-09.10 | The run's cost includes the model | As A, the run's **What this run cost** | The model tokens in and out are on the run's cost | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## The AI Assistant
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-09.11 | What it may reach | As A, **Build › AI Assistant** › **New chat**; open the **Context** tab | **Workspace** is A's, **Acting as** A; **Data policy**, **Tools allowed** and **Asks first for** are listed | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-09.12 | It designs; nothing is saved yet | Type the copy block below; send | A flow is drawn on **Flow**; its label reads **Ready to create** or says what to fill; **Build › Pipelines** has no new pipeline | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-09.13 | Create once, then update | Fill what it asks; **Create pipeline**, confirm; then ask "also keep only amounts over 100" | The pipeline is created as v1; afterwards the button reads **Update pipeline** and saves v2; no second pipeline is made | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-09.14 | It refuses a database write | Send: "Write these rows into the orders table in the store database." | It says writing to a database can't be done here (the step for it is switched off), offers a file, a bucket or a webhook instead, and does not offer to proceed; no step that writes a database is drawn | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-09.15 | It never invents a file | Send: "Design a pipeline that reads `qa/does-not-exist.csv` and saves it as a CSV." | It names the file as not found in this workspace and draws no step reading it | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-09.16 | It never invents a collection | Send: "Call the Quest Diagnostics collection for each order." | It says there is no such API collection in this workspace and names what it can do instead | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-09.17 | A column the input does not have | Ask for a flow over `qa/orders.csv` that filters on `customer_city` (a column the file does not have) | The step that names it gets a warning (the label says *Check N warnings*), with the column it most likely means | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-09.18 | It asks before it acts | Ask it to run the pipeline of QA-09.13 | A card **Confirm before it runs** names the tool and what it will do; nothing runs until you choose **Run pipeline**; **Cancel** runs nothing | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-09.19 | It answers about runs from what you may open | As R, ask "Which runs failed this week?" | The answer lists only runs R may open; **Tool calls** shows the tools it used | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-09.20 | A member cannot create a pipeline | As R (if R's profile includes the AI Assistant), design a flow and look for **Create pipeline** | R may ask and draw; creating the pipeline is refused or not offered: it is an administrator's | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

```A description for QA-09.12
Design a pipeline: every night read qa/orders.csv from storage, keep the paid orders, and save them as a CSV.
```

## Ask your data, the file chat and transcription
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-09.21 | An answer shows where it came from | As A, **Analysis › Ask your data**: ask a question about a dataset you have, such as "How many orders are paid?" | The answer has a chart, the rows behind it and **The query, run as you** over the dataset; the line under it names the model and the time | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-09.22 | Not found is said as that | Ask about something the workspace does not hold, such as "What is the weather on Mars?" | It says it cannot find that in your data; it does not make an answer up | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-09.23 | A question's length | Paste a question over 500 characters | It is not accepted: 500 characters at most | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-09.24 | File chat keeps nothing | **Analysis › Files**, a PDF's **⋯** › **Chat with this file**; ask "List any dates mentioned"; **Close**; open the chat again | The answer can be checked against **View**; after **Close** the conversation is gone | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-09.25 | Transcribe a recording | **Tools › Audio Transcript** › **Upload a file**: the recording; tick **Include timestamps before each segment**; **Extract transcript** | The **Transcript** shows each segment with its time; **Copy** copies it | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Access and isolation
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-09.26 | A viewer has no AI pages | As V, go to `/ai/assistant`, `/pipelines/prompts` and `/data/ask` | Each is refused | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-09.27 | The assistant stays in its workspace | As X, ask the AI Assistant about `QA occupancy` by name | It does not find it: it names it as not in this workspace | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-09.28 | Ask your data stays in its workspace | As X, ask Ask your data a question that only A's data answers | Nothing of A's workspace is cited or counted | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

> **Warning:** Every answer in this area is a model's draft. A check passes on what the console does with the answer (it
> shows its sources, holds it, refuses, asks first), not on whether the model's words are clever.

## Example
At Summit Valley the tester asks the AI Assistant to write the day's orders into the store database. It answers that
writing rows into a database can't be done here, because the step for it is switched off, and offers to save the rows as
a file, upload them to a bucket or send them to a webhook. Asked to read a file the workspace does not have, it names
the file and draws nothing.

articles.title: Test area 10: runs, items and retries
articles.summary: Find and read runs, a run's page and outputs, failures grouped by error, retrying from the failed step, retrying failed items or many runs, comparing runs, and who sees which runs.
articles.who: Testers; the administrator (A), with R, V and X for access and isolation
articles.popular: Test a retry from the failed step
articles.md:
These checks cover what happens after a run starts: finding it, reading its page and its files, a failure on purpose,
and every way to retry: from the failed step, from the start, only the failed items, or many runs at once. A retry from
the failed step reuses the steps before it, so they are neither run nor billed again.

**Before you start:** the pipeline `QA occupancy` ([QA-07](#qa-pipelines)) and its schedule `QA daily`
([QA-08](#qa-triggers)) with a few runs. A pipeline that works **item by item** (each file or row is an item; the
Recipes chapter builds one), with an input in which one item fails. For the failure checks, change `QA occupancy`'s
first step to **Read CSV/JSON/Parquet** of a file that is not there yet, `qa/beds-today.csv`, and keep that file ready.

Tested by ______ on ______

![Runs › Failed](qa-runs-failed "Runs › Failed: error patterns, most frequent first, then the failed runs with their failing step, error and kind")

## Find and read a run
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-10.01 | Find a run | As A, **Run & review › Runs** (**Latest**): **When** Last 7 days, **Pipeline** `QA occupancy`, **Started by** **Run now** | The numbers beside each filter match the rows listed; each row shows queued, started, ended, the duration, the status and the last message | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-10.02 | Search by number | Type a run number in **Search run id or message** | Only that run is listed | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-10.03 | The run's page | Click the run number | The title names the run with its status; the strip shows **Started**, **Ended**, **Duration**, **Started by**, **Steps**, **Rows in → out** and, for A, **Cost** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-10.04 | The tab is in the address | Open **Outputs**; copy the address; open it in a new tab | The page opens on **Outputs** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-10.05 | View a file in place | **Outputs** › the CSV's **View** | It opens as a table; **⋮** offers the download **as CSV, JSON or JSONL** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-10.06 | The log | **Log**: search a word; filter by level; **Next error** | The lines narrow as you type; **Next error** jumps to an error line, when there is one | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-10.07 | Analytics | **Runs › Analytics**, range 7 days | The runs, failed, success rate and median duration; **Pipeline health** lists `QA occupancy` with its runs and success rate | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## A failure on purpose
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-10.08 | A missing file fails the first step | **Run now** on `QA daily` (reading the missing `qa/beds-today.csv`) | The run is **Failed**; its message names the step and *No object at* the file; **Steps** marks the failed step: *Fix the cause, then retry: the steps before it are not run again.* | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-10.09 | Failed runs, grouped | **Runs › Failed**, **Today** | **Error patterns** lists *No object at …* with how many runs and schedules; picking it lists only those runs; **Kind** reads **Other** or **The data** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-10.10 | The run's panel | Click the run on **Runs › Failed** | The failing step, the schedule, the attempt, the times and the full error, with **Open the run** and the retry buttons | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-10.11 | Retry from the failed step | Put `qa/beds-today.csv` in place; **Retry from the failed step** | The console says where the retry starts first; the run continues as **Attempt 2** of the same run and completes | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-10.12 | Each attempt is kept | On the run's **Steps**, pick **Attempt 1**, then **Attempt 2** | Attempt 1 shows the failure; in attempt 2 a step not run again says **Reused from attempt 1** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-10.13 | A retry refused when the pipeline changed before the failed step | Make another run fail at a later step; change a step before it and **Save**; **Retry from the failed step** | Refused, with the reason (the pipeline changed before the failed step); **Run again from the start** is the way | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-10.14 | Retry many runs at once | Make three runs fail; on **Runs › Failed** tick them; **Retry from failed step** | Before you confirm, the panel lists what will be retried and what skipped, each with its reason; each run is retried on its own | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Items
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-10.15 | The Items view | Run the item-by-item pipeline; open the run's **Items** | The summary counts **Items**, **Done** and **Failed**; the filters **All**, **Done**, **Failed** carry those counts; the failed item reads **Failed at** its step | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-10.16 | Why an item failed | **Open** on the failed item | **Steps for this item** with **Why it failed**; **Data at each step**; steps after the failure say **Not run: an earlier step failed** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-10.17 | Retry only the failed item | Fix its cause; **Retry this item** (or **Retry failed items (1)**) | Only that item runs again, from the step it failed at; the done items are untouched; the item's **Earlier versions** list *Attempt 2 · Done · current* and *Attempt 1 · Failed · earlier* | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-10.18 | Act on several items | Tick two items; **Export CSV**, then **Download zip** | The CSV holds the two rows; the zip has a folder for each item with its files | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-10.19 | Find an item across runs and compare | The schedule's **Items** tab: **Find an item** by its name; tick **Compare** on two rows | **Compare two runs** shows the item's fields side by side, what changed in the data and what changed in the pipeline between them | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Who sees which runs
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-10.20 | A reviewer sees the runs asked of them | As R, **Runs › Latest** | R sees R's own schedules' runs and the runs R is asked to review, not A's other runs | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-10.21 | A reviewer cannot retry someone else's run | As R, open a failed run of A's that R may read | No retry is offered, or it is refused: retrying is for the run's owner and the administrators | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-10.22 | A run's cost is for administrators | As R, open a run's page | **Cost** and **What this run cost** are not shown | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-10.23 | A viewer sees only Analytics | As V, open **Runs** | Only the **Analytics** tab; `/runs/latest` is refused | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-10.24 | Masked values stay masked | As a member without access to a sensitive column, open the Items of a run whose data holds one | The value shows **Masked for you** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-10.25 | Another workspace cannot open the run | As A, copy a run's address; as X, open it | **Run #N of schedule #M does not exist or was deleted.** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

![A run opened from another workspace](qa-isolation-run "Another workspace's administrator follows the link to a run: the run does not exist for them")

## Example
At Summit Valley **Wound photos too dark to measure** first failed with four items failed at the measuring step; with the
right photos in place, **Retry failed items** ran only those four again, as attempt 2, and the run completed. **Compare
two runs and retry in bulk** shows a bulk retry of three failed runs: one retried, two skipped, each with its reason.

articles.title: Test area 11: review and approval workflows
articles.summary: Everything waiting in Review, a run's review, Approval steps inside a run, individual and bulk decisions, approval workflows, requests, and who may decide.
articles.who: Testers; A builds, R and A2 decide, with V, F and X for access and isolation
articles.popular: Test an approval from start to decision
articles.md:
These checks cover every decision a person makes: a run's results waiting for review, an Approval step that pauses a
run, documents, and the requests of an approval workflow. Each decision is recorded under the name of the person who
made it, no one decides their own request, and a bulk decision is still one decision per item.

**Before you start:** the team `QA team` with R as its lead ([QA-03.23](#qa-people)), and `QA occupancy`
([QA-07](#qa-pipelines)). Leave **Administration › Data policies › Bulk review** at the workspace's usual setting and
note it.

Tested by ______ on ______

![Review › All waiting](qa-review-all "Review: approvals, runs and documents waiting together, with the kind, who it waits on and how long")

## Review, all in one place
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-11.01 | All waiting | As R, **Run & review › Review** | **All waiting** opens first, with **All**, **Approvals**, **Runs** and **Documents** and their counts; overdue first, then the longest waiting | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-11.02 | The badge matches | Compare the number beside **Review** in the menu with **All waiting** | They are the same | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-11.03 | Narrow by who it waits on | **Waits on**: **You**, then **Your teams** | Only what waits on R, then on R's teams | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-11.04 | Read one in the side panel | Click a row | What it is and what to check, with **Approve…** and **Reject…** when R may decide it there | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## A run's review
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-11.05 | Turn review on | As A, `QA occupancy` › **Settings** › **Review**: tick **Our team**; **Save**; **Run now** | The run ends **Completed · waiting for review**; the Pipelines list's **Data** column says **Reviewed** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-11.06 | Decide it | As the reviewer the review names (or A), open it from **Review**; read **What to review**; **Approve** with a note under **What you checked** | The run reads **Completed · approved**; the decision is recorded under the reviewer's name | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-11.07 | A rejection needs a reason | Run again; **Reject** with no reason, then with one, ticking **Run the schedule again** | Without a reason it cannot be sent; with one the run reads **Completed · rejected** and a new run is made | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-11.08 | A model's answer is marked DRAFT | Review a run of the AI pipeline of [QA-09.08](#qa-ai) with review on | The model's answer is marked **DRAFT**: made by a model for a person to check; not a decision | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-11.09 | A failed run has nothing to approve | Make a reviewed run fail; look for it in **Review › Runs** | It does not wait for review: only a completed run does | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-11.10 | Individual review stays out of bulk | Tick **Requires individual review**; **Save**; make two runs; in **Review**, tick both, **Approve** | Both are skipped with *The pipeline requires individual review* | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-11.11 | The workspace may forbid bulk approval of runs | As A, **Data policies** › **Bulk review**: **Allow bulk approve of runs** off; **Save review policy**; untick individual review; try a bulk approve | Each run is skipped with *Bulk approve is off in this workspace*; a bulk **Reject** still works. Put the policy back | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## An Approval step inside a run
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-11.12 | The run pauses | As A, add **Approval** after **Filter**: **Task title** `QA wards {{rows}}`, **What to check** `Check the full wards`, **Reviewers** `QA team`; **Save**; **Run now** | The run reads **Running · waiting for approval**; R has a task in **Review › Approvals** with the **Pipeline**, **Run**, **Step**, **Rows waiting** and by when to decide | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-11.13 | Approve, and the run goes on | As R, **Approve** with a note | The run continues in a moment and completes; the step shows *Approved by* R | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-11.14 | Reject, and the run fails with the reason | Run again; as R, **Reject**, a reason, **Reject** again | The run fails; its message carries *Rejected by* R and the reason | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-11.15 | Pass a task on | Run again; as R, open the task › **Pass on**, **Pass it to** A2, a note; confirm | A2 has the task; its history says it was passed by R to A2 | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Approval workflows and requests
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-11.16 | Make a workflow | As A, **Build › Approval workflows** › **New workflow**: **Name** `QA purchase`, **Key** `qa-purchase`, **What it approves** `purchase`; **Create and design** | The canvas opens with **Request starts** and **Request ends** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-11.17 | Steps and a condition | **Add a step** › **Condition**: **Field of the request** `amount`, **is more than** `1000`; yes: an **Approval** for **Everyone in a team** `QA team` with **A rejection needs a reason**; no: **Request ends** | The steps are placed; nothing is live until published | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-11.18 | Publish | **Publish version 1** with a note under **What changed** | **Versions** lists version 1 as current | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-11.19 | Start a request | As A2, **Review › Approvals** › **My requests** › **New request**: **Workflow** `QA purchase`, **Title** `QA laptop`, field `amount` = `2500`; **Start the request** | R has a task in **Review**; the request reads **Running** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-11.20 | The condition decides the way | Start another with `amount` = `200` | It goes straight to its end; **History** shows *no* for the condition | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-11.21 | Ask for changes | As R, on the first request's task, **Ask for changes** with a comment | The request shows *Changes asked*; its history carries the comment | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-11.22 | Nobody decides their own request | As R, start a `QA purchase` request with `amount` `5000`; look at it in R's **Review** | It is listed but cannot be decided by R: someone else decides it | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-11.23 | Running requests keep their version | Change the workflow and **Publish version 2**; open a request started before | It still reads version 1 | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-11.24 | Cancel a request | As A2, open a running request › **Cancel request**, confirm | Its history says *Cancelled by* A2; its open task is gone from R's **Review** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-11.25 | Make a workflow inactive | As A, **Make inactive** on `QA purchase`; as A2, **New request** | `QA purchase` is no longer offered | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Bulk, access and isolation
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-11.26 | A wide bulk decision needs the count | As R, select more than 25 items that may be decided; **Approve** | The panel asks you to **Type N to confirm** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-11.27 | A viewer and the front desk have no Review | As V and as F, go to `/review/all` | Refused | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-11.28 | Another workspace's Review | As X, **Review** | None of A's runs, tasks or requests is listed | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Example
At Summit Valley **Controlled substance count reconciliation** pauses at its Approval step for Avi Cohen, the pharmacist,
and completes once he approves; **Bank statement matching** shows a rejection: the run failed with *Rejected by Claire
Martin: Every line unmatched*. Dr. Lena Schmidt's chest X-ray reviews require individual review, so a bulk approval skips
them.

articles.title: Test area 12: Report Studio
articles.summary: Templates and publishing, creating a report and its versions, approving and signing, verifying a signature, COPY and VOID, the page limit, reports from a pipeline, and who may do what.
articles.who: Testers; A designs and generates, A2 and R approve, with V and X for access and isolation
articles.popular: Test that a report is approved and signed by someone else
articles.md:
These checks follow a report from its template to a signed PDF: publishing a template, generating a report, generating
it again, approving and signing it, checking the signature, and the guards around it. Whoever generated a version never
approves it, and nothing is overwritten: each generation is a new version.

**Before you start:** a brand profile with a logo and a signature approved in **Assets & branding** (or the workspace's
own), and a starter template. A2 or R must hold **Approve and sign reports**. Use synthetic data only.

Tested by ______ on ______

## Templates
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-12.01 | Report Studio's tabs | As A, **See results › Reports** | Six tabs: **Overview**, **Templates**, **Library**, **Data**, **Assets & branding**, **Settings** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-12.02 | Start a template from a starter | **Templates**: start a new template from a starter; name it `QA summary` | The template opens in the designer as a draft | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-12.03 | Publish it | Publish the draft | The published version reads **Published · can't change**; a later change makes a new draft, not a change to the published version | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-12.04 | Publishing can need a second person | As A, **Reports › Settings**: tick **Publishing needs a second person**; **Save**; edit `QA summary` as A, then try to publish it as A | A cannot publish a draft A edited last: it goes as a task (**Ask for approval**) to the people under **Who publishes**, in their **Review › Approvals**. Untick the setting afterwards | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Create, version and approve
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-12.05 | Create a report | **New report** from `QA summary` with its test data | The report's page shows **v1** with its PDF (and HTML if the design asks for it); **Generated by** A; **Waiting for approval** if approval is asked for | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-12.06 | Generate again keeps every version | **Generate again** with the same data | **v2** is made; **v1** is still listed; the page says *Generating again makes a new version. Nothing is overwritten.* | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-12.07 | You never approve your own | As A (who generated it), look at v2 | No approve button; the page says *You generated it; someone else approves it.* | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-12.08 | Approve and sign | As A2, open the report; **Approve and sign v2** | v2 reads **Approved** and **Signed**; the PDF carries the approver's signature | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-12.09 | Verify the signature | **Verify signature** on v2's PDF | It says the file is intact and is one of this workspace's approved reports | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-12.10 | A changed file fails the check | Open the downloaded PDF in another program, change a word, save it; **Verify signature** on that file | It does not pass as an intact approved report (not yet verified) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-12.11 | Two approvals | As A, **Settings** › tick **Two approvals**, **Save**; generate **v3**; as A2, approve; as R, approve | A2's button reads **Give the first approval of v3**; the PDF is signed only after the second approval, by someone else, naming both. Untick it afterwards | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-12.12 | Mark as COPY | **Generate again** with **Mark this version as COPY** ticked | The new version carries the **COPY** pill; every page of its files says COPY | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-12.13 | Void a version | **Void** on a version, with a reason | It carries the **VOID** pill with the reason and who voided it | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-12.14 | Share a report | **Share** | *Link copied. Only people in this workspace who may open reports can follow it.* | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-12.15 | Who can see it | The report's **Access** part, **Who can see this report** | Everyone in the workspace who may open Reports, and no one outside it; downloads are signed links that work for five minutes | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-12.16 | Downloads are recorded | Download the PDF; open the report's **Activity** | The download is listed with its time | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Limits and pipelines
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-12.17 | The page limit | As A, **Reports › Settings** › **Most pages in one report**: lower it to `2`, **Save**; create a report whose data lays out to more pages | The report is not made: the message says how many pages it lays out to and the limit, and offers the ways out (one report per row, fewer table rows, export as CSV). Put the limit back (300 by default; only the platform administrator raises it further) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-12.18 | A field missing from the data | Create a report from data that lacks a field the template uses | The message names the field: it is *not in this data*, with what to do (map it, change the binding, or mark it optional) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-12.19 | A report from a pipeline | Add **Generate report** to `QA occupancy` with **Use a saved template** `QA summary`; **Save**; **Run now** | The run's **Outputs** hold the PDF; the report is a version in **Reports › Library**, approved there like any other | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-12.20 | The checks refuse, and the run goes on | Set **When the checks refuse it** to `CONTINUE_WITH_WARNING`; give the step data that fails a check; run | The step completes with no report and a warning on the run | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-12.21 | Retention is previewed, not run | As A, **Reports › Settings** › **What retention would remove**: **Older than (days)** `365`; **Preview** | It lists the files of versions a newer one replaced and frozen data no kept version uses; nothing is removed here; each report's current version and every approved or signed version stay | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Access and isolation
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-12.22 | A reviewer approves but does not design | As R (with **Reports** and **Approve and sign reports**, without **Report templates**), open **Reports** | R can read the Library and approve; `/reports/templates` is refused | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-12.23 | Settings are the administrators' | As R, go to `/reports/settings` | Refused | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-12.24 | A viewer has no Report Studio | As V, go to `/reports/library` | Refused (unless V's profile includes Reports) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-12.25 | Another workspace cannot open the report | As A, copy the report's address; as X, open it | The report does not open for X; nothing of it is shown (not yet verified) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Example
At Summit Valley the Summit Valley admin generates Elena Marsh's discharge summary; the page tells him *You generated it;
someone else approves it.* Dr. Minh Nguyen chooses **Approve and sign**, and **Verify signature** on the PDF confirms it
is intact and one of the workspace's approved reports.

articles.title: Test area 13: dashboards and analysis
articles.summary: Reading, filtering and sharing a board, building one, Analytics Studio, Ask your data and its search, the Data Catalog, and masked values for a viewer and a researcher.
articles.who: Testers; A builds, V and RS read, with X for isolation
articles.popular: Test masking for a viewer and a researcher
articles.md:
These checks cover the results side: dashboards and their filters and links, building a board, exploring a file in
Analytics Studio, asking questions of the data, and the Data Catalog. They test **masking** on purpose: a column the
Data Catalog marks sensitive (a name, a date of birth, a record number) is masked for anyone without access, on a
board, in Analytics Studio, in exports and in Ask your data, until an administrator grants access for a time.

**Before you start:** a synthetic file in storage with a sensitive column, such as `qa/patients.csv` with `mrn`,
`name`, `dob`, `ward` and `los_days` (made-up rows only), and a board that reads it (you build one in QA-13.08). The
researcher account RS and the viewer V.

Tested by ______ on ______

## Read, filter and share
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-13.01 | Find a board | As A, **See results › Dashboards** | Cards grouped: **Favourites**, then one group per pipeline that feeds boards, then **Not fed by a pipeline**; each card with its widgets, files, who made it and when | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-13.02 | Where its data comes from | Open a board fed by a pipeline | The facts line names **Made by** the pipeline and its newest run, linked to the run's page; **Files this board reads** lists the files | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-13.03 | The date range narrows it | Pick **30 days** on the filter bar | Each widget whose data has the date column runs again and says **Filtered**; one without it says **Not by** and the filter's name | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-13.04 | Click a bar to filter | Click one bar of a chart | The whole board narrows to that value; the facts line shows **N filters on**; the × clears it | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-13.05 | The view is in the address | Copy the address with a filter on; open it in a new tab | The board opens with the same filter | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-13.06 | Share a board with a colleague | Send the address to V; V opens it | V sees the same board and filters, run as V | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-13.07 | A viewer cannot change a board | As V, look for **New dashboard** and a widget's edit menu | Neither is offered; the page says V can open, run and filter, and that changing boards needs **Edit dashboards** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Build
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-13.08 | Save an analysis | As A, **Analysis › Analytics Studio** › **Choose a file**: `qa/patients.csv`; **Canvas**: **Dimension** `ward`, **Measure** **Average** of `los_days`; **Run analysis**; **Save analysis** `QA LOS by ward` | The result shows one row per ward; the analysis is saved | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-13.09 | Make a board with it | **Dashboards** › **New dashboard** `QA board`; ⋯ › **Add a widget**: **Shows** **A saved analysis**, `QA LOS by ward`, a bar chart; **Add** | Only the new widget runs; it shows the wards | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-13.10 | A table widget of the file | Save a query `select * from dataset` in **SQL** as `QA patients`; add it as a table widget | The table pages, sorts and offers **Search the rows**, **Columns** and **Export CSV** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-13.11 | A filter bar | ⋯ › **Add a filter bar**: **Add a filter**, **Label** `Ward`, the dataset and column `ward`; **Save filters** | The bar shows **Ward**; ticking a value narrows both widgets | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-13.12 | Deleting a board keeps the saved work | Make a second board with one widget; ⋯ › **Delete this dashboard** | The board is gone; `QA LOS by ward` is still in Analytics Studio | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-13.13 | Pin an answer | **Ask your data**: "Average los_days by ward in qa/patients.csv"; **Pin to dashboard** › **An existing dashboard** `QA board`; **Pin** | **Pinned to** the board; the board shows the tile, which runs its query when the board opens | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-13.14 | No pinning without dashboard editing | As RS (no **Edit dashboards**), ask a chart question | **Pin to dashboard** is greyed out | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## The Data Catalog and masking
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-13.15 | The catalog | As A, **Analysis › Data Catalog** | The figures count **Assets**, **With sensitive fields**, **Stale over 30 days**, **Without an owner**; `qa/patients.csv` is listed | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-13.16 | Sensitive columns are found | Open `qa/patients.csv`'s panel; **Scan for sensitive data** | `mrn`, `name` and `dob` are marked as holding a medical record number, a person name and a date of birth (mark any it missed by hand under **Holds**, then **Save details**); the asset's sensitivity reads **Restricted** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-13.17 | Masked for the researcher | As RS, open the asset in the Data Catalog, then in Analytics Studio (**Data** tab) | The panel says *Its sensitive values are masked for you*; the `mrn`, `name` and `dob` values are masked; `ward` and `los_days` are not | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-13.18 | Masked on a board and in its export | As V (or RS), open `QA board`'s table widget; **Export CSV** | The sensitive columns are masked on screen and in the file | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-13.19 | Masked in Ask your data | As RS, **Ask your data**: "List the names of the patients in qa/patients.csv" | Names are not shown in the answer or its rows | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-13.20 | Ask for access | As RS, in the asset's panel: **Why you need it** `QA check`, **For** **1 day**; **Request access** | The panel says when RS asked; A has the request to decide | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-13.21 | Access granted for a time | As A, approve it in **Review**; as RS, open the asset again | The panel says *You can see its values until* the end; the values show for RS until then, and are masked again after | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Ask your data and its search
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-13.22 | What is searched | As A, **Ask your data** | The badge says what is searched (for example *Searching 3 documents, 7 pipeline results and 6 forms*) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-13.23 | An answer from documents cites them | Ask a question a document or a form answers (for example about a referral of [QA-05](#qa-documents)) | The answer has numbered citations; each source links to its document or form with the passage | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-13.24 | Each person finds only what they may open | As RS, ask the same question | RS gets no answer from documents RS's access does not open | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-13.25 | The search index (administrators) | As A, the **Search index** card on **Ask your data** (marked **Workspace admins**): **Add folder**, pick a folder; **Save**. As RS, look for the card | A is told *Search index saved* and the card counts **Documents**, **Form records**, **Files** and **Passages**; RS has no such card; answers still come only from what the asker may open. With no index on the platform the card says every question reads your sources live | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Isolation
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-13.26 | Another workspace cannot open a board | As A, copy `QA board`'s address; as X, open it | **This dashboard isn't here**: it may have been deleted, or the link belongs to another workspace | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-13.27 | Another workspace's catalog | As X, **Data Catalog**, search `patients` | A's `qa/patients.csv` is not listed | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-13.28 | Another workspace's questions | As X, **Ask your data** about `qa/patients.csv` | Nothing of A's file is found or counted | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

![The Data Catalog as a researcher](qa-catalog-masked "The Data Catalog as the researcher sees it: which assets hold sensitive fields, what those fields hold, and each asset's sensitivity")

## Example
At Summit Valley Dr. Hana Ito opens the Patient 360 file: its `name`, `dob` and `mrn` columns are masked for her. She asks
for 7 days' access *to check the ages in the diabetes cohort*; once the administrator approves it, she sees the values
for a week, then they are masked again.

articles.title: Test area 14: developers and the API
articles.summary: API clients and their scopes, the sandbox and test keys, starting a run through the API, event routes, webhooks with their signature and redelivery, embedded run views, the result as JSON, PDF, HTML or Markdown, and the Developer portal.
articles.who: Testers with a developer's tool for sending API calls (curl, Postman or similar); A sets up, with R and X for access and isolation
articles.md:
These checks cover how your own systems reach the workspace: API clients with only the scopes they need, a sandbox with
test keys that never touch real data or the bill, starting and reading runs, events, webhooks and embedded run views.
The calls themselves, with samples to copy, are in the **Developer portal**; follow its **Quickstart** for the exact
requests.

**Before you start:** a tool for sending API calls, a receiver for webhooks reachable at a public `https` address (a
test receiver of your own), and the workspace's sandbox (your account team creates it once). Keep every secret in your
tool's secret store; never paste one into a note or a screenshot.

Tested by ______ on ______

## API clients
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-14.01 | The limits that apply | As A, **Developers › API Clients** | The box above the list shows each client's most (600 calls a minute, burst 100, by default), all clients together, and this month's calls | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.02 | Make a client; the secret is shown once | **New API client**: **Name** `QA client`, **Scopes** `pipelines:read`, `runs:read`, `runs:write`; **Make client**; **Copy** both | **API client made** shows the **Client id** and **Client secret**; closing it, the secret is never shown again | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.03 | A token, and its scopes | With the tool, exchange the id and secret for a token; list the pipelines; try to send an event | The token works (it lasts 15 minutes); the list answers; the event is refused: the client has no `events:write` | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.04 | An IP allowlist refuses other addresses | **Change** the client: **IP allowlist** `10.0.0.0/8`; call again from your own address | The call is refused. Empty the allowlist again | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.05 | A new secret ends the old | ⋯ › **New secret**; call with the old secret, then the new | The old secret and its tokens stop working at once; the new one gets a token | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.06 | The client's history | ⋯ › **History** | The changes of QA-14.04 and 14.05, by A, with the time | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## The sandbox
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-14.07 | The sandbox is named | **API Clients** › **Sandbox** | The sandbox is named with a **Test** badge; keys there work only in the sandbox | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.08 | Make a test key | **New test key**: a **Name**, the same scopes; **Make test key** | Its **Client id** starts with `cl_test_`; the secret is shown once | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.09 | A test key cannot reach the real workspace | With the test key, ask for one of the real workspace's pipelines by its id | *Not found*, as another organisation's would be | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.10 | Testing in the sandbox is never billed | Start a few sample runs with the test key; open the real workspace's **Billing › Cost & usage** | The real workspace's figures have not moved; the sandbox's own Cost & usage is marked **Sandbox · never billed** (not yet verified end to end) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

![The sandbox on API Clients](qa-sandbox "The Sandbox part of API Clients: the sandbox workspace with its Test badge, and its test keys")

## Runs and events through the API
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-14.11 | Start a run | With `QA client`, start a run of `QA occupancy` (the portal's **Quickstart** shows the request) with an `Idempotency-Key` | The answer names the run; **Runs › Latest** shows it with **Started by** **API** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.12 | Send it twice, get one run | Send the same request with the same `Idempotency-Key` again | The second answer is the first run; no second run starts (not yet verified end to end) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.13 | Read it back | Read the run, its steps, its outputs and its result | Status and times (UTC), each step with its rows, the files by their ids (never a bucket or a path), and at most 100 result rows | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.14 | A record that breaks the input contract is refused | Start a pipeline that has an input contract (the pipeline list in the API names it) with a record missing a required field | Refused with each wrong field named; no run starts (not yet verified end to end) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.15 | An event route | As A, **Event routes** › **New event route**: **Event type** `qa.test.created`, **Starts** **A pipeline's run** `QA occupancy`; **Add route**; send that event with a client that has `events:write` | The answer lists what it started; a run starts | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.16 | An event without a route is refused | Send an event of type `qa.nobody.listens` | Refused; nothing starts | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.17 | Past the limit | Send more calls in a minute than the client's limit (lower it with **Calls a minute** first) | The API answers 429 with how long to wait; nothing is done or billed | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Webhooks and embedded views
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-14.18 | A private address is refused | **Webhooks** › **New webhook**: **URL** `https://192.168.1.40/hook` | Refused when saved | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.19 | Add a webhook | **URL** your receiver's `https` address, **Events** `run.completed` and `run.failed`; **Add webhook**; **Copy** the signing secret | **Webhook added** shows the **Signing secret** once | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.20 | A delivery arrives signed | Run `QA occupancy` | The receiver gets a POST with `Webhook-Signature` (`t` and `v1`) and `Webhook-Id`; an HMAC-SHA256 of the time, a dot and the body with the secret matches `v1` | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
