| QA-14.21 | Retries and the log | Stop the receiver; run again; start the receiver; ⋯ › **Deliveries** | The delivery shows **retrying** attempts, then **delivered**, with **Attempts** and the **Last answer** (not yet verified end to end) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.22 | Send again keeps the id | **Send again** on a delivery | The receiver gets it again with the same `Webhook-Id` | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.23 | A new signing secret overlaps | ⋯ › **New secret** › **Make a new secret** | For 24 hours deliveries are signed with both the new and the old secret | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.24 | Embed a run view | **Change** `QA client`: **Sites that may embed its run views** your test page's origin; ask the API for a view link of a run (`runs:read`); open it in a frame on that page | The run's status, steps and files show in the frame; the row reads **Run views embed on** that site; a page on another site cannot frame it (not yet verified end to end) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.25 | A view link expires | Ask for a link of 1 minute; wait | After it expires, the page says so and reads nothing more | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Access, revoking and isolation
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-14.26 | The Developer portal needs its page | As R (no **Developer portal** in R's profile), go to `/developers/portal`; then add it to R's profile and try again | Refused first; then R reads the portal (its **Base URL**, **Quickstart**, **API reference**) but cannot make clients | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.27 | API Clients are the administrators' | As R, go to `/developers/api-clients` | Refused | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.28 | Revoke ends everything | ⋯ › **Revoke** on `QA client`; call with it | The client and its tokens stop working for good; **Show revoked** lists it | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.29 | Another workspace's client cannot reach this one | With a client of X's workspace, ask for `QA occupancy` by its id, and for one of its runs | *Not found* for both | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Result formats
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-14.30 | The result as JSON, the default | With `QA client`, read a completed run's result with no `format` | The rows of its final output, masked, as in QA-14.13 | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.31 | A run with a report, as PDF, HTML and Markdown | Read the result of a run whose pipeline has a **Generate report** step with `format=pdf`, `format=html`, then `format=md` | A PDF (the signed one if the report was approved), the report's page, and Markdown whose first line reads **From signed report RPT-… version N** (or **(not signed)**), with its tables and lists, and its pictures and signature as links | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.32 | A run without a report | Read a `QA occupancy` run's result with `format=md`, `format=html`, then `format=pdf` | Markdown and HTML hold the result rows as a table, first line **From the result of run …**; the PDF is refused: **no report** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.33 | The format by Accept, and one that is not offered | Read a result with the header `Accept: text/markdown`; then with `format=xlsx` | Markdown; then refused (400) with the allowed formats named: json, pdf, html, md | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.34 | Run and wait in a format | Start a short pipeline with `wait=30s&format=md` | Once it ends, the answer is its Markdown, with the run's address in `Location` | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.35 | A sensitive pipeline's report stays in the console | Mark a pipeline with a report **sensitive**; run it; read its result as `pdf`, `html` and `md`, then as JSON | Each document is refused (**sensitive files**); the JSON answers with the person's details masked | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-14.36 | A webhook carries the chosen formats | **Change** the webhook of QA-14.19: under **The run's result**, tick **JSON** and **Markdown**; **Save**; run a pipeline | The list shows **run.completed carries the result as JSON, Markdown**; the receiver's `run.completed` has `data.results` with `json` and `md` (its text), and the signature matches | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Example
At Summit Valley the *Locked-down client* is allowed only from `10.0.0.0/8` and is refused from anywhere else, and
Priya Singh's test key *Summit Valley sandbox key* (`cl_test_…`) works against the sandbox's sample pipeline while the
real workspace's **Cost & usage** does not move.

articles.title: Test area 15: billing
articles.summary: Cost & usage and its lines, a run's cost, what is not billed twice, backfill estimates, invoices, credit notes, statements and receipts, and who may read them.
articles.who: Testers; as the administrator (A), with R, V and X for access and isolation
articles.md:
These checks follow the work of the earlier areas onto the bill: every run, model call, page read and file kept is
metered, priced from the workspace's rate card, and shown on **Cost & usage** as the invoice will read it. They also
check what is never billed, or not billed twice. Usage is rolled up every few minutes, so wait a little after a run
before you look for it.

**Before you start:** the runs of areas 07 to 10, including the retried run of [QA-10.11](#qa-runs). Prices come from
your account's rate card; the checks look at what is counted, not at the amounts.

Tested by ______ on ______

## Cost & usage
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-15.01 | What prices the month | As A, **Administration & billing › Billing › Cost & usage** | The chips show **Priced with** the rate card and version, the currency, **Day** so far, **Yesterday**, and **Days in** the billing time zone (America/Chicago unless set otherwise) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-15.02 | The four figures | Read the top | **Month to date** (with a forecast and last month's total), **Data deleted**, **Storage kept** and **Seats** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-15.03 | By service | **By service** | The month added up by **Storage**, **Model calls**, **Pipelines**, **Analytics & tools**, **API** and **Seats**, then allowances and **Month to date, as the invoice lists it** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-15.04 | A line and what is behind it | **Line by line**: choose **Pipeline runs** | Its **Quantity**, **Rate** and **Amount**; choosing it shows what is behind it, with the number of events and when the last was | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-15.05 | A day's lines | **Cost by day**: click today | Today's lines open | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-15.06 | Your pipeline is there | **Cost by pipeline** › **By pipeline**: `QA occupancy`; its **Runs** | **By run** lists its runs with **Started**, **Status**, **What it cost** by meter and **Cost**; **Open the run** opens the run's page | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-15.07 | AI calls are counted | **AI model calls** › **By source** | The prompt `QA summary (DRAFT)` of [QA-09](#qa-ai) is listed with its calls and tokens, tries included | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-15.08 | Export | **Export CSV** | The file holds the month's lines as listed | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-15.09 | Trends | **Billing › Analytics**, 3 months | The total, this month so far, the largest service and the costliest pipeline; **Cost by month** coloured by service | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Not billed twice
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-15.10 | A retry from the failed step | **By run**: the run retried in [QA-10.11](#qa-runs) | Only the work of the retried steps is added by attempt 2; the reused steps are not billed again | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-15.11 | Run again from the start | Choose **Run again from the start** on a failed run; look at its cost | Every step is billed again | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-15.12 | A refused API call | After [QA-14.17](#qa-developers), look at **API calls** | The calls answered 429 are not counted | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-15.13 | The console's own reads are billed | Open a dashboard; look at **Analytics queries** and **Storage reads** later | They grow: the console's reads are billed like any other read | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Estimates, invoices and documents
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-15.14 | A backfill's estimate | **Schedules & triggers**, `QA daily`'s **⋮** › **Backfill…** | The **Cost estimate** gives the total and the average run, from the schedule's billed runs of the last 30 days, or says there is nothing to estimate from | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-15.15 | Estimate against billed | **Runs › Backfills**, the backfill of [QA-08.19](#qa-triggers) | Its page shows the **Estimate** it started with and **Billed so far** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-15.16 | This month's invoice is a draft | **Billing › Invoices**, this month | **Draft**, reading *A running draft — rebuilt from the meter until it is issued*; its lines match **Cost & usage** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-15.17 | An issued invoice | Open a past month's invoice, if there is one | **Issued** (or **Paid** or **Overdue**), its rate card version, **Period** in the billing time zone, **Lines**, **Balance**, and its PDF under **Documents** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-15.18 | The billing profile | ⋯ › **Billing profile** | **Legal name**, **Address**, **Billing email**, **Tax number (VAT / GST)**, **Tax rate %**, **Currency**, **Payment terms (days)** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-15.19 | A statement | **Billing documents** › **Statement 2026** | A statement is added to the list: each invoice, payment and credit note of the year, and the **Balance open** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-15.20 | Check a receipt | **Verify a receipt** with a receipt's PDF (if the workspace has one) | It says whether the file is a receipt this platform issued, unchanged since it was signed | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Access and isolation
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-15.21 | Billing is the administrators' | As R and as V, go to `/billing/usage` and `/billing/invoices` | Refused: billing is for workspace administrators | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-15.22 | Another workspace's bill | As X, **Cost & usage** › **By pipeline** | `QA occupancy` and A's runs are not there | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

> **Note:** Figures on **Cost & usage** before a month closes are a running estimate of the invoice, not a bill. Card
> payments are made on the payment provider's own page and are not part of this test.

## Example
At Summit Valley, one run of *Journey 7 · Wound photo* bills a **Pipeline run**, the **Model tokens in** and **out** of its
prompt, an **Image described** and **Storage writes**; its line under **By run** adds them up. A run of *Denials by
month* retried from its last step adds only that step's work again.

articles.title: Test area 16: security and privacy
articles.summary: Workspaces kept apart, data policies and the model rules, masking, retention with its preview and legal holds, our team's recorded sessions, and the audit records.
articles.who: Testers; as the administrator (A) and the second workspace's administrator (X), with R and V
articles.popular: Test that another workspace cannot see or open anything
articles.md:
These checks gather the console's promises about your data. A second workspace can neither see nor open anything of
yours, whatever link it is given. Sensitive data goes only to the models your data policy allows. Retention shows what
it would remove before anything is removed. Our team works in your workspace only in a recorded session. And every
access change, sign-in and decision is recorded where the people who look after it will find it.

**Before you start:** the records made in the earlier areas (a run, a form, a document, a report, a dashboard), and the
addresses of each, copied while signed in as A. X is the administrator of another workspace.

Tested by ______ on ______

## Workspaces are kept apart
Open each address you copied as A, signed in as X. Each line is one check.

| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-16.01 | A run | As X, open A's run address | **Run #N of schedule #M does not exist or was deleted.**; nothing of the run is shown | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-16.02 | A form | As X, open A's form's **Fill in** address | **Form not found.** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-16.03 | A document | As X, open A's document review address | **This document isn't here** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-16.04 | A dashboard | As X, open A's board address | **This dashboard isn't here** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-16.05 | A pipeline | As X, open A's pipeline address | It does not open for X (not yet verified: the exact message) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-16.06 | A report | As X, open A's report address | It does not open for X (not yet verified: the exact message) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-16.07 | Searches and lists | As X, search A's pipeline, form, person and file names on X's **Pipelines**, **Forms**, **Users**, **Data Catalog** and **Ask your data** | Nothing of A's is found | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-16.08 | The bell | Make A's run fail; look at X's bell | X gets no notification of A's work | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

![A run opened from another workspace](qa-isolation-run "Signed in to another workspace, a link to this workspace's run opens nothing: the run does not exist there")

## Data policies and models
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-16.09 | The defaults | As A, **Administration › Data policies** in a workspace that has not saved its policy | **Not saved yet — these are the defaults**: **Sensitive** **Local only**, **Internal** and **Public** **Any model**; **AI write tools** **Off** for Sensitive, **On** for the others | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-16.10 | Save and undo a level | Change **Keep run files** for Internal to `2`; **Save policy**; then **Use the defaults** on that level | The saved value shows, then the default again | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-16.11 | Sensitive data stays on local models | With a hosted model connection in the workspace, try a prompt marked **Sensitive** on it | Refused: Sensitive is **Local only** (not yet verified end to end) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-16.12 | The policy can be read by members | As R (with the AI Assistant), open the assistant's **Context** tab | The data policy per level is listed, read only | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-16.13 | Members cannot change it | As R and V, go to `/administration/data-policies` | Refused | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

![Data policies](qa-data-policies "Data policies: for each level, which models may see it, how long a run keeps its files, and whether the AI Assistant may change things")

## Retention
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-16.14 | Retention starts off | **Data policies** › **Retention** in a workspace that has not set it | It is **Off**; every kind keeps its data forever | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-16.15 | Preview removes nothing | **Edit retention**: **Keep for (days)** `1` for **Notifications**; tick **Remove data older than its days**; **Preview these days**; then close without saving | **If saved, a pass now removes** shows a count for Notifications; nothing is removed: the bell's older notices are all still there | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-16.16 | Audit records keep a minimum | **Edit retention**: try **Audit records** below the platform's minimum | It is not accepted: audit records are kept at least 2,190 days | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-16.17 | A legal hold | **Place a hold** on `QA occupancy` with a reason; then **Release** it | The hold is listed while it is on; releasing ends it; both are recorded | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-16.18 | The history | **History** on Retention | Every pass with when, how it started and what it removed (or **Not run yet**) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Our team's sessions and the audit records
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-16.19 | Our team's activity | As A, **Administration › Activity** (where it appears) | **Our team's activity** lists each change and read by a staff member, with **When**, **Staff member**, **Change or read** (**Read**, **Builder**) and **Service** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-16.20 | A managed session is recorded | Ask your account team to open a managed session and open one run; then read **Activity** | Their screen carried a bar naming your workspace; the run they opened is listed as a **Read** with their name (not yet verified end to end) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-16.21 | Who changed someone's access | **Page access** › **Changes** | The grants of [QA-03](#qa-people) with who, what, for whom, until when and why | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-16.22 | Who approved something | Open an approved request of [QA-11](#qa-approvals) | Its history names who decided, when, and their comment | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-16.23 | Who downloaded a report | The report of [QA-12](#qa-reports) › **Activity** | Each download with its time | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-16.24 | A download link is short-lived | Copy a report's download link; open it after five minutes | It no longer works (not yet verified) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## What the console never does
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-16.25 | It never writes to your databases | See [QA-04.09](#qa-connections), [QA-07.23](#qa-pipelines) and [QA-09.14](#qa-ai) | All three passed: only reading queries run, Write Database cannot be added, and the AI Assistant refuses a database write | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-16.26 | Files delivered to your storage stay | After a run's own files expire, look in the bucket a run wrote to | The files the run wrote to your bucket are still there; only the run's own copies read **Expired** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Example
At Summit Valley the Meridian administrator, given a link to run #1881, sees *Run #1881 of schedule #1113 does not exist or
was deleted.*, and a link to the Nurse triage form says *Form not found.* The tester previews a one-day retention
for notifications and closes it without saving: nothing is removed.

articles.title: Test area 17: settings and alerts
articles.summary: Alert rules that open and resolve alerts, the Tool and Task Registries, configuration values and secrets, appearance and themes, and who may change settings.
articles.who: Testers; as the administrator (A), with R, V and X for access and isolation
articles.md:
These checks cover the workspace's own settings: alerts that tell people when something needs them and clear by
themselves when it is fixed, the registries that decide which tools the AI Assistant and which tasks pipelines may use,
configuration values and secrets that pipelines name instead of holding, and themes.

**Before you start:** `QA occupancy` and its schedule `QA daily` ([QA-08](#qa-triggers)), set to read the missing file
of [QA-10](#qa-runs) so a run can fail on purpose, and `QA team` ([QA-03](#qa-people)).

Tested by ______ on ______

## Alerts
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-17.01 | The recommended rules | As A, **Settings › Alerts** in a workspace with no rules: **Add the recommended rules** | Five rules are added: *A run failed*, *Failures in a burst*, *A schedule missed its slot*, *A run is slower than usual*, *A review is waiting too long*, each telling the administrators by the bell | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-17.02 | Make a rule | **New rule**: **Watch for** **Runs failed**, **Name** `QA failed`, **Failed runs** 1, **Schedule** `QA daily`, **How bad** **Warning**, **Tell them by** **The bell**, **Who hears of it** **Administrators** and **QA team**; **Save the rule** | The rule is listed with its sentence (**When**), whom it **Tells** and its **On** switch | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-17.03 | It fires | **Run now** on `QA daily` (it fails) | An alert opens under **Alerts**, open first, with what happened, since when and **What to do**; A and R (in `QA team`) get a bell notice | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-17.04 | It opens what it is about | **Open** on the alert | The failed run's page opens | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-17.05 | It clears by itself | Put the file in place; retry the run from the failed step | The run completes; the alert resolves, *cleared by itself* | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-17.06 | Resolve by hand | Make it fail again; **Resolve** on the alert | It is resolved, *by a person* | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-17.07 | Mute | Rule's ⋯ › **Mute for** an hour; make the run fail | The alert is recorded, but nobody is told; **Unmute** restores it | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-17.08 | Alerts to a webhook | Tick **Webhooks** on the rule; a webhook subscribed to `alert.opened` and `alert.resolved` ([QA-14](#qa-developers)); fail and fix the run | The receiver gets `alert.opened`, then `alert.resolved` | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Registries
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-17.09 | The Task Registry | **Settings › Task Registry** | Every task with what it does, its kind and how many **Pipelines** use it; **Write Database** listed and not available to add | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-17.10 | Switch a task off | Untick **Sort** under **In this workspace** (a task `QA occupancy` does not use); open a pipeline's **Add step from the Task Registry…** | **Sort** is no longer offered, or is marked **(disabled)** with a hint; the registry row says **Switched here** with A's name. Switch it back | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-17.11 | The Tool Registry | **Settings › Tool Registry**: filter **Writes** | Each tool with the **Permission** it needs and whether it **Asks first**; the write tools ask first | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-17.12 | Switch a tool off | Untick **Enabled** on a write tool; open the AI Assistant's **Context** tab | The tool is listed as blocked, with the reason; **Recent changes** on the registry names A. **Reset** it afterwards | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Values, appearance and the rest
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-17.13 | A secret is never shown again | **Settings › Configuration values** › **New value**: **Key** `QA_TOKEN`, **Kind** secret, a made-up value; save; open it | The value is not shown; to change it you type a new one | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-17.14 | A key's form | **New value** with **Key** `qa-token` | Refused: capital letters, digits and underscores, a letter first | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-17.15 | A plain credential in a pipeline is refused | In a step setting whose name looks like a credential (a password), type a plain value; **Save** the pipeline | The save is refused: it must hold a `${secret:…}` reference | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-17.16 | The workspace's default theme | **Administration › Appearance**: pick **Ocean**; **Save default**; sign in as V (who has not picked a theme) | V opens in **Ocean** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-17.17 | A person's own theme wins | As R, **Your profile** › **Appearance** › **Dark** | R's console turns dark and stays dark on another device (**Saved to your account**); the workspace's default does not change it. **Use the workspace default** goes back | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-17.18 | Kafka & Topics | **Settings › Kafka & Topics** | The brokers the workspace publishes through, whether they answer, and each topic's readers; with no connection of its own, it says it uses the platform's default broker | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Access and isolation
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-17.19 | Settings are the administrators' | As R and V, go to `/settings/alerts`, `/settings/values` and `/administration/appearance` | Refused | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-17.20 | The Tool Registry opens with Prompts | As a member whose profile includes **Prompts**, open `/settings/tools` | The registry opens to read | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-17.21 | Another workspace's settings | As X, **Settings › Alerts** and **Configuration values** | `QA failed` and `QA_TOKEN` are not there | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Example
At Summit Valley the rule *Census feed failed* opened an alert when the census file for 12 October had not arrived, told
the IT team by the bell and the *Ops alerts* webhook, and resolved by itself once the file landed and the run was retried.

articles.title: Test area 18: scale, times and dates
articles.summary: Times on the 24-hour clock in your own time zone, Chicago schedule times, billing days, date ranges, big files, the caps on calls and rows, and runs side by side.
articles.who: Testers; as the administrator (A), with a second device or browser set to another time zone
articles.md:
These checks run across the product. Times: the console shows every time on the 24-hour clock in your own device's
time zone, schedules are set in server time (Chicago), and billing days follow the workspace's billing time zone. Scale:
ordinary steps work through files of millions of rows, while a step that calls a model or a service row by row has a cap
it checks before the first call.

**Before you start:** a second browser (or device) whose time zone is set to another one than yours, for example
Europe/London. A large synthetic CSV, such as a file of 1,000,000 made-up orders with `order_id`, `region`, `category`,
`amount` and `status` (the Recipes chapter shows how to make one; keep it in a test bucket).

Tested by ______ on ______

## Times and dates
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-18.01 | The 24-hour clock | Look at any list of runs and at **Review**'s **Waiting since** | Times read like 14:05, never 2:05 PM; recent ones like "21 min ago" or "26 Oct, 19:27" | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-18.02 | Your own time zone | Open the same run in both browsers | Its start time differs by the zones' difference: each shows its own device's time | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-18.03 | Schedules are in Chicago time | **New schedule**, **Daily** at 06:00; read **Next runs** in both browsers | The editor and **Next runs** say the times are server time (Chicago) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-18.04 | A run's date | A run with a file named `{{date}}` ([QA-07.12](#qa-pipelines)) started just after midnight in your zone but before midnight in Chicago (or the other way) | The file carries the Chicago date | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-18.05 | Billing days | **Cost & usage** in both browsers | Both show the same **Days in** zone (America/Chicago unless set otherwise) and the same day totals | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-18.06 | Backfill days | **Backfill…**, **Dates** a range, **One run per** **Day** | The preview says the days are counted in the billing time zone, and lists each date once | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-18.07 | A custom date range | **Runs › By date** › **Custom**, and a dashboard's **Custom** **From** and **To** | Only runs, or rows, inside the range are shown; the range stays when you come back to the board | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-18.08 | A date as a run parameter | **Run with…** on a schedule with a **Date** parameter: type `2026-13-01` | Refused before the run starts: a date reads like 2026-10-01 | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-18.09 | Times through the API | Read a run through the API ([QA-14.13](#qa-developers)) | Its times are in UTC | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Big data
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-18.10 | A file of a million rows | A pipeline: **Read CSV/JSON/Parquet** of the large file, **Filter** `status` **eq** `paid`, **Aggregate** by `region` and `category` (**sum** of `amount`), **Save File**; **Run now** | The run completes; **Rows in → out** shows 1,000,000 read and one row per region and category kept | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-18.11 | The table viewer stops at 500 | **Outputs** › **View** on a step output of more than 500 rows | It draws 500 rows and says the rest are in the download | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-18.12 | Analytics Studio reads it in place | **Analytics Studio**, open the large file | Its rows, columns and size show; a page of rows opens quickly; nothing is copied | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-18.13 | A result at the row ceiling says so | **SQL**: `select * from dataset`; **Run** | The result says when it stopped at the server's row ceiling; a download of it says it holds only that part | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-18.14 | A model is never sent a million rows | Put an **AI prompt** step straight after the read, **At most rows** at its default | The step fails before any call: the input has more rows than its **At most rows** (50 by default, 500 at most) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-18.15 | Calls at once are capped | Set an AI or **Call API** step's **Calls at once** to `9` | Not accepted: at most 8 | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-18.16 | A size failure has its own kind | After a run fails for size, open **Runs › Failed** | Its **Kind** reads *Too large for memory or a limit* | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Many at once
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-18.17 | One run of a schedule at a time | **Run now** on a schedule twice while the first run works ([QA-08.08](#qa-triggers)) | The second is refused, or recorded as **Skipped**; never two runs of one schedule at once | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-18.18 | Different schedules run together | **Run selected** on three different schedules | All three run at the same time | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-18.19 | Workflow requests run side by side | Start two requests of a workflow whose step runs the same pipeline | Each request gets its own run, side by side (not yet verified end to end) | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-18.20 | Bulk decisions stop at 100 | **Review**, **Select all matching** with more than 100 items | At most 100 go into one decision | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-18.21 | Bulk retry stops at 100 | **Runs › Failed**, select more than 100 failed runs (if you have them) | At most 100 are retried in one go | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-18.22 | A zip of items stops at 200 | A run with more than 200 items: select all, **Download zip** | At most 200 items in one zip | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Example
At Summit Valley **1M orders: streaming totals** reads 1,000,000 orders, keeps 965,517 that pass, and saves 30
region-and-category rows and 198,414 customers. The daily appointment file has about 110,000 rows, but only tomorrow's
240 appointments are sent on, one call each.

articles.title: Test area 19: patient intake
articles.summary: The New patient intake form (sections, show-when rules, required answers, checkboxes, tables, signature), its review workflow with a nurse and a senior nurse, the signed summary, scanned forms, the dashboard, roles and isolation.
articles.who: Testers; the front desk (F) fills in, the reviewer (R) is the nurse, the administrator (A) is the senior nurse and builds, with V and X for access and isolation
articles.popular: Test the patient intake
articles.md:
These checks follow one new patient's intake the whole way: typed in at the front desk (or scanned on paper), checked,
summarised by AI as a DRAFT, approved by a nurse (and by a senior nurse when the priority is high), kept as a signed
**Patient intake summary**, and counted on the dashboard. They also test the form features the intake uses: sections,
answers that appear only when they apply, a **Checkboxes** field and its limits.

**Before you start:** the intake built as in [the recipe](#rcp-patient-intake); the accounts F (profile *Front desk*:
Forms and My requests only), R (in the nurses' team), A (an administrator, the senior nurse), V and X
([Prepare the test accounts](#qa-guide)). The sample files
[intake-answers-sample.json](/help/samples/patient-intake/intake-answers-sample.json) (Ingrid Castellanos, an adult),
[intake-child-sample.json](/help/samples/patient-intake/intake-child-sample.json) (Theo Brannigan, 7),
[intake-pregnancy-sample.json](/help/samples/patient-intake/intake-pregnancy-sample.json),
[intake-scanned-form-sample.pdf](/help/samples/patient-intake/intake-scanned-form-sample.pdf) and
[intake-test-cases.csv](/help/samples/patient-intake/intake-test-cases.csv) (the priority each case should get).
Synthetic patients only.

> **Note:** Not yet verified end to end. These checks were written while Riverside Health's intake was being built; run
> them once on a complete build and correct any expected result that differs.

Tested by ______ on ______

## The form
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-19.01 | Sections in order | As F, **Forms** › **New patient intake** | The fields stand under headings: Patient, Parent or guardian (patients under 18), Emergency contact, Insurance, This visit, Medical history, Social history, Medicines, allergies and vaccines, Review of systems, Care team, Consents and signature (Women's health only when Sex is Female); each heading once | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Checkboxes limits (a test form)
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-19.14 | At least and At most | As A, **New form** `QA checkboxes`; add **Checkboxes (tick all that apply)** with options `Fever`, `Rash`, `Cough`; **At least** `1`, **At most** `2`; **Preview** | The field says **Tick 1 to 2** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

| QA-19.19 | Sections in the builder | Give two fields **Section** `Part A`, the third `Part B`; choose the second field's **Section** box | The box suggests `Part A`; the canvas shows each heading once; moving a Part B field between the two Part A fields shows Part A twice | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-19.20 | My requests | As F, **Review › My requests** after QA-19.13 | A request **Patient intake · intake review**, running; its **History** shows it was requested by F and a run was started | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

| QA-19.23 | The AI adds nothing | Compare the summary and flags with the answers | Every medicine and allergy the summary names is in the intake; none is invented; no diagnosis | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

| QA-19.25 | The senior's decision | As A approve it | The request is approved; **Reports › Library** gets **Patient intake · S-<number>** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-19.26 | Not high: one approval | Send a low-priority case (P01 Lena Halvorsen); as R approve | No senior step; the report is made after R alone | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-19.27 | A rejection needs a reason | Send another intake; as R choose **Reject** with no reason, then with "Wrong patient" | Refused without a reason; with it, the request ends rejected | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

| QA-19.29 | The kept decision | Open Ingrid's request **History**; open her PDF | The history shows what was kept of R's decision; the PDF's *Nurse's review* and the line under the summary name R and the time, with R's note | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-19.30 | Masking in the PDF | Read the PDF's patient and insurance parts | The phone, the emergency and guardian phones and both member IDs show only their last 4 characters | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-19.31 | The PDF's parts | Page through it | Each part is whole on a page; the DRAFT line *Drafted with AI … (a DRAFT, not a diagnosis)*; allergies as red chips; symptoms ticked only; *Missing information to ask*; a QR code | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-19.32 | Approve and sign, Verify | As R (who did not generate it) choose **Approve and sign**; then **Verify signature**; scan the QR code | The version reads **Signed**; the signature holds; the QR code opens the report's verification | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-19.33 | A bad phone goes on, flagged | Send an intake with phone `555-01` | The intake is not stopped; its summary lists the phone under *Checks that failed* | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-19.34 | A child's summary | Send the child sample (Theo Brannigan, 7) and approve | Flags include a child and the severe peanut allergy; the PDF shows the guardian; no Women's health part | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## The dashboard
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-19.35 | Counts | As A open **Dashboards** › **Riverside — Patient intake** | **Intakes reviewed** counts the approved intakes (not the rejected one); **Each reviewed intake** lists them, newest first | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-19.36 | The mix and the rates | Read **Triage priority mix**, **High priority (%)**, **Missing-information rate (%)**, **Flags by type** | They match the intakes sent: Ingrid high, with an anticoagulant flag; the child counted under Child | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-19.37 | Upload a scan | As A, **Documents › Intake** › **Upload** › **Upload documents** with intake-scanned-form-sample.pdf | It arrives and is read; in **Documents in** it is typed **Patient intake · New patient intake form** with its tables | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-19.38 | The wrong type, then extract again | Its menu (⋯) › **Extract again**, **Document type** **Patient intake form** (the starter); then again with **Patient intake · New patient intake form** | The starter reads fewer fields and no medicine table; the right type reads every section again | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-19.39 | Approve the scan | As R, **Review › Documents**: check and approve it | A run of **Patient intake · from documents** starts and waits at the nurse's approval, *Patient intake: 1 scanned intake(s) to review* | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-19.40 | The scan's summary | Approve that run's approval in **Review › Approvals** | A report **Patient intake · D-<number>**; the dashboard's **Where the intakes came from** shows a scanned form | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

![Two intake types](intake-qa-two-types "Documents › Document types: the starter Patient intake form and Patient intake · New patient intake form, which starts Patient intake · from documents")

## Roles and isolation
| # | Check | Steps | Expected | Pass / Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-19.41 | Front desk: the form only | As F look at the menu; open `/forms/submissions`, `/runs/latest`, `/reports/library` by address | The menu offers **Forms** and **Review**, where only **My requests** opens; each address says it is not open to them | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-19.42 | Front desk builds nothing | As F, **Forms** | No **New form**, no edit or row menu on **New patient intake** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-19.43 | The nurse does not fill forms | As R (a profile without Forms) open `/forms/builder` | Not open to R; R still decides in **Review** | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-19.44 | Viewer sees nothing | As V open the form, Submissions, the runs of *Patient intake · assess*, Documents and the Library | Each is refused or empty of intakes | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |
| QA-19.45 | Another workspace | As X open the form's fill address, the workflow, the template, the document type and a report's address copied from Riverside | Each is not found or refused; nothing of Riverside's shows | ☐ Pass ☐ Fail |

## Example
At Riverside Health the front desk sends Ingrid Castellanos's intake; the reviewer, as the nurse, approves it with a note,
and the administrator approves it again as the senior nurse because the DRAFT priority is high. The signed summary names
the reviewer under *Nurse's review*, masks her phone, and verifies. A second intake rejected for a wrong phone makes no
summary, and the Meridian administrator cannot open any of it.

articles.title: A referral arrives by email
articles.summary: Elena Marsh's referral letter is mailed to the workspace, read into fields and approved by a person.
articles.who: Anyone whose page access includes Documents; the review is a document reviewer's
articles.md:
This tour follows one patient through the ETL Console, from the first letter to the last chart. The hospital is
**Summit Valley Health System**, a regional hospital group; the patient is **Elena Marsh**, 67, record number
SV-000117, admitted with type 2 diabetes, an infected wound on her left foot and heart failure.

> **Note:** Summit Valley, Elena Marsh and every person, number and result in this tour are fictional. The data is
> synthetic, made for the demonstration. Nothing here is clinical advice, and every model answer you see is a DRAFT for
> a person to check.

## What happened
A community clinic, Northside Clinic, mails a referral for Elena to Summit Valley. It is sent to the workspace's own
**Email-in** address, so nobody has to download and upload it. The message carries two PDF attachments: the two-page
letter, and its second page as a scan.

1. Each attachment becomes a document. **Documents › Intake › Email-in** lists both under **What arrived**, from
   "Referral: Elena Marsh (SV-000117)", with the outcome **Taken**.
2. Document Intelligence reads the letter against the **Referral** document type: the patient, the reason for the
   referral, its urgency and the other fields the type asks for.
3. The letter lacked two values the type requires, the referral date and who it was referred to. Values a document is
   missing or unsure of send it to **Review › Documents**.
4. Greta Fischer, from health information, opens the document, fills in the two values and approves it. On
   **Documents › Documents in** the referral now reads **Approved**, 13 fields.

![Documents in, with Elena Marsh's referral approved](tour-referral "Documents › Documents in: the referral from Northside Clinic, read as a Referral and approved (fictional patient, synthetic data)")

## Where to see it
- **Documents › Intake**, tab **Email-in**: the workspace's address and everything that arrived by mail. The same file
  mailed again is kept once.
- **Documents › Documents in**: each document, its type, how many fields were read, how sure the reading was, and its
  state.
- **Review › Documents**: the documents waiting for a person, oldest first.

## Good to know
- Email-in takes up to 20 attachments a message, 20 MB each. Anyone who knows the address can send to it, so an
  administrator can give the workspace a new address with **New address** to shut out the old one.
- An approved document's values land in **Documents › Approved data**, where pipelines can read them.

## Learn more
The Documents topic says more: [Upload documents and mail them in](#doc-intake), [Document types](#doc-types) and [Review a document](#doc-review).
Next in the tour: [the journey starts](#tour-journey-starts).

articles.title: The journey starts
articles.summary: The approved referral feeds a pipeline, and an event opens the Patient journey approval workflow.
articles.who: Building workflows is a workspace administrator's; anyone whose page access includes Approval workflows may read them
articles.md:
Once the referral is approved, the console takes over the paperwork. One pipeline turns the referral into an admission,
and an approval workflow, **Patient journey**, carries Elena from registration to the signed discharge packet. (A
fictional patient and synthetic data, as everywhere in this tour.)

## What happened
1. The approval itself starts the pipeline **Journey 1 · Referral to admission**: its run page says **Started by A
   trigger**. The run reads the approved referral, checks it against the workspace's data contract for referrals
   (marking any problem, never dropping the row), works out Elena's age and the urgency, and keeps the referral as a
   file in the journey's folder.
2. Its last step calls the workspace's own API once to send an event, **admission.accepted**. The first try of that
   step failed on a setting; once it was corrected the run was retried from step 6, and its page shows **Attempt 2**,
   the five earlier steps "Reused from attempt 1".
3. An event route sends that event to the **Patient journey** workflow, which opens a request for Elena:
   "Event admission.accepted", with her name, record number, age, reason and urgency as the request's details.

![The Patient journey workflow on its map](tour-workflow "Build › Approval workflows: the Patient journey workflow, 16 steps, its first step selected")

## The workflow's map
**Build › Approval workflows** draws a workflow as a map, from **Request starts** to the end. Patient journey has 16
steps of five kinds:

| Kind | In Patient journey |
|---|---|
| Run pipeline | Registration, Care-plan draft (AI), Medication safety check, Discharge summary draft (AI), Discharge packet |
| Condition | Registered? and High risk in the care plan? |
| Task | Self-pay counselling, Nurse triage (fill the Nurse triage form), Ready for discharge? |
| Approval | Attending physician approves the care plan, Senior physician approves, Physician approves the discharge |
| Notify and record | Tell the ward, Journey stages (kept as a dataset), Tell the requester |

Select a step to read its settings on the right. The first, **Run pipeline**, names the schedule to run, passes the
request's record number as the pipeline's parameter (`{{subject.mrn}}`), ticks **Wait until the run ends, its
approvals included**, and keeps the answer as `registration`, so the next condition can read `registration.eligible`.

> **Note:** Publishing a workflow makes a new version. A request already running keeps the version it started on:
> Elena's request ran on version 3 while version 5 was published later.

## Where to see it
- **Build › Approval workflows**: the workflow, its **Steps**, its **Versions** and a **Test run**.
- **Run & review › Review › Approvals**, tab **My requests**: the request, its details and its **History**, one line
  per step, newest last.

## Learn more
See [Design an approval workflow](#apr-workflows), [Events and event routes](#dev-events) and
[Start a pipeline when a document is approved](#trg-document). Next:
[registration](#tour-registration).

articles.title: Registration
articles.summary: The workflow runs the registration pipeline, which checks insurance and fetches the patient record from two connected APIs.
articles.who: Anyone whose page access includes Runs or Schedules & triggers

where.label: Get data in › Connections › API collections

articles.md:
The first step of the Patient journey workflow is a **Run pipeline** step: it starts the pipeline **Journey 4 ·
Registration: eligibility then patient record** for Elena's record number, and waits for it to finish. (Fictional
patient, synthetic data.)

## What happened
1. The workflow starts the run with one parameter, `mrn = SV-000117`.
2. The run asks a payer's eligibility service whether Elena's cover is active. It is a sandbox that stands in for a
   real payer, set up as an **API collection** under **Connections**.
3. It joins the answer to the workspace's payer roster. Because the sandbox only echoes what it is sent, the roster,
   not the sandbox, decides whether she is eligible.
4. It fetches her demographic record from a public FHIR test server, a second API collection, and writes one patient
   record to the journey's folder, which the later pipelines read.
5. The run answers `eligible: yes`. The workflow kept the answer as `registration`, so its next step, the condition
   **Registered?**, takes the "yes" branch, straight on to triage. The self-pay counselling task is skipped.

The run had 14 steps and took 1 min 20 sec.

![The registration run's Items tab](tour-registration "The registration run, tab Items: one item, Elena's referral, Done at every step")

## Items: one per patient
A run that works item by item (each patient, each file, each document) has an **Items** tab. Here there is one item,
`referral-SV-000117.pdf`, **Done**. When the same pipeline runs for the ten patients of the cohort, each patient is an
item of their own: if one fails, **Retry failed items** runs only that one again, from the step it failed at.

## Where to see it
- The request's **History** (Review › Approvals › My requests) says "registration: started run #2051" with a link.
- **Run & review › Runs › Latest** lists the run; its page has the tabs **Steps**, **Map**, **Items**, **Outputs** and
  **Log**, and a link to **What this run cost**.

## Learn more
See [Make an API collection](#con-api-collections), [How an API signs in](#con-api-auth), [A run's page](#run-page) and
[The Items view](#run-items). Next: [triage](#tour-triage).

articles.title: Triage
articles.summary: A task asks the ward's nurses to fill the triage form; the form starts a pipeline that flags abnormal vitals.
articles.who: Nurses fill the form from their task; anyone whose page access includes Forms › Submissions reads the answers
articles.md:
Registered, Elena reaches the ward. The workflow's next step is a **task**: "Nurse triage (fill the Nurse triage
form)", for the team **Ward 4B nursing**. (Fictional patient, synthetic data.)

## What happened
1. The task appears in **Review › Approvals** for every member of Ward 4B nursing, under **My teams**, with a due time
   four hours away.
2. Rosa Alvarez, the charge nurse, fills the **Nurse triage** form with Elena's vital signs and marks the task done;
   the request's history reads
   "Nurse triage (fill the Nurse triage form): done by Rosa Alvarez".
3. Submitting the form starts the pipeline **Journey 5 · Nurse triage and abnormal vitals**. Its run page says
   **Started by A trigger**: the form submitted.
4. The run turns the vitals into numbers (a value that is not a number becomes empty rather than failing the run),
   checks each against its range, works out an early-warning score in code, and keeps one triage file per patient.
5. It keeps only the abnormal readings and sends a notice, "Abnormal vitals", for them. Elena's readings were
   abnormal, so the notice went out.

![The triage run's steps](tour-triage "Journey 5: the triage submission read, checked against its ranges, scored and the abnormal readings sent on")

> **Tip:** A check like this marks the rows that break a rule instead of stopping the run, so one odd reading never
> loses the rest. A contract set to fail stops the run instead; see
> [A row that does not hold to its contract](#ts-documents--a-row-that-does-not-hold-to-its-contract).

## Where to see it
- **Review › Approvals**: the triage task, its due time, **Mark done** and **Pass on**.
- **Forms › Submissions**: each form's answers, who sent them and when, and whether they started the form's pipeline.
- **Run & review › Runs**: the triage run and its seven steps.

## Learn more
See [Build a form](#form-build), [What a submission starts](#form-starts) and
[Who decides: people, roles, teams and managers](#apr-who-decides). Next: [diagnostics](#tour-diagnostics).

articles.title: Diagnostics
articles.summary: Lab results arrive from the partner lab, the wound photo is measured and described as a DRAFT, and the chest X-ray waits for the radiologist.
articles.who: Reviewers decide runs in Review › Runs and Approval steps in Review › Approvals; the team each pipeline names
articles.md:
Three kinds of result reach Elena's file while she is on the ward, each through its own pipeline, and each is checked by
a person before anything relies on it. (Fictional patient and people, synthetic data; the X-ray is a public research
image assigned to the fictional patient.)

## Lab results from the partner lab
1. The partner lab, Northgate Labs, sends each result to the console's API as an event, one per test: HbA1c, CRP, white
   cells, potassium, creatinine and glucose.
2. Each event starts a run of **Journey 6 · Lab results from the partner lab**. The run checks the result against the
   lab result data contract, flags abnormal and critical values in code, keeps the result in the journey's folder and,
   for a critical value, notifies the physicians. Elena's HbA1c was critical.
3. The pipeline holds its results for review. Dr. Anika Patel approves each run ("Lab result reviewed."); its status
   reads **Completed · approved**.

## The wound photo
1. Daniel Kim, a ward nurse, drops three photos of the wound, each with a centimetre ruler beside it, through
   **Documents › Intake › File drop**. Each file starts a run of **Journey 7 · Wound photo: measure, describe,
   wound-care review**.
2. The run measures the wound against the ruler **in code**, not by the model. A vision model only writes a
   description, labelled DRAFT.
3. The run compares the visit with the last one, works out how much the area changed, and stops at an **Approval**
   step: "Wound care approves the measurement".
4. Sam Harper, the wound specialist, approves it ("Measurement checked against the photo."). The run goes on and makes
   one wound report per photo, a PDF in **Reports › Library**.

![The wound photo run](tour-wound "Journey 7: measured in code, described as a DRAFT, approved by wound care, one report per photo")

## The chest X-ray
1. The X-ray dropped in the same way starts **Journey 8 · Chest X-ray triage with radiologist review**. A vision model
   writes a DRAFT triage.
2. The pipeline is set so each run is reviewed one by one, never in bulk. Dr. Lena Schmidt, the radiologist, reads it
   and approves: "Lung fields reviewed; DRAFT label noted."

![The X-ray run with its review](tour-xray "Journey 8: the DRAFT triage and the radiologist's approval in the Review card")

> **Warning:** A model's answer is a draft for a person to check, never a decision. The tour's pipelines say DRAFT in
> the step's name and in what they keep, and a person approves every one.

## Where to see it
- **Review › All waiting**: everything waiting for a person, with one count on the menu; **Runs** for runs held for
  review, **Approvals** for Approval steps.
- The run's own page: its **Review** card shows who decided, when and their comment; **AI answers** shows what the
  model said.

## Learn more
See [AI and media steps](#step-ai), [Which models may see which data](#ai-data-levels),
[Review a run's results](#apr-run-review) and [Approval steps inside a run](#apr-approval-steps). Next: [the care plan](#tour-care-plan).

articles.title: The care plan
articles.summary: The AI drafts the plan, a colleague approves it while Dr. Patel is away, a senior doctor approves because the risk is High, and the pharmacist checks the medicines.
articles.who: The approvers each step names: a person, a team, or a role
articles.md:
With registration, triage, labs and imaging in, the workflow asks for a care plan. This is where the approval workflow
earns its keep: who decides depends on what the plan says, and on who is in. (Fictional patient and clinicians,
synthetic data.)

## What happened
1. **Care-plan draft (AI)**: the workflow runs **Journey 9 · Care-plan draft** for Elena. It gathers the outputs of the
   earlier pipelines and asks the workspace's model for a care plan, labelled DRAFT. The answer includes a risk level,
   and it came back **High**. The run's **AI answers** tab shows the call: the prompt "Care plan (DRAFT)", how long it
   took and how many tokens it used.
2. **Attending physician approves the care plan**: the task waits for Dr. Anika Patel. She is away, and Dr. Minh Nguyen
   stands in for her, so the task shows in his list as **Standing in for Dr. Anika Patel**. He approves; the history
   reads "approved by Dr. Minh Nguyen (for Dr. Anika Patel)".
3. **High risk in the care plan?**: a condition reads the plan's risk. Because it is High, the workflow takes the
   "yes" branch.
4. **Senior physician approves**: the team Senior physicians is asked; Dr. Chidi Okafor approves. With a Low risk this
   step would not have been asked at all.
5. **Medication safety check**: the workflow runs **Journey 10**, which lists Elena's medicines, looks up their
   ingredients, joins them to a synthetic interaction reference (for demonstration only, not clinical advice) and to her
   allergies, and holds the 25 flagged pairs at an Approval step. Avi Cohen, the pharmacist, approves them.
6. **Tell the ward**: the Ward 4B nursing team is notified.

![The request's history](tour-care-plan "Review › Approvals › My requests: the Patient journey request, the care plan's risk, and who approved for whom")

## Where to see it
- **Review › Approvals**: the approver's tasks, with **Approve**, **Reject**, **Ask for changes** and **Pass on**.
  Rejecting may need a comment saying why; the step says so.
- The request in **My requests**: its details, including the care plan's risk, and its **History**.

> **Note:** No one may approve their own request: someone else always decides it.

## Learn more
See [Design an approval workflow](#apr-workflows), [Who decides](#apr-who-decides), [Out of office](#adm-out-of-office)
and [AI in pipelines](#ai-steps). Next: [every day on the ward](#tour-ward).

articles.title: Every day on the ward
articles.summary: A schedule reads each day's vitals, a backfill catches up the days already past, and a reading that crosses its threshold raises a notice and a webhook.
articles.who: Schedules are a workspace administrator's to make; anyone whose page access includes Runs follows them
articles.md:
Not everything in a patient's stay waits for a request. Some work is the same every morning, and a schedule does it.
(Fictional patient, synthetic data.)

## What is set up
**Journey 11 · Daily progress and threshold alerts** has a schedule, **Daily at 07:00**. Each morning its run:

1. Reads only the vitals files written since the schedule's last completed run, so a file is never counted twice.
2. Adds them to the progress kept so far, sorts by patient and time, and keeps one reading per patient and time.
3. Works out each reading's change from the day before and whether it crossed its threshold.
4. Keeps only the crossed readings and, when there are any, sends a notice to the ward's nurses and the rows to the
   bedside alert system by a signed webhook.

## Catching up with a backfill
Elena had been on the ward for some days before the schedule was switched on. A **backfill** runs the schedule once for
each day of a past range, so the progress file holds the whole stay. **Run & review › Runs ›
Backfills** shows each backfill's days and how each went; a day that failed is retried from the backfill, not from the
run.

![Journey 11's runs](tour-ward "The daily schedule's runs and the backfill of the admission days")

## Where to see it
- **Build › Pipelines › Schedules & triggers**: the schedule, when it runs next, and **Backfill...**.
- The schedule's runs, one a day, and their **Items**.
- The bell: the notice for a crossed threshold.

## Learn more
See [Run a pipeline on a timetable](#trg-schedules), [Backfills](#trg-backfills) and [Webhooks](#dev-webhooks). Next:
[discharge](#tour-discharge).

articles.title: Discharge
articles.summary: The AI drafts the discharge summary, a physician approves it, and a pipeline makes the signed PDF with its QR code and books the follow-up.
articles.who: Physicians approve; anyone whose page access includes Reports › Library reads the report
articles.md:
When Elena is well enough to go home, the last part of the workflow puts her discharge on paper, approved, signed and
sent on. (Fictional patient and clinicians, synthetic data.)

## What happened
1. **Ready for discharge?**: a task for the Physicians team. Dr. Minh Nguyen marks it done.
2. **Discharge summary draft (AI)**: the workflow runs **Journey 12 · Discharge summary draft**, which reads the earlier
   journey runs and the care plan and asks the model for a summary, labelled DRAFT.
3. **Physician approves the discharge**: the Physicians team is asked; Dr. Nguyen approves.
4. **Discharge packet**: the workflow runs **Journey 13 · Discharge packet: signed PDF, QR verify, follow-up**. Its run:
   - makes the discharge summary from the published template **Discharge summary**, with the workspace's brand,
     a signature and stamp, and a QR code for checking the copy;
   - books the follow-up appointment with a scheduling sandbox and works out its date;
   - sends the follow-up to the patient portal by a signed webhook;
   - and notifies the team that the packet is ready.
5. The report waits for approval in **Review › Approvals**. Approving it signs the PDF: the report's page in **Reports ›
   Library** reads **Signed**, "Approved and signed: Dr. Minh Nguyen".
6. **Journey stages** keeps the request's milestones as a dataset, and **Tell the requester** ends the request,
   **Approved**.

![The discharge summary in the Library](tour-discharge "Reports › Library: the discharge summary, version 1, approved and signed, with its PDF and HTML")

## Check the signed copy
On the report's page choose **Verify signature**. It checks a version's PDF, or a file someone sent you, against the
workspace's approved reports: whether it is intact and whether it is one of ours. The QR code on the PDF leads to the
same check.

> **Warning:** A signature proves who approved which file and that it has not changed since. It does not prove the
> content is right: that is what the person approving reads it for.

## Where to see it
- **Reports › Library**: every report and its versions; the report's page has **Versions**, **Activity** and
  **Access**, the PDF and HTML, and where the version came from (template, pipeline run, generation job, approval).
- The run's **Outputs** tab: the PDF the run kept, with **View** and **Download**.

## Learn more
The Report Studio topic explains templates, brand profiles, approval, signing and verifying a copy; start with
[Report Studio at a glance](#rs-overview). Next:
[the health chart](#tour-health-chart).

articles.title: The health chart
articles.summary: One report brings every stage of the stay together: timeline, vitals, labs, imaging, medicines, care plan and discharge.
articles.who: Anyone whose page access includes Reports › Library reads it; running the pipeline needs Run now on its schedule
articles.md:
Each pipeline in the journey kept its own part of the story. The health chart puts them back together in one report, so
a clinician reading Elena's stay does not have to open fifteen runs. (Fictional patient, synthetic data.)

## How it is made
1. The pipeline **Journey 14 · The patient's health chart (Patient 360)** runs on demand, with three parameters: the
   record number (`mrn`), and the first and last day of the period (`from`, `to`).
2. It reads the runs of the journey's pipelines and the files they kept in the journey's folder (progress, labs,
   imaging), keeps only the rows for that patient, and labels each row with the stage it came from.
3. Its last step generates a report from the published template **Patient health chart**, "Every stage of one
   patient's journey in one chart": a timeline of the stages, a chart of the vital signs, the lab results as a table,
   the wound photos and X-ray with their measurements, the medicines, the care plan and the discharge.
4. The report is a new version in **Reports › Library**, like any other, and can be sent for approval and signed.

![The health chart in the Library](tour-health-chart "Reports › Library: Elena Marsh's health chart, made from the Patient health chart template")

## Limits that apply
- Every page counts toward the workspace's page limit for one report (300 unless an administrator set fewer). A long
  stay with many readings can reach it; the message then says what to do.
- Pictures are read from the bucket by their key. A missing picture prints as a placeholder and the run says so with a
  warning; see [A missing picture or field](#ts-documents--a-missing-picture-or-field).

## Where to see it
- **Reports › Templates**: the template, its versions, its test samples and **Data it needs**, the fields a report
  must have.
- **Reports › Library**: the chart, its versions and its PDF.

## Learn more
The Report Studio topic explains templates, repeating sections, charts and pictures from your data; start with
[Report Studio at a glance](#rs-overview). Next:
[the dashboard](#tour-dashboard).

articles.title: The dashboard
articles.summary: The Patient journey board shows length of stay, readmission risk, vital signs and time per stage for the patients on the journey.
articles.who: Anyone whose page access includes Dashboards; changing a board needs Edit dashboards
articles.md:
The **Patient journey** board is made for a cohort: Elena and nine more fictional patients whose admissions take the
same journey, the nine started by the hospital's own system through the console's API. It shows them all together. (Fictional patients, synthetic data.)

## What feeds it
**Journey 15 · Cohort stages for the dashboard** runs every hour. It reads the runs of the journey's pipelines, turns
them into one row per patient with the time each stage ended, works out the hours to each stage and the length of stay,
adds the readmission risk from the care plans, and writes two files the board reads.

## What the board shows
The board, "The flagship: length of stay, readmission risk, vitals and time per stage (synthetic patients)", has six
tiles:

| Tile | What it answers |
|---|---|
| Patients on the journey | How many patients are on it |
| Average length of stay (days) | How long a stay lasts |
| Readmission risk (care plans) | How the care plans rate the risk |
| Hours to each stage | Where the time goes, stage by stage |
| SpO2 by day (all patients) | The oxygen saturation trend |
| Each patient's stages | A table of every patient's stages, to search and export |

![The Patient journey board](tour-dashboard "See results › Dashboards: the Patient journey board for the ten-patient cohort")

## Read it
1. Open **See results › Dashboards** and choose **Patient journey**.
2. **Files this board reads** lists where its tiles' data comes from.
3. Each tile re-runs when the board opens; **Run every widget** runs them all again.
4. A tile's own menu offers what that tile can do, such as exporting a table tile's rows.

> **Tip:** A tile that reads a file that is not there yet says "Nothing to read at ... The connection worked, so check
> the path." It usually means the pipeline that writes the file has not run yet.

## The end of the tour
From a letter in a mailbox to a board on a screen, every step was a pipeline, a person's decision or both, and each one
can be opened, checked and run again. Start building your own from [What the ETL Console does](#gs-what).

## Learn more
See [Read a dashboard](#dash-boards), [Build and edit a dashboard](#dash-build) and
[Where a board's data comes from](#dash-data-sources).

articles.title: Run now and Run with…
articles.summary: Start a schedule's run at once, give one run its own parameters or AI models, and run several schedules together.
articles.who: Anyone whose page access includes Schedules & triggers; in a workspace our team manages you can still run schedules
articles.md:
Every run belongs to a **schedule**: a pipeline plus when it runs. **Run now** starts a schedule's run at once,
whatever its timetable says. **Run with…** does the same and lets you give that one run its own parameter values, or
the AI model each AI step uses, without changing the schedule.

## Run a schedule now

1. Open **Build › Pipelines › Schedules & triggers**.
2. Find the schedule: search by id, schedule or pipeline, or filter by type and run status.
3. Open its **⋮** menu and choose **Run now**. The run is queued and the row's **Run status** follows it.

![The Schedules & triggers list](trg-list "Schedules & triggers: live run counts, then each schedule with its pipeline, mode, timetable, next or last run and state")

Or, on a pipeline's own page, choose **Run now** at the top. If the pipeline has unsaved changes the button reads
**Save & run now** and saves them first; if several schedules run it, it asks which; if none does, it gives the pipeline
an on-demand schedule (it runs only when started) and runs it.

> **Note:** **Run now** is not offered for an inactive schedule ("Activate this schedule to run it") or while the
> schedule already has a run queued or running.

## Give one run its own values: Run with…

**Run with…** is in the **⋮** menu when the pipeline declares run parameters. When its only choice is a model, it reads
**Run with a different AI model…**.

1. Open the schedule's **⋮** menu and choose **Run with…**.
2. Under **Parameters**, each parameter shows its default and the placeholder steps read it by (`{{param.from}}`).
   Change the values for this run. Dates are picked from a calendar; a choice from its list.
3. Under **AI models**, choose the model each AI step runs on, if you want another one for this run.
4. Choose **Run**.

The values are for this run only: the schedule keeps its own settings, and the next scheduled run is not changed. A value
is checked before the run starts (a date as 2026-10-01, a number, one of the choices); a blank value takes the default.

![Run with… on a schedule with two date parameters](trg-run-with "Run with…: this run's From and To dates; the schedule keeps its own")

## Run several schedules at once

1. Tick the schedules in the list (the box in the header ticks every schedule on the page).
2. Choose **Run selected** in the bar that appears, and confirm.

A schedule already queued or running cannot be ticked.

## Example

Greta Fischer, Summit Valley's health information lead, needs the consent forms signed in September. She opens the schedule **Consent forms by date
range**, chooses **Run with…**, sets **From** to 1 Sep 2026 and **To** to 30 Sep 2026, and presses **Run**. The run
counts the consent forms per procedure for September only; the schedule's defaults (October to December) are unchanged.

## Limits

| What | Limit |
|---|---|
| Run now while the schedule has a run queued or running | Not offered (files and documents that arrive meanwhile wait their turn) |
| A text value | 500 characters on one line |
| Who | Anyone whose page access includes Schedules & triggers; a member sees and runs their own schedules |

articles.title: Run a pipeline on a timetable
articles.summary: Every few minutes, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly or by a cron line; the start time; pausing, skipping and the emails.
articles.who: Anyone whose page access includes Schedules & triggers; in a workspace our team manages, schedules are read-only to you

where.label: Build › Pipelines › Schedules & triggers › New schedule

articles.popular: Run a pipeline every morning
articles.md:
A **schedule** runs one pipeline: on a timetable, only when started, and also when a file arrives or a document is
approved. The editor reads as three questions: **What runs**, **When it runs** and **Email me when**. Beside it, **What
you will get** says the schedule in a sentence and lists its next runs.

![A daily schedule in the editor](trg-schedule "A schedule: what runs, when it runs, who is emailed, and the next runs worked out")

## Make a schedule

1. Open **Build › Pipelines › Schedules & triggers** and choose **New schedule** (or **Schedule** on a pipeline's page).
2. Under **What runs**, give a **Schedule name** and choose the **Pipeline**. **Open the pipeline** goes to it.
3. Under **When it runs**, choose **On a timetable** (by itself) or **Only when started** (from **Run now**, or when a
   workflow starts it).
4. For a timetable, choose **How often** and fill in the sentence (see below). Optionally set **Ends**: it still runs on
   that day.
5. Under **Also starts when**, tick **A file arrives** or **A document is approved** if it should also start on those
   (see [When a file arrives](#trg-file) and [When a document is approved](#trg-document)).
6. Under **Email me when**, tick **A run completes**, **A run fails** and/or **A run is skipped**.
7. Leave the switch at the foot on **Active: runs as soon as it is saved**, or turn it off to save it without runs.
8. Choose **Create schedule** (or **Save changes**).

Check **Next runs** on the right before you save: it is worked out by the scheduler itself.

## How often: the frequencies

| How often | The sentence | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Minutes** | Every N minutes from a time, starting a day | Every 15 minutes from 00:00 |
| **Hourly** | Every N hours from a time, starting a day | Every 1 hour from 00:05 |
| **Daily** | Every N days at a time, starting a day | Every 1 day at 06:00 |
| **Weekly** | Every N weeks at a time, **On these days** | Every 1 week at 06:00 on Mon |
| **Monthly** | Every N months on a day (or the start date's day) at a time | Every 1 month on day 2 at 05:00 |
| **Advanced (cron)** | A cron line, with an optional **Not before** day | `30 8 * * 1-5` |

Times use the 24-hour clock.

> **Note:** Schedule times are server time (Chicago), as the editor and **Next runs** say. A workspace in another time
> zone sets the Chicago time that matches its own.

## Use a cron line

Choose **Advanced (cron)** and type the **Cron expression**: minute, hour, day of month, month and day of week, in
server time (Chicago). The examples under the box fill it in.

```A cron line: 08:30 on weekdays
30 8 * * 1-5
```

```A cron line: every 15 minutes
*/15 * * * *
```

![The cron settings of a schedule](trg-cron "Advanced (cron): the expression, its examples, Ends and Not before")

## Pause, skip or stop a schedule

From the schedule's **⋮** menu on the list:

- **Deactivate** stops it running. Slots that pass while it is off are recorded as **Missed**, not replayed when you
  turn it back on with **Activate**.
- **Skip next run** asks first, naming the run, then skips that one run (recorded as **Skipped**); later runs stay on
  schedule.
- **Email notifications** changes who is emailed.
- **Duplicate** copies the schedule; **Delete** removes it (its run history is kept).

Switching a schedule to **Only when started** keeps its timetable, paused: switching back resumes it.

## Retries and priority

Open **Advanced** in the editor:

- **Priority**: 1 to 9, 1 is highest.
- **Attempts**: 1 to 10; 1 means no retry. With more, **Retry after** (1 to 3,600 seconds) doubles each attempt, up to
  an hour.

## Example

Summit Valley's **Bed occupancy by ward** runs **On a timetable**, **Daily**, every 1 day at 06:00, so the bed board
is ready when the morning shift starts. Its **ADT feed** runs **Hourly** from 00:05, and **Patient statements** runs **Monthly** on
day 2.

## Limits

| What | Limit |
|---|---|
| Priority | 1 to 9 |
| Attempts | 1 to 10 |
| Retry after | 1 to 3,600 seconds, doubling |
| Next runs shown | The next five |

articles.title: Start a pipeline when a file arrives
articles.summary: The workspace inbox and File drop, which files start which schedule, one pipeline for both a timetable and the inbox, and reading only new files.
articles.who: Anyone whose page access includes Schedules & triggers sets the trigger; File drop needs it in your page access, and its settings an administrator

where.label: Get data in › Documents › Intake › File drop

articles.popular: Start a pipeline when a file arrives
articles.md:
Each workspace has an **inbox**: a place where arriving files are checked, stored in the workspace's bucket, and handed
to every schedule set to start when a matching file arrives. People put files in it from **File drop**; a form's
submissions land there too.

## Put files in the inbox

1. Open **Get data in › Documents › Intake** and its **File drop** section (more in [File drop](#doc-file-drop)).
2. Drop files on **Drop files here** (several at once are sent one by one), or pick them.
3. Each file shows **Uploaded** or **Refused**, with the reason. **What the file drop accepts** lists the file types.

The **Settings** card shows the storage connection the files go to, **Where files land**
(`intake/<date>/<arrival>-<file name>`) and the **Size limit**.

> **Note:** Executables and scripts are refused whatever they are named, and a file's contents must match its
> extension. A refused file is not stored. Files are not scanned for viruses.

## Make a schedule start when a file arrives

1. Open the schedule in **Build › Pipelines › Schedules & triggers** (or make a new one).
2. Under **Also starts when**, tick **A file arrives**.
3. **Which files**: a pattern for the file's name: `*` matches any run of characters, `?` one. Blank for every file.
   For example `call-*.m4a` or `invoices_*.pdf`.
4. **Files per run**: 1 makes each file its own run. More: files that waited for a run go together, up to this many,
   and the pipeline reads them all.
5. Save. **What you will get** says "Also when a file arrives in the inbox matching …".

A file that lands while a run is going waits its turn; files waiting are taken in the order they arrived.

![A schedule that runs hourly and also when a recording arrives](trg-file "One schedule, two ways in: every hour, and whenever a call-*.m4a file arrives")

## Read the file the run was started for

The pipeline's first step decides what it reads:

- **Read CSV/JSON/Parquet** with **Bucket** and **File** left empty reads the run's own file.
- **Read S3** with **The run's own files first** on reads the files the run was started for; any other run reads its
  **Prefix**. The file steps (**Transcribe audio**, **Convert file**, **Split pages**) then work through them.
- Steps can name the file with `{{input_key}}`, `{{input_name}}`, and for a batch `{{input_count}}` and
  `{{input_keys}}`.

## One pipeline for a timetable and the inbox

Give the schedule both a timetable (**On a timetable**, **Hourly**, say) and **A file arrives**, and set the pipeline's
**Read S3** step to:

1. **The run's own files first**: on, so an arrival's run reads just that file.
2. **Which objects**: `last_run`, so a timetable run reads only the objects written since the schedule's last completed
   run, oldest first. A failed run moves nothing on, so its files come again next time.

Files that arrive are handled at once; the hourly run sweeps up anything that came another way.

## Example

Summit Valley's home-health team records care calls. **Care-call insight, one report per call** runs **Hourly** and
also when a file named like `call-*.m4a` arrives. Its **Read S3** step reads `home/calls/` with **The run's own files
first** on and **Which objects** `last_run`; each call is transcribed, summarised as a DRAFT and made into its own
report for the nurse, Tamara Brooks, to check.

## Limits

| What | Limit |
|---|---|
| Which files | A file's name, not a folder; at most 255 characters |
| Files per run | 1 to 50 |
| File size | The size limit shown on File drop |

articles.title: Start a pipeline when a form is submitted
articles.summary: Let each submission of a form start a schedule's run, and read the answers in the pipeline.
articles.who: Anyone who may build forms sets it; anyone the form is shared with can submit it
articles.md:
A form can start a pipeline. Each submission is kept, written to the workspace inbox as JSON, and the schedule you choose
runs with it, so a nurse's triage form can be scored, checked and filed the moment it is sent.

## Link a form to a schedule

1. Make the schedule first: a schedule of the pipeline that should handle the answers, usually **Only when started**
   (see [Run a pipeline on a timetable](#trg-schedules--make-a-schedule)).
2. Open **Get data in › Forms**, and open the form.
3. Open its **Settings** tab.
4. In **When submitted, start**, choose the schedule. **Nothing: keep the submission** starts nothing.
5. Check the form's **Status** is **Active**: only an Active form takes submissions.
6. Save the form.

The Forms list shows what each form starts in its **Starts** column.

![The Forms list with what each form starts](trg-form "Forms: the Starts column names the pipeline each form's submissions start")

> **Tip:** A form can also start an approval workflow (its **Approval** setting). It may start both: the workflow for the
> people who decide, the pipeline for the data.

## Read the answers in the pipeline

The submission arrives as the run's own file. A **Read CSV/JSON/Parquet** step with **Bucket** and **File** left empty
reads it as one row, a column per answer. Later steps use the answers by their names, such as `{{mrn}}`.

## Example

Rosa Alvarez, the charge nurse on Ward 4B, fills in the **Nurse triage** form. It starts **Journey 5 · Nurse triage and
abnormal vitals**: the vitals are turned into numbers, checked against their ranges, scored, and an abnormal reading
sends a warning to the charge nurse.

## Limits

| What | Limit |
|---|---|
| Schedules one form starts | One |
| Submissions a form takes | Only while it is Active |

articles.title: Start a pipeline when a document is approved
